DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL Policy 2.001 1 | P a g e Title: State Agency Nutrition Services Plan Category: Nutrition Services Plan and Evaluation CFR Reference 7 CFR § 246.11(c) Policy Number 2.001 Effective Date 8/15/23 Revised Date 8/15/23

POLICY STATEMENT The State Agency must develop, implement, evaluate, and promote a Nutrition Services Plan in alignment with the FNS WIC Nutrition Service Standards #1. The State Agency must promote its Nutrition Services Plan and integrate relevant components of the Plan into public health nutrition and other agency programs and must make the plan (or appropriate summary documents) available to WIC, Maternal and Child Health Bureau, and food assistance partners. PROCEDURE 1. The State Agency must plan ongoing activities with the Local Agency and additional stakeholders that ensure alignment with the Nutrition Services Plan and report on the progress of established goals and objectives annually. The Local Agency must establish their Nutrition Services Plan (the Local Agency Workplan & Narrative, 10.001B) according to DC WIC policy 2.002 Local Agency Nutrition Services Plan. 2. The State Nutrition Services Plan will align with goals and objectives outlined in the annual State Plan in accordance with DC WIC policy 12.011 Annual State Plan. 3. As part of the DC WIC State Plan, the Nutrition Services Plan shall be made public and promoted in accordance with DC WIC policy 12.011 Annual State Plan. 4. The State Agency will ensure completion of the evaluation component of the Nutrition Services Plan prior to August 15th of each year as part of the State Plan process. DEFINITIONS Nutrition Services Plan: Nutrition Services include the full range of activities performed by a variety of staff to operate a WIC Program. The Nutrition Services Plan outlines the State and Local Agency plans to deliver quality nutrition services based on the needs of its population and participants and provide staff training in accordance with federal regulations. The plan includes the nutrition services section of the state plan, as well as the State Agency efforts to incorporate the FNS WIC Nutrition Services Standards. (USDA FNS Nutrition Services Standards, Standard #1) REFERENCES 7 CFR § 246.4 7 CFR § 246.11(c) 7 CFR § 246.11(d)(2) FNS WIC Nutrition Services Standard #1 DC WIC policies 2.002 Local Agency Nutrition Services Plan, 12.011 Annual State Plan

body:
DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.003 1 | P a g e Title: Nutrition and Breastfeeding Assessment Category: Nutrition Assessment CFR Reference: 246.7 Policy Number: 2.003 Effective Date: 1/1/2016 Revised Date: 8/15/23

POLICY STATEMENT All participants deemed geographically, financially, and categorically eligible in accordance with DC WIC policies 8.004 Categorical Eligibility, 8.005 Residency Eligibility, and 8.006 Income Eligibility will have a nutrition assessment completed by a CPA/CPPA. The nutrition assessment is necessary to identify the fourth WIC-eligibility criteria of nutritional risk. All pregnant and postpartum participants must have a breastfeeding assessment completed as part of the nutrition assessment. The nutrition assessment must be completed at the participant’s initial certification and mid- certification appointments. PROCEDURE 1. The nutrition assessment is conducted via the VENA approach and assesses nutritional risk based on the following categories: • Anthropometric • Biochemical • Clinical • Dietary • Environmental Nutritional risk may be assigned manually by the CPA/CPPA and/or automatically assigned in the MIS based on responses of required fields within the participant’s record. 2. The CPA / CPPA must conduct a breastfeeding assessment for all pregnant and postpartum participants. The breastfeeding assessment can include the participant’s thoughts, feelings, goals, and support towards breastfeeding. The CPA/ CPPA must document this portion of the assessment in the participant’s care plan in the MIS. 3. At minimum, nutritional risk must be assessed and documented in the MIS at the time of certification and mid-certification for all WIC participants. The CPA/ CPPA shall document the nutrition education provided from the nutrition assessment in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.006 Nutrition Education Documentation. 4. All high-risk participants must be referred to a CPA in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.008 Serving High Risk Participants. DEFINITIONS CPA *– Competent Professional Authority; a licensed nutritionist, registered dietitian (RD), or other staff approved by the State Agency to provide nutrition services to “high” and “low” risk DC WIC participants. CPPA *– Competent Paraprofessional Authority; staff approved by the State Agency to provide nutrition services to “low risk” DC WIC participants.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.003 2 | P a g e MIS – management information system; an information and data collection system that allows the State and Local Agency to perform and manage WIC services. The MIS used in DC WIC is called the Health and Nutrition Delivery System (HANDS). VENA – Value Enhanced Nutrition Assessment; a standardized process for conducting the nutrition assessment in a WIC setting leading to improved tailoring and delivering of nutrition services. VENA sets participant-centered standards for the nutrition assessment that determines eligibility, enabling local agency nutritionists to personalize WIC nutrition education, provide more relevant referrals, and tailor food packages to the individual participant’s needs. *See DC WIC policies 4.002 Position Descriptions and 8.007 Nutrition Risk Identification for further detail on the roles and responsibilities of CPA and CPPA REFERENCES 7 CFR § 246.7(e) FNS WIC Nutrition Service Standard # 6 FNS WIC Value Enhanced Nutrition Assessment Guidance (VENA) DC WIC policies 2.008 Serving High Risk Participants, 4.002 Position Descriptions, 8.004 Categorical Eligibility, 8.005 Residency Eligibility, 8.006 Income Eligibility, 8.007 Nutrition Risk Identification

body:
DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.004 1 | P a g e Title: Determining Nutritional Risk Category: Nutrition Assessment CFR Reference: 246.7e Policy Number: 2.004 Effective Date: 8/15/16 Revised Date: 8/15/23

POLICY STATEMENT WIC staff will perform anthropometric and biochemical screening at the time of certification, as required in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.010 Anthros and Bios. This information will be assessed along with clinical, dietary, and environmental responses collected during the nutrition assessment to determine appropriate nutritional risk code(s) for each participant. PROCEDURE 1. For all allowed nutrition risk criteria outlined in DC WIC Nutritional Risk Manual, the documented risk condition must apply to an applicant's current or most recent nutrition risk condition, as opposed to any history of the condition, unless otherwise stated in the specific definition of the nutrition risk criterion. 2. The CPA/CPPA will follow the steps in DC WIC’s Anthropometric and Lab Manuals to collect anthropometric and biochemical data on WIC participants. This data will be documented in the MIS. 3. A risk code may not be assigned based on a self-diagnosis (i.e., without a medical diagnosis), however it is appropriate for WIC staff to provide referral services to participants who report having symptoms so that a medical provider can confirm or rule out the presence of a medical condition. a. Self-reported medical diagnosis should be documented appropriately. b. A self-reported medical diagnosis should prompt the CPA/CPPA to validate the presence of the condition by asking more probing questions related to the self-reported professional diagnosis, such as: • Whether the condition is being managed by a medical professional. • The name and contact information for that medical professional (to allow communication and verification if necessary). • Whether it is being controlled by diet, medication, or other therapy; and • What types of medications, if any have been prescribed, are being taken to address the condition. 4. Non-traditional health care providers such as shamans, medicine men or women, acupuncturists, chiropractors, or holistic health advisors are not considered to be physicians whose diagnoses can be accepted for purposes of this policy or for establishing the eligibility of an applicant for WIC Program benefits. 5. The CPA/CPPA must utilize VENA techniques to further probe and tailor the nutrition assessment to be participant-centered. The CPA/ CPPA may utilize attachment 2.004A VENA_ABCDE Guide to assist in collecting nutritional risk data and selecting appropriate nutritional risk codes. REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.7e WIC Policy Memorandum 2011-5

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.005 1 | P a g e Title: Nutrition Education Overview Category: Nutrition and Breastfeeding Education CFR Reference: 246.11 Policy Number: 2.005 Effective Date: 1/1/16 Revised Date: 8/15/23

POLICY STATEMENT: Nutrition education, including breastfeeding promotion and support, must be made available to all WIC participants and their Authorized Representatives. The nutrition education provided will meet the health, cultural, and language needs of the participant and be consistent with the current science and recommendations of recognized national health organizations such as the American Academy of Pediatrics, the Center for Disease Control and Prevention, and the Dietary Guidelines for Americans. PROCEDURE 1. The Local Agency must establish protocols for conducting nutrition education contacts based on caseload and participant needs. a. At minimum, two nutrition education contacts must be attempted and documented per six-month certification period and four nutrition education contacts per one-year certification period. b. The Local Agency must utilize different delivery methods for hosting and conducting nutrition education in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.007 Nutrition Education Choice. 2. The State Agency must ensure all staff participate in activities to stay current in nutritional sciences and recommendations in accordance with DC WIC policy 4.004 Staff Training. 3. Nutrition education should be participant-centered and emphasize the relationship between nutrition, physical activity, and health outcomes. 4. Nutrition education is provided in either a primary or secondary manner: a. Primary nutrition education - education provided at the initial certification, high-risk follow- up, mid-certification, /or subsequent certification appointments. The education is tailored specifically to each participant based on their nutritional risk factors and focuses on the individual’s capacities, strengths, and developmental needs. The CPA/CPPA will document this form of nutrition education contact in the TGIF format: • Thoughts – a summary of the participant or authorized representative’s chief health concern. • Goals – an agreed upon action the participant or authorized representative plans to achieve. The CPA/CPPA should try to establish SMART goals with the participant when possible. • Information – the CPA/CPPA can expand in greater detail any pertinent information relevant to the nutrition assessment and education that occurred. This is the section for the CPA / CPPA to include breastfeeding assessment information. • Follow-Up- list of specific referrals made or areas to discuss at the participant’s next appointment. b. Secondary nutrition education – this manner of education is reserved for low-risk participants and is offered only after a primary nutrition education contact has been made. The content of this type of nutrition education is more generalized and can be reserved for a broader audience of WIC participants. Topics selected must be relevant to participant category and take into consideration individual risk factors or those common to the

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.005 2 | P a g e population served in the Local Agency, as appropriate. See DC WIC policy 2.007 Nutrition Education Choice for further details. 5. The Local Agency must consider the health, cultural, and language needs of participants when procuring nutritional education materials (e.g., handouts, recipes cards, etc.). a. The Local Agency may procure from approved vendors listed in attachment 2.005A Nutrition Education Resource List. b. The Local Agency must obtain approval from the State Agency for any nutrition education materials created in-house. REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.11 WIC Policy Memo # 2008-4 FNS WIC Nutrition Service Standard 7 DC WIC policies 2.007 Nutrition Education Choice, 4.004 Staff Training ATTACHMENTS & FORMS DC WIC policy 2.004A VENA and ABCDE Guide DC WIC policy 2.005A Nutrition Education Resource List

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.006 1 | P a g e Title: Nutrition Education Documentation Category: Nutrition and Breastfeeding Education CFR Reference: 7 CFR 246.11(e)(4) Policy Number: 2.006 Effective Date: 1/1/2016 Revised Date: 8/15/23

POLICY STATEMENT Nutrition education, including breastfeeding promotion and support, must be thoroughly integrated into participant health care plans, the delivery of supplemental foods, and other Program operations. All nutrition education contacts, or attempts to contact, must be documented in the MIS and in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.005 Nutrition Education Overview. PROCEDURE 1. Primary nutrition education contacts must be documented in the TGIF format (see DC WIC policy 2.005 Nutrition Education Overview). 2. Required education topics include the following for the initial primary nutrition education contact of a participant’s certification: a. Drug use, tobacco, and alcohol screening and appropriate education given in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.020 Substance Use Screening & Referrals. b. All pregnant participants will be encouraged to breastfeeding, unless contraindicated for health reasons. 3. Exit counseling must be provided to all pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding women prior to the end of their certification period. 4. All primary nutrition education contacts must be documented in the MIS on the same day the contact occurred. 5. The Local Agency must establish protocols for documenting secondary nutrition education in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.007 Nutrition Education Choice. 6. The Local Agency must establish protocols for documenting all attempts to conduct nutrition education in accordance with DC WIC policies 2.005 Nutrition Education Overview and 2.007 Nutrition Education Choice. 7. All notes should be: a. Consistent – establishes standards/protocols to which all staff must adhere. b. Clear – easily understood by other staff members; using documentation abbreviations, etc., as established by the State and/or Local Agency. c. Organized – follows an established order and minimizes duplication. d. Complete – creates a picture of the participant, describes or lists the services provided over time, and outlines a plan for future services. e. Concise – contains minimal extraneous information. f. Include timeframe and documentation of completing care plan. REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.11(e)(4) WIC Policy Memo 2008-4 WIC Policy Memo 1994-9 FNS WIC Nutrition Service Standard #7

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.007 1 | P a g e Title: Nutrition Education Choice Category: Nutrition and Breastfeeding Education CFR Reference: 246.11 Policy Number: 2.007 Effective Date: 8/15/23 Revised Date: 8/15/23

POLICY STATEMENT Nutrition education, including breastfeeding promotion and support, must be available to all participants through either individual or group sessions appropriate to the individual participant’s nutritional risks, needs, and interests. Contacts must be designed to meet the cultural and language needs of Program participants. The Local Agency must offer at least two delivery methods of secondary nutrition education in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.005 Nutrition Education Overview. PROCEDURE The Local Agency must establish delivery methods for participants eligible for secondary nutrition education. Delivery methods may be in-person, by phone, or online. Criteria for delivery methods are outlined in the table below. Delivery method of nutrition education Risk level Participant category Individual: in-person High risk (by CPA) Low risk All categories Individual: phone High risk (by CPA) Low risk All categories Individual: telehealth/video call High risk (by CPA) Low risk All categories Individual: self-paced online or in-person Low risk All child categories All pregnant and postpartum categories Infants between 6-12 months Group: online or in- person Low risk All categories

Individual In-person: The participant or authorized representative must come to the WIC clinic to receive this delivery method. Telephone: WIC staff engage the participant and maintain confidentiality. WIC staff should offer to send reinforcements (e.g., handouts, website links, etc.) to the participant in their preferred format (electronic, text message, mail). Telehealth/video call: WIC staff engage the participant and maintain confidentiality. The Local Agency must ensure a quiet space to conduct the telehealth/video call. WIC staff should offer to send reinforcements (e.g., handouts, website links, etc.) to the participant in their preferred format (electronic, text message, mail).

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.007 2 | P a g e Self-paced online nutrition education platform: Online, self-paced, and interactive nutrition education modules/lessons are an appropriate format for participants to complete secondary nutrition education. The Local Agency should ensure procedures for reviewing module completion and contacting participants for benefit issuance. Allowable online platforms are specified by the State Agency. Group In-person: The participant or authorized representative must come to the WIC clinic to receive this delivery method. The Local Agency must ensure a private and large enough space to host a group education session. Online: WIC staff engage the participant and maintain confidentiality. WIC staff should offer to send reinforcements to the participant in their preferred format. The Local Agency must ensure a quiet and private space to conduct the group education session. The Local Agency should ensure procedures that allow for timely documentation and benefit issuance to all attendees. Missed Nutrition Education Appointments and Non-Denial of WIC Benefits The Local Agency must make a reasonable effort to provide nutrition education to each participant. The Local Agency must set guidelines for what constitutes a reasonable effort. Participants cannot be denied program benefits for failure to attend an educational activity or for lack of willingness, readiness, or ability to participate in the activity. If a participant does not attend or participate in a scheduled nutrition education contact, the Local Agency must ensure staff document all attempts to contact in the MIS. REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.11 FNS WIC Nutrition Service Standard # 7, # 14 DC WIC policy 2.005 Nutrition Education Overview ATTACHMENTS & FORMS DC WIC State Agency-provided hand-outs

body:
DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.008 1 | P a g e Title: Serving High-Risk Participants Category: Nutrition and Breastfeeding Education CFR Reference: 246.11 Policy Number: 2.008 Effective Date: 1/1/2016 Revised Date: 8/15/23

POLICY STATEMENT The State Agency must establish procedures to ensure adequate documentation and timely follow-up for participants designated high-risk. PROCEDURE 1. The State Agency establishes criteria for identifying participants with certain nutritional risk factors that require monitoring and follow-up by a CPA, see DC WIC policy 2.003 Nutrition and Breastfeeding Assessment. These risks are flagged in the MIS and are listed on DC WIC’s CPA Cheat Sheet.

2. At minimum, participants identified as high-risk must receive two individual nutrition education contacts by a CPA within three months of the initial identification of the high-risk condition. CPAs shall document the nutrition education contact in TGIF format, see DC WIC policy 2.005 Nutrition Education Overview.

3. The CPA may use their professional judgment to determine the frequency of monitoring and follow-up for each participant with a high-risk nutritional status.

4. In lieu of a CPA, a CPPA may complete a high-risk certification, but cannot provide education for risk codes that are deemed high-risk. The CPPA can counsel the participant on basic nutrition education and risk codes that are non-high risk. A high-risk participant may receive up to two months of food benefits between the certification and high-risk visit per the Local Agency discretion.

5. If a CPA determines through a subsequent nutrition assessment that a participant is no longer high-risk, the CPA may remove the high-risk designation in the MIS. The CPA must document the rational for removing the high-risk status. DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.009 1 | P a g e Title: Breastfeeding Education and Support Overview Category: Nutrition and Breastfeeding Education CFR Reference: 7 CFR § 246.11(e)(1) 7 CFR § 246.2 Policy Number: 2.009 Effective Date: 1/1/2016 Revised Date: 8/15/2023

POLICY STATEMENT Breastfeeding education, promotion, and support must be thoroughly integrated into the State and Local Agency operations and made available to all pregnant and breastfeeding participants. All pregnant participants must be encouraged to breastfeed unless contraindicated for health reasons. PROCEDURE 1. The State Agency and Local Agency ensure that all staff receiving initial and ongoing training in breastfeeding promotion and support in accordance with DC WIC policy 4.004 Staff Training. 2. Breastfeeding promotion and support activities must be outlined in the State and Local Agency’s Nutrition Services Plans in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.001 State Agency Nutrition Services Plan and 2.002 Local Agency Nutrition Services Plan. The Local Agency may provide breastfeeding promotion and support in one or more of the following ways: • Implement WIC’s Breastfeeding Peer Counseling Program in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.011 Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Program. • Provide online breastfeeding education via recorded (asynchronous) classes, articles, videos, or other modules. • Provide live breastfeeding classes or support groups, virtually or in-person. • Provide live app-based consultation for breastfeeding support. • Enter into an agreement with an organization to provide CLC, IBCLC, or other advanced breastfeeding support to WIC participants. • Any other breastfeeding promotion and support delivery method approved by the State Agency. 3. The Local Agency monitors that all staff provide breastfeeding education, promotion and support to participants appropriate to their job roles and responsibilities in accordance with DC WIC policy 4.002 Position Descriptions. a. The Local Agency provides initial breastfeeding education and support training as part of new employee orientation. b. The Local Agency establishes procedures for yielding/referring participants to the proper supporting authority when breastfeeding concerns fall out of scope of practice for staff members. c. For participants in which breastfeeding is not possible or contraindicated, the CPA must document this information in the participant’s care plan note in this MIS.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.009 2 | P a g e 4. The State and Local Agency ensure staff provide accurate and up-to-date breastfeeding messages from reputable sources including Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine (ABM), the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), and the Centers for Disease Control (CDC). REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.11(e)(1) 7 CFR 246.2 FNS WIC Nutrition Services Standard # 8 FNS WIC Breastfeeding Policy and Guidance DC WIC policies 2.001 State Agency Nutrition Services Plan, 2.002 Local Agency Nutrition Services Plan, 2.013 Breastfeeding Aids and Supplies, 4.002 Position Descriptions, 4.004 Staff Training

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.010 1 | P a g e Title: Breastfeeding Promotion in WIC Clinics Category: Nutrition and Breastfeeding Education CFR Reference: 7 CFR § 246.11(c)(7) Policy Number: 2.010 Effective Date: 1/1/2016 Revised Date: 8/15/2023

POLICY STATEMENT The State Agency ensures that the Local Agency adheres to the following: 1. Maintain a positive clinic environment which endorses breastfeeding as the preferred method of infant feeding. 2. Designate an appropriate staff member to coordinate breastfeeding promotion and support activities in accordance with DC WIC policy 4.002 Position Descriptions. 3. Ensure that women have access to breastfeeding promotion and support activities during the prenatal and postpartum periods. PROCEDURE 1. The Local Agency must, at minimum, ensure a positive clinic environment for breastfeeding by: a. Posting breastfeeding promotion, information, and resources in plain view of all participants. b. Welcoming participants to breastfeed anywhere in the WIC clinic, as they feel comfortable, and providing a private space to breastfeed or express milk. c. Refrain from using or posting any products, supplies, or promotional materials branded with infant formula company information, products, or logos. 2. The Local Agency must designate a breastfeeding coordinator to assist in the implementation and adherence of the Local Agency Nutrition Services Plan breastfeeding activities, and to assist with employee training in breastfeeding education and support. 3. The Local Agency ensures adequate staffing and/or procedures to provide breastfeeding education, promotion, and support activities to all pregnant and postpartum participants at each of its clinic sites.

REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.11(c)(7) FNS WIC Nutrition Service Standard #8 FNS WIC Breastfeeding Policy and Guidance DC WIC Policy 4.002 Position Descriptions

Policy 2.011 1 | P a g e Title: Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Program Category: Breastfeeding Peer Counseling CFR Reference: n/a Policy Number: 2.011 Effective Date: 1/1/2016 Revised Date: 8/15/23

POLICY STATEMENT The Breastfeeding Peer Counselor (BFPC) program must be made available to participants and adhere to the standards set by the State Agency. PROCEDURE The Local Agency must ensure the following: 1. All BFPCs complete the required training in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.009 Breastfeeding Education and Support Overview and 4.004 Staff Training. Additional training and support should be offered to BFPCs as needed. 2. The BFPC works under the direction of the Local Agency Breastfeeding Coordinator, Designated Breastfeeding Expert (DBE), Lactation Consultant, or the designated CPA at her site. All matters should be directed toward the on-site supervisor or State Breastfeeding Coordinator as appropriate. 3. The BFPC follows established yielding/referring procedures for issues outside of their scope of practice in accordance with DC WIC policy 4.002 Position Descriptions and attachment 2.011A BFPC Scope of Practice. 4. All BFPCs document in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.012 BFPC Contact Requirements. 5. Monthly records related to breastfeeding contacts must be submitted to the State Agency by the 10th of the following month via email to info.wic@dc.gov. 7. BFPCs will be available to participants outside of regular clinic hours, as needed. DEFINITIONS Designated Breastfeeding Expert (DBE) – an individual who is an expert with special experience or training in helping breastfeeding mothers and who provides breastfeeding experience and care for more complex breastfeeding problems when WIC staff face situations outside of their scope of practice. Individuals with this designation can be WIC staff including Breastfeeding Coordinators, IBCLCs, CLCs, or nutritionists. DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.012 1 | P a g e Title: Breastfeeding Contact Requirements Category: Nutrition and Breastfeeding Education CFR Reference: 7 CFR § 246.11 Policy Number: 2.012 Effective Date: 8/15/23 Revised Date: 8/15/23

POLICY STATEMENT The Local Agency establishes procedures for BFPCs to contact and refer pregnant and postpartum participants to ensure adequate breastfeeding care and support. PROCEDURE 1. The Local Agency ensures that the initial breastfeeding assessment is performed by a CPA/CPPA and is documented in the participant’s record in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.003 Nutrition and Breastfeeding Assessment. The CPA/CPPA is responsible for referring participants into the Breastfeeding Peer Counselor (BFPC) program. If a participant declines to participate in the BFPC program, the WIC staff member must document as such in the participant’s record. 2. The Local Agency determines the frequency of BFPC contacts with the following minimum standards: a. Participants should have at least one contact with a BFPC during their pregnancy, and b. Participants should have at least one contact with a BFPC after delivery. 3. The Local Agency must ensure BFPCs document: a. All successful contacts and contact attempts in the Peer Counselor Screen of the MIS. b. Future callback dates within appropriate timeframes established by the Local Agency. c. The content of the successful contact in the participant’s note section of the MIS at the discretion of the BFPC for continuity of care. 4. The State Agency recommends more frequent breastfeeding contact and support for high-risk pregnant and postpartum participants (e.g., pregnant with multiples, history of preterm or early term delivery, etc.) in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.008 Serving High Risk Participants. a. The Local Agency DBE or breastfeeding authority will determine the need for more frequent breastfeeding contact and support. b. The BFPC may continue to contact participants with breastfeeding concerns outside of their scope but may not provide counseling or education on these issues. REFERENCES FNS WIC Nutrition Service Standard # 9 FNS WIC Breastfeeding Policy and Guidance (2016) DC WIC Policies 2.003 Nutrition and Breastfeeding Assessment, 2.008 Serving High Risk Participants

body:
DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.013 1 | P a g e Title: Breastfeeding Aids and Accessories Category: Nutrition and Breastfeeding Education CFR Reference: 7 CFR § 246.14(c)(1) Policy Number: 2.013 Effective Date: 12/29/2000 Revised Date: 8/15/23

POLICY STATEMENT The Local Agency must make breastfeeding supplies available to participants to assist in managing breastfeeding concerns. PROCEDURE The Local Agency must: 1. Maintain a supply of breast pumps (manual and electric), as well as breast pads and other appropriate supports as determined by the State Agency. 2. Ensure that breastfeeding participants are instructed on hand expression of breast milk, breast milk handling and storage, and pump cleaning before issuing a breast pump. 3. Provide participants with resources to procure a breast pump from their insurance (if applicable) while pregnant or after delivery. 4. Provide training to staff on how to use and distribute breastfeeding aids and accessories. 5. Ensure staff document the aid in the MIS. 6. Nipple shields, if provided, must only be distributed under the guidance of a WIC-designated DBE or IBCLC as a short-term solution to breastfeeding issues. NUTRITION SERVICE ADMINISTRATION (NSA) FUNDS Local Agency allowable costs on NSA funds: • Breast pumps, • Breastfeeding aids that directly support the efforts of breastfeeding parents to remove milk from the breast and/or provide human milk to their infants, • Breastfeeding accessories are devices or products that, while not directly aiding the removal of milk from the breast, may facilitate breastfeeding. Unallowable NSA costs: • Breastfeeding aids/accessories that do not directly support the initiation and continuation of breastfeeding cannot be purchased with WIC funds. • Examples include topical creams, foot stools, baby bottles, nursing blouses, etc. (See the USDA Breastfeeding Policy and Guidance, 2016, for more information.) BREAST PUMPS The State Agency has discretion to determine under what conditions breast pumps may be issued to WIC participants (USDA Breastfeeding Policy and Guidance, 2016). The DC WIC State Agency allows breast pumps to be issued to any WIC participant who is breastfeeding. Breast pumps should not be issued to pregnant participants unless they are breastfeeding a WIC participant infant. DC WIC encourages participants to obtain a breast pump through their health insurance. The Local Agency must obtain approval from the State Agency prior to procuring breast pumps to align with cost containment measures. To be compatible with the MIS, the State Agency recommends that

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 2.013 2 | P a g e the breast pumps purchased by the Local Agency have the serial number on the outside of the pump box. The State Agency recommends that participants be counseled on proper use of a breast pump, proper cleaning, and milk storage according to CDC guidelines. The State Agency recommends the Local Agency staff follow up with the participant after issuance of a pump. BREAST PUMP RELEASE LIABILITY FORM: The Local Agency must ensure each participant issued a breast pump signs the Breast Pump Release of Liability form (see attachment 2.013A Breast Pump Release of Liability Form). The signed form must be scanned in the participant’s record in the MIS. Retention of paper records is not required. NOTES ON BREASTFEEDING AIDS: 1. The Local Agency is not permitted to charge participants for a breast pump or any other breastfeeding aid or accessory. Breast pumps are not a guaranteed program benefit but are aids that the State Agency may choose to offer WIC participants. 2. DC WIC does not distribute multi-user breast pumps, nor does DC WIC accept returns of breast pumps once issued. 3. Provision of a breast pump or breastfeeding aid(s) must accompany appropriate breastfeeding education and support. The following are general circumstances when WIC staff may issue breast pumps to participants: a. The participant is having difficulty establishing or maintaining an adequate milk supply due to maternal/infant illness. b. During mother/infant separation (such as infant hospitalization or mother’s return to work or school); and c. To mothers who have temporary breastfeeding problems, such as engorgement. REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.14(c)(1) FNS WIC Nutrition Service Standard #8 FNS WIC Breastfeeding Policy and Guidance WIC Policy Memo #1995-05 Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Proper Storage and Preparation of Breast Milk. Accessed at: https://www.cdc.gov/breastfeeding/recommendations/handling_breastmilk.htm ATTACHMENTS & FORMS 2.013A Breast Pump Release of Liability Form Refer to a thorough guide to allowable costs in the Peer Counseling Program from Minnesota WIC, accessed at: https://www.health.state.mn.us/docs/people/wic/localagency/program/finance/peerallowable.pdf (2023, Minnesota Department of Health – WIC Program, health.wic@state.mn.us)

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 3.001 1 | P a g e Title: MIS Security Overview Category: MIS CFR Reference: 2 CFR 200.313(d)(1) 2 CFR 200.333 CFR 246.25(a)(2) CFR § 246.26(d) Policy Number: 3.001 Effective Date: 01/01/2016 Revised Date: 11/30/2023

POLICY STATEMENT: The DC WIC State and Local Agency must ensure the security and integrity of participant and program data within the MIS by adhering to the following:

1. Confidentiality Agreements -Upon hiring, the Local Agency requires each staff member to sign and submit attachment 3.001A MIS Confidentiality Agreement – New User Account to ensure WIC participant data privacy. The signed form must be submitted to the State Agency before the new employee can receive access to the MIS.

Additionally, each staff member* must complete the Online Annual DC WIC Data Confidentiality/ Security Agreement as provided by the State Agency.

*Staff within their first year of hire are not required to submit the additional Online Annual DC WIC Data Confidentiality/Security Agreement.

2. MIS User ID Requests - Each State and Local Agency staff member must be given a unique user identifier (ID) to access the MIS. User access must be assigned based on the staff member’s title and role within the DC WIC program. See attachment 3.001B HANDS Permission Settings for access levels and permission settings.

If a staff member’s title and role within the DC WIC program changes, including termination of employment from the DC WIC program, the Local Agency must request a change in MIS user access.

3. IT Security Awareness Training - All State and Local Agency staff receive ongoing IT security awareness training. The State Agency will provide IT security awareness training annually (see DC WIC policy 4.004 Staff Training).

4. Protection of DC WIC IT Equipment - The Local Agency ensures that DC WIC program IT resources (e.g. computers, cell phones, laptops, scanners, etc) are secured against theft, intrusion, and unauthorized access and use. The State Agency will perform a biennial security review of the Local Agency to ensure that data files and computer programs are protected.

5. Ensuring Participant Privacy - Participant data is kept secure at employee workstations by locking computer screens when not in use, securing any loose documents that contain personal identifiable information (PII), and ensuring a private and secure space when speaking with WIC participants.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 3.001 2 | P a g e PROCEDURE Confidentiality Agreements

The Local Agency must maintain a record of all signed initial Confidentiality Agreements for auditing purposes.

The State Agency will maintain a record of all annual employee Confidentiality Agreements for auditing purposes.

MIS User ID Requests 1. The Local Agency must submit all MIS User ID requests, including change in employee’s title and role, to info.wic@dc.gov and contain the following:

Full Name

Email Address

Phone Number (if applicable)

Clinic Roles / Job Title

MIS Permission #

MIS environments (Production and/or Training)

Local Agency and Clinic Codes (“All Clinics” for access to all clinics within LA)

Reason of the request

Additionally, all new user requests must submit a signed attachment 3.001A – MIS Confidentiality Agreement – New User Account. 2. Termination of MIS user IDs – The employee’s full name, email address, and effective date of termination.

3. The State and Local Agency must maintain a record of all MIS user ID requests for auditing purposes. IT Security Awareness Training The State Agency provides annual IT security awareness training and is responsible for maintaining an annual record of staff who have completed the training.

Protection of DC WIC IT Equipment The Local Agency is responsible for monitoring staff’s use of DC WIC program IT equipment to ensure proper use. If local agency staff mishandle DC WIC IT equipment (e.g., conducting personal business, download or install unapproved software, etc.), the Local Agency must promptly notify the State Agency. The State Agency will provide directives on the course of action. Ensuring Participant Privacy In addition to locking computer screens when not in use, using screen protectors when in use, securing any loose documents that contain PII, and ensuring a private and secure space when speaking with WIC participants, State and Local Agency staff must be mindful of what information is shared and with whom and where. See DC WIC policy 12.019 Confidentiality for additional guidance.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 3.001 3 | P a g e The State Agency recommends the following: • The Local Agency provides annual training on participant data privacy. • In written correspondence, using the participant’s WIC Client ID in place of name or other PII. • Disposing of participant and/or program information via shredders or use of locked shred bins. • The Local Agency ensures facility security by establishing or following Local Agency protocols for limiting access to buildings, rooms, and equipment that store DC WIC participant and program data.

The Local Agency is responsible for notifying the State Agency promptly if a breach of confidentiality occurs.

DC WIC IT Equipment Configuration and Updates

The Local Agency must ensure all DC WIC IT equipment is regularly updated and protected against malware. See DC WIC policy 3.003 MIS Configurations and Equipment Inventory for additional guidance.

REFERENCES 2 CFR 200.313(d)(1) 2 CFR 200.333 CFR 246.25(a)(2) CFR § 246.26(d) DC WIC policies 3.003 MIS Configurations and Equipment Inventory, 4.004 Staff Training, 12.019 Confidentiality ATTACHMENTS & FORMS 3.001A MIS HANDS Confidentiality Agreement - New User Account 3.001B HANDS Permission Settings

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 3.003 1 | P a g e Title: MIS Configurations and Equipment Inventory Category: MIS CFR Reference: § 3016.32 (d)(1)(2) Policy Number: 3.003 Effective Date: 8/30/2009 Revised Date: 11/30/2023

POLICY STATEMENT: The State and Local Agency ensure that all IT equipment provided to perform the functions of the DC WIC program are properly configured, regularly maintained, and inventoried on an ongoing basis in accordance with § 3016.32 (d)(1)(2). State Agency • The State Agency provides the mandatory configuration file for use on Local Agency laptops used to perform the functions of the DC WIC program. • The State Agency is responsible for communicating IT equipment configuration and specification updates to the Local Agency. • The State Agency provides the Local Agency troubleshooting assistance of the mandatory configuration file only if specified equipment is used, see attachment 3.003A HANDS Equipment and Peripherals. Equipment used outside of that specified by the State Agency may not receive troubleshooting assistance. • The State Agency will provide the Local Agency with Pin Pads needed to perform eWIC card issuance in the MIS. Local Agency • The Local Agency is responsible for purchasing, installing, configuring, and maintaining IT equipment to the preferred specifications provided by the State Agency. See 3.003A HANDS Equipment and Peripherals for additional details. • The Local Agency must successfully test all IT equipment and its peripherals before deploying for use to perform the functions of the DC WIC program. See attachment 3.003B HANDS Peripheral Testing for equipment testing procedures. • The Local Agency must maintain IT equipment inventory and inventory records for auditing purposes. Records must be kept on file for three years.

PROCEDURE IT equipment The State Agency will provide the Local Agency with a listing of required IT equipment and peripherals needed to perform the functions of the DC WIC program. This includes IT equipment such as: • Networked printers • Card readers • Desktop scanners • Laptops • Signature pad

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 3.003 2 | P a g e • Pins Pads – only to use those provided by the State Agency • USB hub • Docking station See 3.003B HANDS Peripheral Testing for IT equipment testing procedures. IT Equipment Configuration The State Agency provides the Local Agency the most current mandatory configuration file to be installed on all laptops that are used to perform the functions of the DC WIC program. For Local Agency procured laptops, the Local Agency may add its own imaging if it does not interfere with the most current MIS configuration file. IT Equipment Inventory The Local Agency must annually review and verify their equipment inventory and submit an inventory log to the State Agency at the end of September of each year. See attachment 3.003C Equipment Inventory Reporting Template for logging and inventorying IT equipment. The Local Agency must dispose of any IT equipment that is lost through theft, irreparable or obsolete according to the Local Agency’s electronic equipment disposal procedures. Disposal of equipment must be accompanied by a completed copy of the Local Agency’s Disposal Report internal to the organization, or a police report for stolen equipment. REFERENCES § 3016.32 (d)(1)(2) ATTACHMENTS & FORMS 3.003A HANDS Equipment and Peripherals, 3.003B HANDS Peripheral Testing, 3.003C Equipment Inventory Reporting Template

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

4.001 1 | P a g e Title: Staffing Requirements Category: Nutrition Services Staffing CFR Reference: 7 CFR § 246.3 (e) 7 CFR § 246.11(c) Policy Number: 4.001 Effective Date: 11/30/2016 Revised Date: 8/15/23

POLICY STATEMENT The Local Agency must appropriately recruit, hire, and train staff to administer an efficient and effective Program including, but not limited to, the functions of nutrition education, breastfeeding promotion and support, certification, food delivery, fiscal reporting, monitoring, and training. PROCEDURE 1. The Local Agency must develop staffing practices to ensure Program benefits are delivered in the most effective and efficient manner, and must comply with the USDA regulations governing nondiscrimination, citation §246.8 Nondiscrimination and OMB regulations governing the administration of grants, 2 CFR part 200, FNS guidelines and instructions. 2. The Local Agency must outline their staffing each year in the budget and budget narrative in accordance with DC Health Office of Grants Management requirements and DC WIC policy 10.001. 3. The Local Agency must fulfill staffing needs according to position standards in DC WIC policy 4.002. The State Agency recommends a staffing ratio of 1:300 participants. The State Agency reserves the right to advise the Local Agency on staffing ratios if guidance is obtained from USDA on a national or regional level. 4. All Local Agency staff must complete task-specific training as outlined in policies 4.002 Position Descriptions and 4.004 Staff Training. REFERENCES 7 CFR § 246.3 (e) 7 CFR § 246.11(c) DC WIC policy 4.002 Position Descriptions, 4.004 Staff Training, 10.001 Local Agency Reporting Procedures

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 4.002

1 | P a g e Title: Position Descriptions Category: Nutrition Services Staffing CFR Reference: 7 § 246.3(e) 7 § 246.11 (c)(7)(ii) 7 § 246.8 Policy Number: 4.002 Effective Date: 11/30/2016 Revised Date: 6/15/2026

POLICY STATEMENT The Local Agency must ensure that sufficient staff is available to administer an efficient and effective Program including, but not limited to, the functions of nutrition education, breastfeeding promotion and support, certification, food delivery, fiscal reporting, monitoring, and training. PROCEDURE Qualified staff must be employed or on contract with the Local Agency to provide WIC services in accordance with federal regulations, the DC WIC State Plan, and DC WIC policies. Program budget, participation, and Local Agency needs should be considered when determining staffing levels for WIC services. The Local Agency is responsible for hiring WIC staff according to the guidelines set forth in this policy and their own Local Agency organizational policies for hiring and credentialing. In accordance with the DC Code, paraprofessionals (such as dietetic technicians or assistants) must work under the supervision of a licensed dietitian or nutritionist. The State Agency recommends that the Local Agency have adequate bilingual staff to serve their participant population. The State Agency provides minimum requirements for each Local Agency position (outlined below). The Local Agency must ensure their job descriptions and postings align with the minimum requirements set forth below. The State Agency requires that Local Agency have a Local Agency WIC Director (LAD) to administer the program. Not all positions listed below are required; the positions that each Local Agency requires for operations is at the discretion of the Local Agency. The State Agency reserves the right to advise the Local Agency on staffing ratios if guidance is obtained from USDA on a national or regional level (see DC WIC policy 4.001 Staffing Requirements). REFERENCES FNS WIC Nutrition Services Standards 3 and 4 Code of the District of Columbia § 3–1207.01. Qualifications for licensure. Code of the District of Columbia § 3–1201.02. Definitions of health occupations.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

4.002 2 | P a g e MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS FOR EACH LOCAL AGENCY POSITION The following describes the minimum requirements for each Local Agency position title. WIC Local Agency Leadership Position Title Qualifications Roles and Responsibilities Local Agency Director (LAD) • Master’s degree in public health, nutrition science, dietetics, or other health related field or bachelor’s degree with at least 3 years of professional experience in a public health setting. • Supervisory experience preferred. • Experience in administrative or operations management in a health care setting preferred. • Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN) and/or Licensed Dietitian or Nutritionist (LD/LN) in the District of Columbia preferred. If the Local Agency does not employ a licensed CPA, the LAD must maintain licensure. • Supervises Local Agency staff; ensures staff are trained and performing job roles in accordance with DC WIC policy and procedures. Conducts annual performance reviews. • Develops the Local Agency Nutrition Services Plan and completes required documents and reports as requested by the State Agency. • Assesses program data to analyze trends and make informed program decisions. • Participates in monthly LAD meeting and quarterly technical assistance meetings with the State Agency. • Develops and maintains the Local Agency WIC Program budget. • Plans and coordinates outreach and other program activities with program partners and community-based organizations. Local Agency Nutrition Coordinator (NC) • Must meet minimum qualifications of a CPA. • Minimum 2 years of job-related experience. • Completes a competency-based training program on performing duties of CPA. • Performs duties of the qualified nutritionist and • Participates in the development of the Local Agency Nutrition Services Plan • Participates in professional development activities. • Provides in-service training to local agency staff on nutrition services. • Assists in supervision of local agency staff who provide nutrition services. • Provides technical assistance to local agency staff and community partners, as warranted. • Coordinates with the Local Agency Breastfeeding Coordinator to plan breastfeeding activities for the local agency and community partners.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

4.002 3 | P a g e WIC Local Agency Leadership Position Title Qualifications Roles and Responsibilities • Conducts QA/QI activities that ensure the local agency operates in accordance with DC WIC policies and procedures. • Assists the LAD in development and management of the nutrition services budget.

Nutrition Position Title Qualifications Roles and Responsibilities Competent Paraprofessional Authority (CPPA) CPPAs must meet one of the following qualifications: o Bachelor’s degree in nutrition or other health-related field or o A minimum of two years of WIC experience or other relevant healthcare experience and a minimum completion of at least three* of the following accredited health-related courses:  Intro to Nutrition or Nutrition Basics  Community or Public Health Nutrition  Health Education or Health Sciences  Lifecycle Nutrition  Nutrition Assessment or Diet Assessment & Planning  Nutrition or Health Counseling, or Health Communication *Certified lactation coursework (i.e. CBS or CLC) will be credited towards • Screens for program eligibility; assesses and documents a participant’s nutrition risk(s), provides nutrition and breastfeeding education to low-risk participants, identifies the need for individual care plans, refers participants to other health and social services and provides appropriate follow-up referrals. • Responds to participant inquiries, answers phone and emails, schedules appointments. • Conducts individual and/or group nutrition education appointments. • Participates in professional development activities.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

4.002 4 | P a g e Nutrition Position Title Qualifications Roles and Responsibilities the minimum coursework completion.

• Customer service and computer skills preferred. • Completion of a competency-based training program from the State Agency. Qualified Nutritionist; Competent Professional Authority (CPA) • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in dietetics, nutrition, or nutritional science or physician, physician assistant (PA) or registered nurse (RN); or State Agency- approved health official.lIC • Licensed Dietitian or Nutritionist (LD or LDN) in the District of Columbia required. • Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN)* or Certified Nutrition Specialist (CNS) required. *RD registration-eligible candidates may qualify only with verified exam eligibility status. Continued employment is contingent on passing the RD exam and obtaining DC licensure within 6 months of hire. Failure to meet these requirements will result in demotion or separation from employment. • Completion of a competency-based training program from the State Agency on performing duties of CPA. • Screens for program eligibility; assesses and documents a participant’s nutrition risk(s), identifies the need for individual care plans, refers participants to other health and social services and provides appropriate follow-up referrals. • Provides nutrition and breastfeeding education to participants identified as high-risk; implements individual care plans and conducts follow-up to monitor/evaluate health outcomes and need for additional services. • Reviews requests for special formulas and WIC-eligible nutritionals; coordinates care with participant’s health care team, as appropriate • Conducts individual and/or group nutrition education appointments. • Participates in professional development activities. • May assist in the planning and coordination of the Local Agency Nutrition Services Plan. • May assist in training of local agency staff; performing staff observations, and/or reviewing program metrics to assist in the development of the Local Agency Nutrition Services Plan

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

4.002 5 | P a g e Breastfeeding Position Title Qualifications Roles and Responsibilities Local Agency Breastfeeding Coordinator • Meets minimum qualifications of a CPA or DBE • Minimum 1 year experience counseling breastfeeding participants. • CLC or IBCLC preferred. • At minimum, completes WIC Breastfeeding Curriculum levels 1-4 • Coordinates with the LAD and NC breastfeeding promotion and support activities for the local agency and community partners. • Conducts QA/QI activities related to breastfeeding promotion and support in the local agency. • Ensures local agency staff are trained and kept up to date on breastfeeding education and promotion; ensures staff provide breastfeeding support within scope of practice. • Provides supervision to breastfeeding peer counselors (BFPCs) • Ensures that breast pump issuance, inventory, and maintenance are logged and monitored. • Reports on BFPC program activities to LAD and the State Agency • Participates in professional development activities. • May serve as the local agency’s designated breastfeeding expert (DBE) if qualified according to the DBE requirements. Breastfeeding Peer Counselor (BFPC) • Has personal experience with breastfeeding, having breastfed at least one baby. • Ideally is a paraprofessional (without extended professional training in health, nutrition, or clinical management of breastfeeding) who shares characteristics found in the WIC population served at the local agency. • Completion of competency-based training and WIC Breastfeeding Curriculum levels 1-2. • Provides mother-to-mother support to prenatal and postpartum WIC mothers by providing basic BF information and encouragement. • Is available to participants outside of usual clinic hours and the WIC clinic environment. • Follows issuance guidelines of breastfeeding aids in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.013 Breastfeeding Aids and Accessories. • Counsels prenatal and postpartum participants by telephone as well as face-to-face visits at the home, hospital, and/or WIC clinic at regularly scheduled intervals. • Refers participants to the WIC DBE, CPA, or other appropriate health or social service agency, including outside community breastfeeding resources, for situations outside the peer counselor’s scope of practice. • Participates in professional development activities.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

4.002 6 | P a g e Breastfeeding Position Title Qualifications Roles and Responsibilities Designated Breastfeeding Expert (DBE) • Meets minimum qualifications of CPA or has completed a minimum of 8 college courses in health sciences (will require State-Agency approval). • CLC or IBCLC strongly preferred. • At least 1 year experience counseling breastfeeding participants. • Completion of USDA WIC Breastfeeding Curriculum levels 1-4. • Assists breastfeeding participants with complex breastfeeding challenges. • Provides follow-up support to breastfeeding participants. • Documents breastfeeding support in the participant’s record; coordinates with health care team of participant, as warranted; provides and documents appropriate referrals for participants. • Participates in professional development activities. • May serve as a breastfeeding resource and mentor for local agency staff. • May provide breastfeeding training for local agency staff. • May participate in breastfeeding activities in the community.

Administrative Support Position Title Qualifications Roles and Responsibilities Nutrition Education Technician (NET) /Administrative Clerk • High school diploma or GED • Demonstrated customer service, time management, and computer skills. • At least 6 months of experience in a community health setting preferred. • Bilingual preferred. • Screens for program eligibility. • Greets and receives new program applicants; answers telephone, responds to email requests, schedules appointments. • Responds to participant inquiries, provides referrals for participants; documents according to establish DC WIC and the Local Agency policy and procedures. • Conducts secondary nutrition activities in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.007 Nutrition Education Choice. • Participates in professional development activities.

4.003 - 1 Organization and Management

Revised June 2019 IX. Organization and Management – Time Study

PROCEDURE 4.003 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration Revised July 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 7/26/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.11 – Nutrition Education CFR § 246.14 –Program Costs (1)

III. Applicability DC WIC State and Local agencies. IV. Policy Statement 1. Federal regulations require that time studies be conducted to document the amount of time each staff devotes to nutrition education, breastfeeding, program management , and client services in their time allocated to WIC. 2. The time study must be conducted for a one (1) month period per calendar quarter. All persons who perform WIC functions, including students, volunteers and WIC staff (paid and in-kind), should complete the time study.

V. Definitions & Acronyms  Nutrition Education means individual or group education sessions and the provision of information and education materials designed to improve health status, achieve positive change in dietary habits, and emphasize relationships between nutrition and health, all in keeping with the individual’s personal, cultural, and socio-economic preferences.  Program Management means oversight of activities within the clinic to ensure program success including providing certification assessments, scheduling appointments, monitoring training and reports, etc  Client Services means any interactions with Program participants including administrative activities (answering phones, issuing food benefit checks, pulling and filing charts, etc) and taking participants anthropometric / biochemical measurements.  Breastfeeding means time spent performing breastfeeding promotion and support activities including providing counseling to breastfeeding mothers, and documenting breastfeeding contacts in CARES, etc.

For more detailed descriptions of activities per each staff functional category, see appendix 4.003B Category Descriptions.

4.003 - 2 Organization and Management

Revised June 2019 VI. Procedures for Conducting a Time Study 1. Receive a memorandum from State Agency with details regarding the time study 2. Refer to appendix 4.003A- Local Agency Time and Effort Form (excel sheet). Follow instructions for completing the various worksheets that are to be submitted to the State Agency. A Category description (Appendix 4.003B) is provided to describe categories of duties. 3. Use the Time Study Worksheet Tab in 4.003A to conduct the time study for the one-month period per quarter. The month that will be tested from each quarter will be randomly assigned by the State Agency each fiscal year. 4. Complete the Time Study Worksheet tab for all persons who perform WIC functions, including students, volunteers and WIC staff. Each person must complete a worksheet for a one-month period to fulfill the time study requirements. 5. Local Agency Directors or a designated authority must complete the Local Agency Site Summary and the Local Agency Summary Sheet tabs . 6. Submit first, second, third and fourth quarter time studies on January 15, April 15, July 15 and October 15 of each fiscal year.

VII. Appendix

4.003A Local Agency Time and Effort Form (excel document) 4.003B Category Description of Tasks 4.003C Time Study Instructions pdf

VIII. Reference N/A

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 4.004 1 | P a g e Title: Staff Training Category: Nutrition Services Staffing CFR Reference: 7 CFR 246.11(c)(2) and 246.11(c)(7) Policy Number 4.004 Effective Date Revised Date 8/15/23 POLICY STATEMENT The State and Local Agency provide all staff initial and ongoing training specific to their job roles and responsibilities in accordance with DC WIC policy 4.002 Position Descriptions. All DC WIC staff must attend the State Agency New Employee Training within the first 6 months of hire. PROCEDURE 1. The State Agency recommends that the Local Agency designates a Local Agency Trainer to assist in overseeing staff training activities including new employee onboarding, identifying staff training needs, and conducting training sessions at the Local Agency in-service meetings. 2. The Local Agency ensures timely completion of all new employee training materials as provided by the State Agency. Each staff member must receive task-specific training as in accordance with DC WIC policy 4.002 Position Descriptions. 3. The Local Agency ensures all new staff attend the State Agency New Employee Training within the first 6 months of hire. Prior to attending State Agency New Employee Training staff must: a. Have worked at the Local Agency for a minimum of 6 weeks. b. Completed all required training and observation logs as provided by the State Agency. 4. The State Agency conducts quarterly all-staff meetings to provide program updates, professional development, and ongoing technical assistance. All staff are strongly encouraged to attend. If staff are unable to attend the quarterly meetings, it is the responsibility of the Local Agency to ensure that the staff member receives all updates and performs their job in accordance with the most recent program directives. The State Agency reserves the right to change the schedule of training according to Program needs. 5. The State Agency will provide ongoing breastfeeding technical assistance to Local Agency staff. The Local Agency is responsible for ensuring the appropriate staff attend these meetings and perform their job in accordance with the most recent State Agency requirements. REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.11(c)(2) 7 CFR 246.11(c)(7) FNS WIC Nutrition Service Standard # 5 DC WIC policy 4.002 ATTACHMENTS & FORMS New Employee Online Training Guide New Employee Competency Checklist New Employee Observation Checklist New Employee Workbook
