5.001 - 1 Nutrition Services + Admin

Revised August 2019 V. Nutrition Services & Administration (NSA) - Overview of Financial Management PROCEDURE 5.001 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised: July 2019 Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 11/23/2015

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.16(d) Distribution of funds to local agencies

III. Applicability DC WIC State and Local Agencies IV. Policy Statement Financial Management of the District of Columbia’s WIC Program shall ensure that all local agencies develop and implement a financial management system consistent with requirements prescribed by FNS and the State Agency pursuant to the requirements of this section. The regulations, circulars and policies that govern operations of the WIC state and local agencies are: 1. Federal a) Federal Register 7 CFR Part 246 WIC Program Consolidated Regulations

b) 2 CFR 200 Uniform Administrative Requirement, Cost Principals, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards

c) FNS Memo SFP 10-017, Updated Prior Approval Guidance 2. District a) Local Agency Policy and Procedure Manual b) WIC Conditions of Grant Award c) WIC and Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Budget Package All of the above referenced federal and state regulations are available on-line and should be on file at the local agency. The WIC Conditions of Grant Award and the WIC and Breastfeeding Peer Counselor (BPC) Budget Package and WIC Budget Instructions are revised annually. These updated files are issued as attachments to the annual local agency grant award letter.

5.001 - 2 Nutrition Services + Admin

Revised August 2019 The applicable regulations and policies should be consulted whenever a question is raised concerning allowable costs or procedures. If further clarification is needed, the DC WIC State Agency should be contacted. If necessary, the appropriate federal or state authority will be contacted for explanation or clarification.

V. Definitions & Acronyms Breastfeeding Peer Counselor (BPC) VI. Procedures 1. Accountability / Program Costs

a. General

Each WIC local agency must maintain an accounting system and separate records relating to the WIC grant which conform to all state and federal regulations as well as generally accepted accounting principles. Any expenditure charged to a WIC grant must be traceable to source documentation.

Federal regulations require that records be retained for at least three years from the filing of the final closeout report as outlined in section B.3 of this policy. USDA has the option of requiring a longer record retention period if it is felt to be justified, or if any of those conditions specified in Section 246.25 (a) (2) of the federal regulations exist.

WIC funds are divided into two broad categories: Food funds and Nutrition Services and Administration (NSA) funds. Local agencies are not awarded Food funds. NSA funds are further subdivided into the following cost categories i. Certification ii. Nutrition Education iii. Breastfeeding Promotion and Support iv. Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Support v. Program Operations Separate accumulation of costs under each of these categories must be maintained. The WIC local agency shall not have expenditures that exceed the award for the current fiscal year. Expenditures in excess of the current fiscal year award will be disallowed and not reimbursed by the Program.

5.001 - 3 Nutrition Services + Admin

Revised August 2019 b. Nutrition Education and Breastfeeding Spending Requirement At least 20% of NSA funds expended by each local agency must be for nutrition education. In addition, at least 5% of NSA funds expended by each local agency must be for breastfeeding promotion and support. c. Time Studies Local agencies are required to perform time studies during the first month of each quarter of the State Fiscal Year (July, October, January and April) or on a daily basis under certain circumstances. See Policy and Procedure 4.03 (Time Study Requirements for Staff Paid with WIC or BPC Funds) for further guidance. Salary and fringe cost expenditures for each quarter are allocated to the appropriate cost category based on the time study percentages. d. Other Costs Costs other than those for nutrition education and breastfeeding promotion and support must be allocated to the appropriate cost category on the monthly/quarterly expenditure report. Indirect costs are those costs incurred for a common purpose benefiting more than one program and not readily assignable to the program benefited. The WIC Program limits indirect costs to a specified percentage of actual expenditures for eligible salary line items (not including fringe benefits). This is further explained in the WIC Budget Instructions that are included with the annual local agency grant award letter. e. Inventory Records Local agencies are required to maintain equipment inventory records for all equipment items that are purchased with WIC grant funds. These records should allow easy identification of each item and its location. f. Items Requiring Specific WIC State Agency or USDA Approval Items purchased using WIC Program funds after the original budget was approved must be approved in writing by the State WIC Financial Officer. All requests are to be submitted via email. It is the responsibility of the Local Agency to retain approvals for recordkeeping purposes. • Purchases Over $1,000.00: Written approval for purchases of sensitive equipment costing $1,000.00 or more is required by the State WIC Financial Officer. Sensitive equipment includes capital or non-capital items such as all computer equipment such as laptops and notebook computers. Portable items such as tools, hand radios and cameras that are prone to theft and concealable in a handbag or briefcase are also considered sensitive items. Equipment items that are too large for concealment, such as typewriters and projectors, shall be considered sensitive items if there is a history

5.001 - 4 Nutrition Services + Admin

Revised August 2019 of loss or theft within a particular local agency. Firearms and other law enforcement type weapons are always considered sensitive regardless of acquisition cost. • Purchases Over $5,000: The USDA must be notified in writing by the State WIC Office of any automation services or equipment purchase totaling $5,000 to $99,999 within 60 days of the expenditure or contract execution. USDA approval is required prior to the purchase of any non- computer equipment item with a unit cost of $25,000 or greater. WIC State Office and USDA approval is required prior to the start of any capital improvement project (including repairs) if the total cost is $5,000 or greater. Refer to Policy and Procedure 5.002 (Administrative Costs) for instructions. • Travel: Expenses for travel, lodging, meals, conference fees, etc. for agency staff that work for both WIC and another program must be approved in advance by the local agency WIC Coordinator. Travel requests for the local agency WIC Coordinator that works for both WIC and another program must be approved in advance by their supervisor. • Incentive/Outreach Items: Prior written approval from the State WIC Financial Officer is required for the purchase of all incentive / outreach items if the unit cost exceeds $4.00. • Documentation: For the items that require approval, a copy of the approval from the State WIC Financial Officer must be maintained in the local agency files. When budget modifications are submitted, the approved items must be included in the modified budget. • Budget Line Item Revisions Any line item revision more than 10% above the original amount budgeted requires justification for the additional costs to be submitted with the budget revision , and requires prior approval from the State WIC Financial Officer. g. Audits In accordance with the provisions in Federal Register 2 CFR 200, all non-federal entities that expend $750,000 or more in a year in federal awards shall have a single or program-specific audit conducted for that year. WIC local agencies must submit a copy of the annual single audit report to the WIC State Office upon its completion. USDA and other Federal and State agencies reserve the right to audit a Local Agency's operations at any time.

5.001 - 5 Nutrition Services + Admin

Revised August 2019 h. Financial Review The DC WIC Program routinely performs Management Evaluations of local agencies. Prior to the start of the Management Evaluation, an electronic letter will be sent to the local agency fiscal staff and local agency director requesting that documentation be submitted. The requested documentation is to include, but is not limited to, cost allocation plans, proof of payment, records for costs reported to the WIC program, spending approvals and records for time studies. Documents should be submitted in electronic or paper form in the timeframe stated in the letter. Expenditures may be disallowed if supporting documentation cannot be provided. Disallowed expenditures are subject to repayment to the state WIC office. WIC funds shall not be used for the repayment of disallowed expenditures. During the Management Evaluation, the WIC financial management staff will schedule an on-site appointment with the local agency coordinator to perform a physical inventory of equipment. The on-site visit may also include a review of certain accounting records and procedures. Individual training sessions on WIC financial management policies, recordkeeping, reporting and time studies are provided to all new agency directors and fiscal officers. Additional training will be provided to any local agency staff upon request.

2. Funding, Caseload Assignments and Reporting Requirements a. WIC Grant Local agency NSA funding is awarded on a Federal fiscal year basis (Oct. 1st through Sept. 30th). Funding is awarded using the caseload assigned to each local agency, the rate per participant and base funding (based on caseload assignment). Funding rates may be adjusted annually and are subject to availability of funding. NSA Funding formula (per participant rate x caseload assignment) + Base Funding = FY Award b. Breastfeeding Peer Counselor (BPC) Funding Local agency BFPC funding is awarded on a Federal fiscal year basis (Oct. 1st through Sept. 30th). BFPC funding acceptance is voluntary for local agencies and is not required. BFPC awards are determined by using the estimated number of pregnant and breastfeeding women participants in each participating local agency and the rate per participant. Funding rates may be adjusted annually and are subject to availability of funding.

5.001 - 6 Nutrition Services + Admin

Revised August 2019 BPC Funding formula (per participant rate x estimated pregnant and breastfeeding women participants) = FY Award c. Caseload Assignments Local agency caseload assignments are determined each year in October for the Federal fiscal year starting October 1st. Assignments are based on participation from the previous year, special populations served, percent of target population being served, and any other relevant information that is available. Caseload assignments and actual participation are reviewed on a monthly basis. Caseload assignments are normally adjusted once during the year, if indicated, based on actual participation but may be adjusted more frequently at the discretion of the DC WIC State Agency. Local agencies are required to serve an average of at least 97% of their caseload assignment during the year. If a local agency does not meet this requirement, their caseload assignment may be reduced for the following year. d. Local Agency Budgets Local agencies should refer to the WIC Budget Instructions when preparing their annual budgets and budget modifications. Local agency budgets are due at the end of September each year. Budget modifications are usually limited to one per year which is due with the third quarter expenditure report. The DC WIC State Agency requires an agency Cost Allocation Plan for each budget line item that is a shared cost. The cost allocation sample format in attachment 5.007A (Budget Schedule) can be modified, as needed, to meet this requirement. e. Monthly/Quarterly Expenditure Reports The DC WIC State Agency requires the submission of expenditure reports on a monthly basis. The format for the monthly expenditure report is included in the WIC Budget Instructions and WIC Budget Package. Expenditure reports must be submitted electronically to the DC WIC State Agency through the Department of Health’s, Electronic Grants Management System (EGMS) within 30 days after the end of the preceding month being reported. If this deadline cannot be met, a request for an extension, with justification stating the reason for lateness, must be made to the State WIC Financial Officer or the WIC Program Manager in advance of the 30 day deadline. The WIC Financial Officer or the WIC Program Manager will approve or deny the request in writing f. Compliance 1) Adherence to all instructions and due dates listed in the WIC Program Budget Package is required to maintain compliance with the terms and conditions of the Federal Award. If found non- compliant, one or more of the following actions will be taken in accordance with the 2 CFR 200.338 Remedies for Noncompliance:

5.001 - 7 Nutrition Services + Admin

Revised August 2019 i. Temporary withholding of cash payments pending correction of the deficiency by the non-Federal entity or more severe enforcement action by the Federal awarding agency;

ii. Disallowance of all or part of the cost of the activity or action not in compliance:

a. Costs determined unallowable will be charged back to the agency; b. Late submissions will have a portion of funding disallowed according to the following formula:

Disallowed Cost = (Total budgeted Indirect Cost ÷ number of business days in the fiscal year) × (number of business days past the assigned due date) × 15%. iii. Wholly or partly suspending or terminating the Federal award;

iv. Initiating suspension or debarment proceedings as authorized under 2 CFR part 180 and Federal awarding agency regulations;

v. Withholding further Federal awards for the project or program;

vi. Other remedies that may be legally available. g. Local Agency Payments Local Agency payments will be made upon receipt and verification of a monthly expenditure reports.

3. Record Retention Schedule Program records must be retained for at least three (3) years following the date of filing the final closeout report for the period to which the report pertains. For example, the closeout report for Federal Fiscal Year 2010 was filed at the end of September 2011. All records for FFY 2010 must be retained for a period of three (3) years after the filing date. The following dates indicate when program records may be destroyed for each of the applicable Federal Fiscal Years: Federal Fiscal Year Dates Records May Be Destroyed FFY 2015 (10/14 – 9/15) September 30, 2019 FFY 2016 (10/15 – 9/16) September 30, 2020 FFY 2017 (10/16 – 9/17) September 30, 2021 FFY 2018 (10/17 – 9/18) September 30, 2022 FFY 2019 (10/18 – 9/19) September 30, 2023

5.001 - 8 Nutrition Services + Admin

Revised August 2019 FFY 2020 (10/19 – 9/20) September 30, 2024 FFY 2021 (10/20 – 9/21) September 30, 2025 An audit may extend the three (3) year requirement. If a particular Federal fiscal year has been audited and there are issues to be resolved, the program records must be retained until all issues have been resolved or until the end of the three (3) year period, whichever is later.

VII. Contacts

5.002 Administrative Costs VIII. Reference CFR § 246.13 (j) Local Agency Financial Management CFR § 246.14 (a)(1) Program Costs

5.002 - 1 NSA

Revised July 2019 V. Nutrition Services and Administration (NSA) – Administrative Costs (General) PROCEDURE 5.002 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised July 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 04/12/2017

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.13(j) Local Agency Financial Management CFR § 246.14(a) Program Costs

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and DC WIC Local Agencies IV. Policy Statement The State agency shall maintain a financial management system, which provides accurate, current and complete disclosure of the financial status of the Program. This shall include an accounting for all property and other assets and all Program funds received and expended each fiscal year.

Allowable Administrative Costs 1. Direct Charges – Allowable administrative costs per personal compensation; personnel benefits; postage/shipping; travel expenses; equipment purchase and rental; communications and utilities; printing and reproduction; office supplies; building and facilities space rental; maintenance; outreach services; translators and interpreters; fair hearings; transportation and other expenses directly related to WIC activities. 2. Personnel – The cost of personnel time directly involved in WIC Program operation. Time sheets or a time study must be available to support the charge of employees who spend only a portion of their time on WIC. The time of personnel employed in general capacity, such as agency directors, manager, receptionists, etc., is not an allowable direct charge. 3. Travel – The cost of local agency staff, including transportation, lodging, subsistence, and related items incurred by employees due to WIC-related business. Use of WIC funds for local agency staff to attend meetings, workshops, or continuing education sessions directly related to WIC duties may be allowed when they fall within the definition of maternal and child health or provide for the professional development of staff.

5.002 - 2 NSA

Revised July 2019 4. Equipment – All equipment including computer require State Agency approval as follows:

Non - computer equipment up to $24,999 a. Purchase or rental of equipment with a unit cost of up to $24,999 requires State Agency approval before the equipment can be purchased or rented. State Agency will respond within two (2) weeks. Non - computer equipment costing over $25,000 b. Major equipment or any other capital-related costs in excess of $25,000, must be submitted in writing to the State Agency. State Agency will respond within approximately six (6) weeks after receiving prior approval from FNS. Computer equipment up to $5,000 c. Purchase or rental of equipment with a unit cost of up to $5,000 requires State Agency approval before the equipment can be purchased or rented. State Agency will respond within two (2) weeks.

Computer equipment costing between $5,000 and $25,000 d. Major equipment or any other capital-related costs between $5,000 and $25,000 must be submitted in writing to the State Agency. State Agency will respond within approximately six (6) weeks after receiving prior approval from FNS. Guidance for equipment purchase is provided in FNS Handbook 901. e. Medical Equipment – Medical equipment purchase is limited to the following: Spectrophotometer, centrifuge and scale for measuring cell volume, scale (pediatric or adult), and measuring boards. Guidance for equipment purchase is provided in FNS Instruction 815-1, Purchase of Medical equipment 5. Equipment Documentation – Documentation of equipment purchase must be sent to the WIC Manager at the State Agency. 6. Program Incentive Items – Prior approval is required from the State Agency to purchase program incentive items. Program incentives may include promotion items given to applicant, potentially eligible persons, participants, or persons closely associated with the Program for outreach purposes to encourage program utilization and redemption. 7. Costs Associated with Childhood Immunizations – WIC participant immunization assessment, referral, education and caseload management are allowable WIC costs. The State Agency will obtain and distribute materials on immunization for clients. Local agencies with special needs must notify the State Agency for

5.002 - 3 NSA

Revised July 2019 assistance in acquiring suitable educational materials. WIC funds cannot be used to purchase or administer vaccines. 8. Building and Facilities Space Rental – Space cost is allowable when supported by justification. 9. Expenses Shared Between WIC and Other Programs – Direct charges must be based on WIC’s actual expenses or an equitable prorata charge. Documentation outlining the procedure for charging costs allowable to WIC and other programs must be on file at the main site or readily available. 10. Audits Performed by Outside Agencies – Direct charges for audits are not allowable unless accepted by the State Agency as a replacement for the USDA- required audit. The State Agency requires prior written approval for such cost. 11. Management Studies Performed by Outside Agencies – The State Agency must obtain prior written approval from the Food and Nutrition Services (FNS) for management studies performed by agencies or departments other than the State or local agency, or those performed by outside consultants under contract with the State.

Unallowable Administrative Costs 1. Indirect Costs – Some items commonly included under indirect costs may be allowable if they are itemized as a direct cost. 2. Physician and Nurse Salaries – Costs associated with these professionals are not allowed unless the WIC Manager approves them. 3. Medical and Automated Data Processing (ADP) Equipment – Except as provided for in FNS Instruction 815-1.

V. Procedures The following process must be followed concerning requests of items and services relating to administrative costs:

Equipment 1. Submit a written request to the State Agency that includes: a. A description of the equipment; b. Justification of the need; c. At least two (2) bids (including sales tax, shipping and handling); and d. Equipment specifications that include information pertaining to the model, serial number, size, quantity, and any other enhancements that can be identified as appropriate. . 2. For non-computer equipment costing up to $24,999 and computer equipment costing up to $5,000 await written notification from the State Agency within two (2) weeks.

5.002 - 4 NSA

Revised July 2019 3. For computer equipment costing over $25,000, await facilitation of approval from FNS. Upon FNS approval, the State Agency will provide a written notification within six (6) weeks.

4. Upon receipt of the equipment, send the following information to the WIC Program Manager: a. Description of the item(s); b. Cost; c. Date of acquisition; d. Manufacturer’s or other serial number; e. Source of the item; f. Use and location; and g. A copy of the bill of sale.

5. Label equipment with the inventory number.

6. Update the inventory report form and submit it to the State Agency with the monthly invoice.

Program Incentive Items 1. Complete the Incentive Approval Request Form in Appendix 5.002A. 2. Submit to the State Agency. 3. Allow two (2) weeks for review and response from State Agency.

Building and Facilities Space Rental

Submit a request to the State Agency with the following information: 1. Justification of need; 2. Name and address of lease-holder; 3. The location; 4. The number of square feet allocated to WIC; 5. The cost per square foot per year; 6. The total monthly and annual rent costs; 7. What the rental includes (utilities, maintenance, etc.); and 8. A statement that the space will be used for WIC Program purposes only. Audits Performed by Outside Agencies

Submit a request to the State Agency with the following:

5.002 - 5 NSA

Revised July 2019 1. Scope of the audit; 2. Time period covered; 3. Cost allocation method to be used to distribute cost (when the audit covers other Programs); and 4. Certification to confirm the independence of the audit entity.

Management Studies Performed by Outside Agencies 1. Submit written request to the State Agency. 2. Upon receipt, the State Agency will review and determine if request is necessary and appropriate. 3. After the internal review, the State Agency will forward the request to FNS for review and response. 4. Await written notification from the State Agency.

VI. Appendix

5.002A Incentive Approval Request Form

VII. Reference N/A

5.004 - 1 NSA

Revised July 2019 V. Nutrition Services and Administration (NSA) – Outreach, Nutrition Education, and Breastfeeding Promotion Items

PROCEDURE 5.004 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised July 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 07/01/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.16(d) Distribution of funds to local agencies

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and DC WIC Local Agencies

IV. Policy Statement WIC Program outreach or promotional items refers to a class of goods, usually of a nominal value, that are given to applicants, participants, potential participants, or persons closely associated with the WIC Program (such as staff) for the specific program purposes of outreach, nutrition education, and breastfeeding promotion. The local agency shall determine whether an item meets the criteria for a specific program purpose as outlined below. They shall also give careful consideration to the public perception of program funds spent on items even when the connection to outreach, nutrition education, and breastfeeding promotion and support is clear.

V. Definitions & Acronyms Outreach means promotional efforts to encourage and increase participation in the WIC Program.

Nutrition Education means “individual or group education sessions and the provision of information and educational materials designed to improve health status, achieve positive change in dietary habits, and emphasize relationships between nutrition and health, all in keeping with the individual’s personal, cultural, and socio-economical preferences” (7 CFR 246.2).

Breastfeeding promotion means strategies, initiatives, and services to encourage and increase the initiation and support the duration of breastfeeding among WIC participants.

VI. Procedures 1. The local agency shall purchase and distribute outreach or promotional items according to procurement Policies and Procedures provided they meet the guidelines in one of the following categories:

5.004 - 2 NSA

Revised July 2019 a. Outreach - Outreach efforts must be consistent with the goals of the WIC Program. Outreach may be a local or statewide effort, directed at increasing the number of participants at a local agency or reaching a group of potential participants who are unaware of the WIC Program or unsure how to access it. Program outreach items for outreach shall:

a. Contain a WIC specific message that targets the potentially eligible population; b. normally be seen in public; c. contain the USDA nondiscrimination statement on publications or other printed materials that include program information; d. have value as outreach devices that equal or outweigh other uses; e. include WIC contact information such as the state or local agency name, address and/or telephone number; f. constitute or show promise of an innovative or proven way of encouraging WIC participation; and g. be reasonable and necessary costs with a total cost per item of less than $4.00

If you are unsure if an item is allowable or if the cost per item exceeds $4.00, please contact the DC WIC Financial Manager before the item is purchased for their review and approval.

b. Nutrition Education c. Breastfeeding Promotion

2. Monitoring - Purchase of outreach items will be reviewed during the management evaluation process. If the State Agency determines through a review of the local agency’s reports, program or financial analysis, monitoring, or audits that an outreach or promotion item fails to meet the criteria outlined in this policy, or the purchase did not comply with procurement policies and procedures, a formal claim may be assessed against the local agency in accordance with & CFR 246.23 (a) (1).

VII. Examples of Allowable and Unallowable WIC Program Outreach or The determination of an allowable item is more dependent upon the context of an item’s use and the message it conveys than the item itself. Using the criteria listed in the preceding paragraphs for specific Program purposes, the following are some examples of allowable and unallowable program outreach or promotional items.

1. Examples of Some Allowable Items

5.004 - 3 NSA

Revised July 2019 Promotional Items a. Outreach – T-shirts, buttons, diapers, bibs, toothbrushes, pens, cups or other items of nominal value with reasonable opportunity for public display that contain a WIC promotional message b. Nutrition education – books, calendars that contain important nutrition education messages, refrigerator magnets picturing the MyPlate, and sippy cups that are provided to mothers of infants who are learning how to drink from a cup as reinforcement of a relevant nutrition education c. Breastfeeding promotion and support – t-shirts, buttons or other items of nominal value with a breastfeeding promotion or support message printed on the item (e.g. “Breast Fed is Best Fed”)

2. Examples of Some Unallowable Items a. celebratory items or items designed primarily as staff morale boosters, generally for the personal use of the staff, with minimal public display b. items of nominal value which have no outreach, nutrition education, or breastfeeding message c. any program outreach item intended for persons who are not participants, potential participants or their parents/guardians, or for persons with no connection to the WIC Program, such as staff and cooperating agency representatives d. items not of nominal value such as diaper bags, infant slings, or ponchos (regardless of any outreach, nutrition education, or breastfeeding promotion messages). These items would not meet the “reasonable and necessary” test.

If you are unsure if an item is allowable or if the cost per item exceeds $4.00, please contact the DC WIC Financial Officer before the item is purchased for their review and approval.

VIII. WIC Program Staff and Outreach Items Recognizing that program staff travel throughout the general community and participate in various cooperative functions with the target WIC population or agencies that also service the WIC target population, it may occasionally be appropriate to provide some types of program incentive items to program staff. The items must present a WIC outreach, nutrition education or breastfeeding message and contain the local WIC agency name and contact information (telephone number or web site) as opposed, for example, to an agency logo and must be items that would be widely seen by the general population or the target population. Items whose exposure will likely be limited to the office surroundings of the staff members will generally not be allowable costs. Items purchased specifically for staff must meet the criteria above.

IX. Appendix

N/A X. Reference 5.005A Allowable Costs for Program Materials

5.005 - 1 NSA

Revised July 2019 V. NUTRITION SERVICES & ADMINISTRATION (NSA) – Allowable Costs for Program Support Materials

PROCEDURE 5.005 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised July 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 04/10/2017

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.16(d) Distribution of funds to local agencies

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff IV. Policy Statement USDA allows Nutrition Services and Administration (NSA) funds to be spent on incentive items and other goods and services that directly and indirectly support outreach, nutrition education, and breastfeeding. Program incentive items refer to a class of goods of nominal value that are given to applicants, participants, potential participants, and/or WIC staff persons for the purpose of outreach, nutrition education, or breastfeeding promotion. To be allowable, incentive items and other goods and services must be both necessary and reasonable for the proper administration of the WIC Program; that is, they are necessary to carry out essential Program functions, provide a benefit commensurate with the cost incurred, be consistent with the costs of similar items from other vendors, be a priority expenditure relative to other demands on available administrative resources, and have a proven or intuitive positive impact.

V. Procedures The following process must be followed by local agencies concerning claims for reimbursement:

1. Incentive items and other goods and services shall be intended primarily for participants or potential participants. Incentive items may not be given during a certification to participants’ family members who are not enrolled in the WIC Program. Incentive items can, on occasion, be provided to WIC staff provided they contain a WIC outreach, nutrition education or breastfeeding message and can be widely seen by the general or target population.

2. Local agencies shall follow these additional guidelines when purchasing program support materials:

5.005 - 2 NSA

Revised July 2019

a. Outreach: Items shall be intended to encourage and increase participation in the WIC Program, contain a WIC-specific message that targets the potentially eligible population, normally be seen in public, include the WIC contact information such as the State or local agency name, address, and/or telephone number, and constitute an innovative or proven way to encourage WIC participation.

b. Nutrition Education, including Physical Activity: Items shall be targeted to participants and be distributed to the appropriate participant category in conjunction with a relevant nutrition education contact to reinforce nutrition and physical activity messages. Items shall include messages that link nutrition and physical activity and, where possible, use or adapt existing materials such as the MyPlate materials available through the DCWIC.org website.

Examples of allowed incentive items include: an infant weaning cup or infant spoon provided to the caregiver of an infant participant at the mid- certification visit; a wall calendar with important nutrition messages; a MyPlate refrigerator magnet; a water bottle or ball given to participants to promote physical activity.

c. Breastfeeding Promotion: There are two types of program support materials for breastfeeding—breastfeeding incentives and breastfeeding aids.

1) Breastfeeding incentives shall be targeted to participants and, when applicable, be distributed to the appropriate category of participant (for example, water bottles to pregnant or breastfeeding women or diaper wipe containers to breastfed infants). If a dual nutrition education and breastfeeding message is present, the incentive shall be provided at an appropriate time for the participants’ usefulness and in conjunction with relevant nutrition education.

2) Breastfeeding aids directly support the initiation or continuation of breastfeeding (for example, breast pumps or nursing pads). They cannot be provided to participants solely as an inducement to consider or continue breastfeeding, yet should be offered to breastfeeding participants based on established need.

d. Reading Readiness: Books may be provided to participants or potential participants as an incentive item. The DC WIC Program may purchase inexpensive books that contain clear, age-appropriate nutrition education or health promotion messages.

3. Local agencies shall describe how they use or plan to use incentive items in their Annual Nutrition Services Plan.

5.005 - 3 NSA

Revised July 2019 VI. Appendix N/A

Revised July 2019 V. Nutrition Services and Administration (NSA) – Claims for Reimbursement

PROCEDURE 5.008 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised July 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 08/23/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.16(d) Distribution of funds to local agencies

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement 1. The State Agency shall distribute the funds based on monthly claims submitted by the local agency. 2. The local agency must submit program expenditures through the Department of Health’s Electronic Grants Management System (EGMS). 3. When the invoice indicates equipment expenditures, the WIC Program Inventory Report must be included. 4. Expenditures must align with the approved annual budget. Actual reimbursement will not exceed the annual budget for approved WIC expenditures. 5. The State Agency shall offset the advances made against incoming claims as they are submitted to ensure that funding levels reflect the actual expenditures reported by the local agency. 6. If awarded, claims for special projects will be invoiced and tracked separately.

V. Procedures The following process must be followed by local agencies concerning claims for reimbursement:

1. Submit the WIC Program Invoice via EGMS, and the Quarterly Staffing Report on a quarterly basis. See Appendix 5.008A for the forms and instructions. 2. Attach copies of supporting documentation for all expenses. 3. Attach the WIC Program Inventory Report (See Policy and Procedure 5.011) if equipment has been purchased during that billing period. 4. Submit the complete package to the State Agency by the due date.

5.008 - 2 NSA

Revised July 2019 5. Receive reimbursement check from the District of Columbia Department of Health. 6. On a quarterly basis, receive information from the State Agency on how the adjustment amount was derived.

VI. Appendix

5.008A WIC Program Invoice Form VII. Reference 5.011 Equipment Inventory Report

Revised July 2019 V. Nutrition Services and Administration (NSA) - Equipment Inventory, Security and Disposal

PROCEDURE 5.011 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration Revised July 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 03/28/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.13(j) Local agency financial management

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement 1. The Local Agency shall maintain an equipment inventory of non-computer equipment items purchased with WIC Program funds. 2. The Local Agency shall complete the non-computer equipment inventory form whenever equipment is obtained. 3. The Local Agency must maintain all non-computer equipment inventory items in a secure manner. 4. The Local Agency shall notify the State Agency of any non-computer equipment that is stolen. 5. The Local Agency shall dispose of non-computer equipment that is broken, too costly to repair or obsolete.

NOTE: Local Agency shall follow Policy 3.003 for managing computer and multi-media equipment. V. Procedures The following process must be followed by local agencies concerning equipment inventory, security and disposal:

Non-computer Equipment Inventory: 1. Complete the WIC Program Inventory Report with all existing items purchased since the beginning of the local WIC Program. This report is submitted as part of the Local Agency Workplan and Quarterly Narrative Report (See Appendix 10.001C). 2. Update the inventory report as new items are purchased.

5.011 - 2 NSA

Revised July 2019 3. Submit the updated inventory report to the State Agency with the Claims for Reimbursement (Policy and Procedure 5.008) for the month that the purchase was made. 4. Keep a copy on file at the Local Agency. 5. Make provision for verification of the inventory by State Agency staff during Local Agency site visits.

Non-computer Equipment Security: 1. Maintain equipment in a secure manner. 2. Notify the State Agency in writing when equipment has been stolen.

Non-computer Equipment Disposal: 1. Submit a request to dispose of equipment using the Equipment Disposal Report Form in Appendix 5.011B. 2. Send a copy to the State Agency for approval. 3. Receive written response from the State Agency within 14 business days. 4. Take action based on State Agency response.

VI. Appendix

5.011A Non-Computer WIC Program Inventory Report and Instructions 5.011B Equipment Disposal Report Form

7.001 - 1 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 VII. Caseload Management – Appointment Scheduling, Overview and Definition

PROCEDURE 7.001 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 01/01/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.2 Definitions CFR § 246.7(f)(2) Timeframe for Processing Applicants

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement 1. The local agency shall begin the processing standards for providing services to applicants at the initial point of contact, that is, when the applicant visits or makes an oral or written request for benefits to any clinic. 2. The local agency staff must schedule assessment appointments according to Policy and Procedure 7.002-7.006 of this functional area. 3. The Local agency shall provide early morning and evening appointment hours at a minimum of 50% of its clinics, or all clinics if the local agency has two or less sites. 4. The local agency shall provide certification, re-certification appointments and check pick-up availability at all times during the hours of operation. 5. When there is sufficient staff, the local agency should stagger their individual lunch hours to ensure that coverage is provided for WIC services between the hours of 11:00am - 2:00pm. 6. The Local agency shall notify the State Agency of any changes in clinic hours and operations that affect appointment scheduling at least 14 days in advance of the effective date.

V. Caseload Management Definitions Local agency shall use the following definitions of caseload management terms: a. Accessibility – The ease with which WIC information and services can be obtained by the public. b. Appointment no-show rate – The number of persons who fail to keep a scheduled appointment for WIC services divided by the total number

7.001 - 2 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 scheduled, multiplied by 100 and expressed as a percent (e.g., 10/30 = no show rate of 33%). c. Applicant – Anyone who contacts the local agency to request WIC benefits. d. Capacity – The optimum or maximum number of participants who can be served in a given setting and with a given staff configuration. e. Certification – Documentation of the eligibility of an applicant for WIC services using the specified criteria. f. Eligibility assessment – The review of categorical, residential, financial and nutrition/medical risk criteria to determine the eligibility of WIC applicants. g. Priority appointments – Appointments made within 10 calendar days of telephone or on-site request for pregnant and breastfeeding women, infants and children (potential Priority I-III), and migrant farm workers and their family members. See Policy and Procedure 8.002 Priority System for definitions of Priorities I-VI. h. Walk-in – A person who comes to the WIC clinic without an appointment or referral from a health professional and is assessed for WIC services on the same day. i. Reserved appointments – Time held to assess high-risk patients referred from clinics within health or medical center, hospital or outreach event

VI. Procedures The following process must be followed by local agency coordinators and supervisors concerning establishing caseload: 1. Ensure that all WIC employees understand the caseload management definitions. 2. Establish customer convenient early, evening, and Saturday hours for appointments at a minimum of 50% of all sites. If a Local Agency has two or fewer sites, all sites must establish customer convenient hours as indicted above. 3. Notify the State Agency of changes in clinic hours and operations that affect appointment scheduling at least 14 calendar days in advance of the effective date. 4. The State Agency must be informed as soon as possible whenever there are Local Agency site closures as the result of building maintenance issues (such as no air conditioning). Every attempt possible must be employed to alert participants who have scheduled appointments during the emergency closure of the site location. The WIC Local Agency Director can also coordinate with the State Agency IT Help Desk to generate a mass text message to alert participants of the closure and indicate the expected day/date of re-opening. Participants must be directed to a nearby WIC site during the closure of their regular WIC site.

VII. Appendix N/A

7.001 - 3 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019

7.002 - 1 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 VII. Caseload Management – Appointment Scheduling, Screening Applicants for Assessment Appointments

PROCEDURE 7.002 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date:01/01/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.7(f)(2) Timeframe for Processing Applicants III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement The State and local agencies shall use the standardized protocol for screening applicants seeking assessment appointments. See Appendix 7.002A “Script for Screening Applicants By Phone” for guidance on prescreening applicants.

V. Procedures Processing standards - Local Agencies shall process applicants within the following timeframes:

1. Timeframes begin when the individual visits the local agency during clinic hours to make an oral or written request for Program benefits. To ensure accurate records of such requests, local agencies shall record the applicant’s name, address and the date. The remainder of information necessary to determine eligibility shall be obtained by the time of certification. 2. When the local agency is not serving its maximum caseload, it shall accept applications, make eligibility determinations, notify applicants of decisions made and if applicants are to be enrolled, issue WIC food instruments, cash value vouchers or farmers’ market seasonal food instruments. 3. If not enrolled the day of the first visit, special nutritional risk applicants shall be notified of their eligibility or ineligibility within 10 days of the date of the first request for Program benefits. The State agency shall establish criteria for identifying categories of persons at special nutritional risk who require expedited services. 4. All other applicants shall be notified of their eligibility or ineligibility within 20 days of the date of the first request for Program benefits, if not enrolled during the first visit.

7.002 - 2 Caseload Management Revised August 2019 The following process must be followed by local agency staff when screening WIC applicants: 1. Determine residency in the District of Columbia. 2. Determine category (pregnant, breastfeeding or postpartum woman, infant or child) of potential applicant. 3. Determine financial status using adjunctive programs or current income guidelines. 4. Local agencies shall consider the income of the family during the past 12 months and the family's current rate of income to determine which indicator more accurately reflects the family's status. §246.7 (d)(2)(i) 5. Individuals conducting financial eligibility should check income table (appendix 8.006A) to verify if applicant is eligible for the program. 6. If deemed potentially eligible, make an assessment appointment and record the information in the appointment scheduling sheet. Inform the applicant what documents to bring and remind them to bring the child(ren) to be assessed. VII. Appendix 7.002A Script for Screening Applicants by Phone VIII. Reference 8.006A Income Guidelines

7.003 - 1 Caseload Management

Revised September 2019 VII. Caseload Management – Appointment Scheduling, Minimum Number of Appointments

PROCEDURE 7.003 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 07/28/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.7(f)(2) Timeframe for Processing Applicants

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement 1. Local agencies shall use the statewide show-rate to determine the minimum number of daily appointments. Appointments are defined as initial certifications, nutrition education/check pick-up, re-certifications, and medical updates. Each local agency shall calculate monthly show-rates. See chart listed in section V. Procedures. 2. The State agency shall review the show rate quarterly and make the necessary adjustments to reflect the rise and fall of the show-rate statewide. 3. Upon request, the State agency will provide the local agency with a print-out of the monthly summary of calls made, by the auto dialer voice messaging system. 4. The local agency should correlate the monthly enrollment average against the monthly closeout average to ascertain the utilization of the services rendered. 5. Assessment appointments shall be available eighty percent (80%) of the clinic opening hours. 6. Check pick-up/nutrition education appointments shall be available during one hundred percent (100%) of the clinic opening hours. 7. At least ninety percent (90%) of the daily, weekly, and monthly assessment appointments should be held for potential Priorities I, II and III applicants and participants: a. Whose current certification period will soon expire, b. Who call the clinic for an appointment, or c. Who visit the clinic for an appointment

7.003 - 2 Caseload Management

Revised September 2019 8. Appointments slots shall not be held for lower priorities. If, however, no appointments have been scheduled a week prior to Priority I, II and III applicants, an appointment can be given to any applicant regardless of potential priority.

V. Procedures

1) Local Agencies should refer to 4.003A to determine the number of CPA and CPPA’s that are needed to support their caseload 2) Local agencies must have adequate CPA coverage to cover the high-risk portion of their caseload 3) CPA’s should be assigned to sites with higher high-risk participation

7.004 - 1 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 VII. Caseload Management – Appointment Scheduling by Priorities

PROCEDURE 7.004 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date:

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.7(f)(2) Timeframe for Processing Applicants

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement New Assessment Appointments:

a. New pregnant and breastfeeding women, and infants and children who are potentially Priority I - III, or members of migrant households are to be given priority for WIC assessment appointments. Appointments for these priorities must be made available for these individuals within 10 calendar days of telephone or on-site requests.

b. Applicants who are not potential Priority I, II, or III are to be scheduled for an eligibility assessment appointment within 20 calendar days of telephone or on- site requests. These appointments are to be scheduled in priority order.

Subsequent Assessment Appointments:

a. Participants must receive at least 15 days advance notification of the end of their certification period.

b. Participants must be scheduled for subsequent assessment appointment within 30-days before or after the end of their current certification period based on priority (See letters “c” and “d” below).

c. The WIC clinic must designate sufficient appointment slots for women and children expected to fall within Priorities I, II, or III for subsequent assessment appointments.

d. Priorities I, II, and III participants will be scheduled for subsequent assessment appointments before the end of the current certification period.

7.004 - 2 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019

e. Priority IV - VI participants, with the exception of Priority IV pregnant women who plan to breastfeed their infants, will not be scheduled for subsequent assessment appointments before the end of the current certification period, but must be informed to call for an assessment appointment at or near the end of the certification period.

V. Procedure for new assessment appointments The following procedure should be followed when scheduling new assessment appointments:

1. Schedule potential Priority I, II, and III applicants within 10 days of initial request or earlier.

2. Schedule potential Priority IV, V, and VI applicants within 20 days of request or earlier.

If appointment cannot be made within 20 days of initial request, start a wait list. See Policy and Procedure 7.007-7.009 for instructions on starting a wait list.

VI. Procedure for Subsequent Assessment Appointments The following procedure should be followed when scheduling new assessment appointments:

1. At the last check pick-up before the certification period ends, or at least 15 days before the end of the current certification period, inform the participant or authorized representative verbally when the current certification period will expire.

2. Automatically schedule the following participants for subsequent assessment appointments: Priority I, II, and IV pregnant women who plan to breastfed their infants; Priority I pregnant women whose current risk criteria would place them in Priority III postpartum; Priority I and II infants; and Priority III children. Give a Notice of Assessment Appointment (See Appendix 7.004A).

3. Use the following document Check Pick-Up Report to identify potential Priority I, II, and III participants for subsequent assessment appointments.

4. Record appointments in the appointment scheduler and give a written appointment notice to the participants.

5. Inform participants in Priorities IV-VI to call for a subsequent assessment appointment at least two weeks before the end of their certification period.

VII. Appendix 7.004A Notice of Assessment Appointment

7.004 - 3 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019

VIII. Reference 7.007 Waiting List Overview 7.008 Non-Pre-Certified Waiting List 7.009 Pre-Certified Waiting Lists

7.006 - 1 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 VII. Caseload Management – Appointment Scheduling, Emergency Situations

PROCEDURE 7.006 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 01/01/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.7 (f)(2) Timeframes for processing applicants

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement WIC staff shall provide services to clients who are unable to obtain certification and check issues services due to emergencies (e.g., inclement weather, clinic closings, and other emergencies). V. Procedures The following procedure should be followed by local agency staff concerning emergency situations: 1. Use open scheduling for missed assessments (initial and subsequent). Do not restrict assessments based on status. Set up blocks of time for the assessment. 2. Double appointments for a specified period to accommodate missed certifications and mid-certification assessments. 3. Implement special extended hours (e.g., early morning, evenings, shift schedules and Saturday hours). 4. Allow walk-ins for check pick-up and certification. The Local Agency can designate specific days and times for walk-ins. 5. In some cases, vouchers can be mailed. Voucher mailing will be handled on an individual basis. Contact the State Agency for approval. Explore overtime pay, shift schedules, or compensatory and flexible time options to comply with the extended hours policy. VI. Appendix

N/A VII. Reference N/A

7.007 - 1 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 VII. Caseload Management – Wait List Overview

PROCEDURE 7.006 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 01/01/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.7 (f)(1) Waiting List

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement When the local agency is serving its maximum caseload, the local agency shall maintain a waiting list of individuals who visit the local agency to express interest in receiving Program benefits and who are likely to be served.

V. Procedures 1. The local agency shall maintain waiting lists of individuals who contact the local agency to express interest in receiving Program benefits when: a. There are no funds available to provide Program benefits, b. The agency has exceeded assigned caseload, or c. The agency or site has not yet achieved the assigned caseload, but is unable to provide individuals with appointments within 20 days of the date of request. 2. The waiting lists shall include the following: a. Name of the applicant, b. Date the applicant was placed on a waiting list, c. Address or phone number of the applicant and d. Status of the applicant (e.g., pregnant, breastfeeding, age of applicant) 3. The local agency shall notify individuals of their placement on a waiting list within 20 days after the initial contact. 4. The local agency shall use two types of waiting list: (a) Non-Pre-certified and (b) Pre-certified. Within each type of list, the local agency shall maintain separate sheets for the following three (3) statuses:

7.007 - 2 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 a. Pregnant women, breastfeeding women and infants – potential Priorities I, II and III; b. Children – potential Priority III and V; and c. Non-breastfeeding, postpartum women – potential Priority VI. 5. The Non-Pre-certified Waiting List is the list of individuals who have contacted the local agency, but are unable to receive an assessment appointment because of a reason listed in 1a-c above. This is the main waiting list. See Policy and Procedure 7.008 for detailed information regarding the Non-Pre-certified Waiting List.

6. The Pre-certified Waiting List is the list of pregnant, breastfeeding and postpartum women, infants and children under five years of age who have been: (a) participants on the WIC Program during the last 6 months and whose Priority is not being served at that time, but have a valid certification or (b) participants who have been pre-certified for WIC for the first time, but unable to receive benefits due to one of the reasons listed in 1a-c above. See Policy and Procedure 7.009 for detailed information regarding the Pre-certified Waiting List.

VI. Appendix

N/A

7.008 - 1 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 VII. Caseload Management – Non Pre-Certified Waiting Lists PROCEDURE 7.008 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 01/01/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.7(f)(1) Waiting lists

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement 1. The local agency shall start a Non-Pre-certified Waiting List for pregnant, breastfeeding, and postpartum non-breastfeeding women, infants and children under 5 years of age who contact the WIC clinic by phone or in person to request Program benefits. 2. The local agency shall use the CARES Applicant Prescreening data entry screen and the “Non-Pre-certified” Waiting List Form in Appendix 7.008B to maintain the waiting list. 3. Individuals on the Non-Pre-certified Waiting List must be transferred from one Non-Pre-certified Waiting List to another for the following status changes: a. Infant to child, b. Pregnant to non-breastfeeding postpartum women or c. Breastfeeding to non-breastfeeding postpartum woman. 4. Individuals on the Non-Pre-certified Waiting List must be removed for the following reasons: a. Categorical ineligibility: i. Child who has reached his/her 5th birthday, ii. A non-breastfeeding six (6) month postpartum woman, or iii. A woman who was breastfeeding and is no longer breastfeeding. b. The applicant no longer desires WIC benefits. c. The applicant failed to keep a confirmed assessment appointment without notification or good cause after being contacted by WIC staff.

7.008 - 2 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 d. The applicant has been certified for WIC. e. Death of the applicant. f. The applicant has been pre-certified and placed on the appropriate Pre- Certified Waiting List. g. The applicant transferred to another “Non-Pre-certified” Waiting List.

5. The local agency shall review the Non-Pre-certified Waiting List to determine if persons should be removed for any of the reasons listed above (No. 4a-g) on a monthly basis.

V. Procedures The following procedures must be followed by local agency staff concerning utilization of the Non-Pre-certified Waiting List: 1. Complete the Non-Pre-Certified Waiting List Form. See Appendices 7.008B and 7.008A for form and instructions. To manage the Waiting List of Applicants in the CARES system refers to chapter twelve in the Service Site WIC Training Manual. 2. Transferring Between Non-Pre-certified Waiting Lists a. Review the Non-Pre-certified Waiting List to determine if the status of any applicant has changed, i.e., infant to child, pregnant to non-breastfeeding postpartum women, breastfeeding postpartum women to non- breastfeeding postpartum woman. b. Determine which Non-Pre-certified Waiting List the person should be placed on based on the new potential priority of the person and enter the Action Taken on the original Non-Pre-certified Waiting List Form in Field 11. c. Record all the information from the original waiting list onto the appropriate new Non-Pre-certified Waiting List. 3. Removing Individuals from the Non-Pre-certified Waiting List i. Review the Non-Pre-certified Waiting List to determine person(s) to be removed. ii. Send the applicant a Notice of Removal from the Waiting List at least 15 days prior to removal. See Appendix 7.008C for a copy of the notice. Place a copy of the notice in a “Removal from the Non-Pre-certified Waiting List” file. iii. Complete Field 11: Action Taken and Date on the Non-Pre-certified Waiting List as follows: i. Action Taken. Use the codes at the bottom of the form and indicate the reason for removing the applicant from the waiting list, and

7.008 - 3 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 ii. Date Action Taken. Record the date that the applicant was notified of removal from the waiting list. 4. Removing Individuals from the Non-Pre-certified Waiting List

a. Begin this function with one of the following screens displayed: i. Participant List ii. Participant Folder iii. Participant Certification b. Click the Wait List toolbar button. The Manage Waiting List screen will display. c. Select an applicant to remove in the Waiting List table. d. Click Remove from Waiting List to remove the applicant from the Waiting List. A confirmation message displays confirming your request. e. Click, Yes to confirm the removal of the applicant from the Waiting List.

VI. Appendix

7.008A Instructions for Completing the Non-Pre-Certified Waiting List 7.008B Non-Pre-Certified Waiting List Form 7.008C Notice of Removal from the Waiting List

VII. Reference N/A

body:
7.009 - 1 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 VII. Caseload Management – Pre- Certified Waiting Lists

PROCEDURE 7.009 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 01/01/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.7 (f)(1) Waiting Lists

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement When the local agency is serving its maximum caseload, the local agency shall maintain a waiting list of individuals who visit the local agency to express interest in receiving Program benefits and who are likely to be served.

V. Pre- certified Waiting List 1. The local agency shall implement a Pre-certified Waiting List when a waiting list is in effect and upon the request or inquiry of an applicant. 2. Pregnant, breastfeeding and postpartum women, infants and children under five years of age who have been (a) participants on the WIC Program during the last six (6) months whose Priority is not being served at this time, or (b) have been pre-certified for WIC (for the first time). 3. Applicants who have a valid Verification of Certification (VOC) card shall be placed on the Pre-certified Waiting List when no space is available on the Program. 4. The local agency must notify Priority I VOC applicants of vacant slots before any other person on the Pre-certified Waiting List. 5. The local agency shall place the applicant on the Non-Pre-certified Waiting List if the certification period expires before removal/transfer from the Pre-certified Waiting List. 6. The local agency shall use the “Pre-certified” Waiting List Form in Appendix 7.009B to maintain the waiting list. 7. The local agency shall transfer individuals from one Pre-certified Waiting List to another for the following status changes: a. Infant to Child, b. Pregnant to non-breastfeeding postpartum woman, or c. Breastfeeding to non-breastfeeding postpartum woman

7.009 - 2 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019

8. The local agency shall remove individuals from the Pre-certified Waiting List for the following reasons: a. Categorically Ineligible i. A child who has reached his/her 5th birthday, ii. A non-breastfeeding six (6) month postpartum woman or, iii. A woman who is not breastfeeding b. The applicant no longer desires WIC benefits c. The applicant failed to keep a confirmed assessment appointment without notification or good cause after being contacted by WIC staff d. The applicant has been certified for WIC (transfer) e. Death of the applicant f. The applicant has been on the Pre-certified Waiting List for longer than six (6) months and the pre-certification has expired

VI. Procedure for Completing the Pre- Certified Waiting List The following procedure must be followed when completing the Pre-certified waiting list: 1. Complete the Pre-certified Waiting List form. See Appendix 7.009A and 7.009B for instructions and form.

VII. Procedure to Pre-Certify an Applicant

The following procedure must be followed to pre-certify an applicant: 1. Determine if the applicant or participant is a DC resident. 2. Determine if the applicant or participant is income eligible. 3. Determine if the applicant or participant meets the medical/nutritional risk criteria established by the Program. 4. If the applicant meets all of the above criteria and their Priority category is no longer being served, add their name and all other information to the appropriate Pre-certified Waiting List. See Appendix 7.009A for instructions on completing the Pre-Certified Waiting List. 5. If the applicant is ineligible based on the above criteria, give the applicant a Notice of Ineligibility. Enter the appropriate code on the waiting list. 6. When the above steps (a-d) are completed, record the information on the WIC Certification Form or turnaround document. 7. Place all Certification Forms for the Pre-certified Waiting List in the holding file which is a separate file kept for pre-certified persons.

7.009 - 3 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 VIII. Procedure for Transferring between Pre-Certified Waiting Lists The following procedure must be followed when transferring applicants between Pre-certified waiting lists: 1. Review the Pre-certified Waiting List on a monthly basis to determine if the status of any applicant has changed. 2. Determine which Pre-Certified Waiting List the person should be placed on based on the new potential priority. Enter the transfer code (see codes at the bottom of the form) in Field 9 on the original Waiting List. 3. Record all the information from the original waiting list onto the appropriate new Pre-certified Waiting List.

IX. Procedure for Removing Individuals from the Pre-Certified Waiting List The following procedure must be followed when removing individuals from the Pre- certified waiting list: 1. Review the Pre-certified Waiting List on a monthly basis to determine if persons should be removed. 2. Send the applicant a Notice of Removal from the Waiting List within 15 days of removal. See Appendix 7.008C for a copy of the notice. Place a copy of the notice in the individual’s pre-certification file. Place the file in the inactive files. 3. Complete Field 9: Action Taken and Date as follows: a. Action Taken: Use the codes at the bottom of the for m and indicate the reason for removing the applicant from the waiting list. b. Date Action Taken: Record the date that the applicant was notified or removed from the waiting list.

X. Procedure for Transferring Applicants from the Pre-Certified Waiting List to Active Certification The following procedure must be followed when removing applicants from the Pre- certified waiting list to active certification: 1. Contact the pre-certified applicant and inform him/her of the availability of Program benefits. 2. Confirm an appointment time for the applicant to come in to sign the rights and obligations statement and to pick-up the first set of WIC vouchers. 3. Check that the date of pre-certification, which is the date of certification, has been entered on the Certification Form. 4. Issue WIC vouchers. 5. Complete Field 9: Action Taken and Date as follows: a. Action Taken: Use the codes at the bottom of the Pre-certified Waiting List and indicate the reason for removing the applicant from the waiting list. b. Date Action Taken: Record the date that the applicant was notified of removal from the waiting list for placement on the Program.

7.009 - 4 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 VII. Caseload Management – Outreach

PROCEDURE 7.010 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date:01/01/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.6 (b)(3) Agreements with local agencies/Provisions of agreement

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement 1. The local agency shall make available appropriate health services to participants and inform applicants of the health services that are available. 2. The local agency shall recruit and accept any potentially eligible person who meets the standards for eligibility and applies for WIC. 3. The local agency shall establish close collaborations within each of their respective facilities; pre-natal OB-GYN and pediatric clinics. At least two walk-in appointment slots should be made available for each clinic (OB-GYN and pediatric) each day. WIC staff should provide the clinics with WIC outreach materials to attract potentially eligible persons. 4. The local agency shall establish close collaborations with one (1) child care center within their geographical proximity. During FY 2018 and 2019 the State Agency has established relationships with the following child care centers:  Apple Tree  KIPP  Bryia  La Clínica Del Pueblo  Rosemount  Centro Nia The State Agency can provide the contact persons and facilitate the initial stages of the collaboration.

7.010 - 2 Caseload Management

Revised August 2019 5. The local agency shall develop an outreach plan for each fiscal year with measurable goals, objectives, activities and methods. This plan shall be in accordance with the State Agency outreach goals and submitted as part of the local agency Annual Plan of Operations. 6. The local agency should also project its caseload each year based on their enrollment data; specifically targeting the category (women, infants, children) that have shown a steady decline. 7. The local agency shall project its caseload for each fiscal year based upon closeout participation from the previous fiscal year, and other demographic data. The projected caseload shall be submitted as part of the local agency Annual Plan of Operations.

V. Procedures 1. Using the Local Agency Workplan and Quarterly Narrative Report (see 10.001B), provide information on: a. Caseload projection for upcoming fiscal year using closeout data from previous fiscal year(s) and other demographic data b. Total population served c. Benefit targeting plan d. Develop an outreach plan with measurable goals, objectives and activities e. Perceived challenges f. Deviations from workplan 2. Submit these plans as part of the Local Agency Workplan to the State agency (see home 10.001 for reporting procedures). 3. Monitor and report progress, using the Status Report Form in Appendix 7.010D, on achieving outreach goals and attaining authorized caseload in the Quarterly Program Report (Appendix 10.001B) to the State Agency.

VI. Appendix

N/A VII. Reference 10.001 Reporting Procedures 10.001B Local Agency Workplan and Quarterly Narrative
