body:
VIII. Certification December 2021 8.001-1 b. Health and Nutrition Assessment o Risk Code Identification o Nutrition Education and Goal Setting o Referrals c. Food Package d. Documentation

8.001 - Certification Overview CFR § 246.7(c) Eligibility Criteria and Basic Certification Procedure; CFR § 246.7(e) Nutritional risk; CFR § 246.7(f) Processing Standards; CFR § 246.7(g) Certification Periods; WIC Policy Memorandum#2016-5 Separation of Duties at WIC Local Agencies I. Policy Statement When funding permits, WIC Program benefits must be disseminated to low-income pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding women; infants, and children up to age 5 who exhibit nutritional or medical risks, and who meet the established income eligibility criteria. DC WIC local agencies must make WIC services available to any individual who meets the eligibility requirements and applies for participation. LAs must provide WIC services to participants at no cost or financial burden to the participant. Local Agencies shall not: a. Limit participation to those persons who participate in that local agency’s health services b. Require applicants to enroll in the local agency’s health care system c. Require participants to be currently receiving health care from a private physician or other health care provider All participants will be screened and certified using the Health and Nutrition Delivery System (HANDS) automated system. HANDS will automatically document the date of initial contact in the system. WIC staff are expected to input accurate information into HANDS. By entering and saving data in HANDS, WIC staff validate and confirm that what has been entered is accurate and truthful. LAs shall not give participant information to a third party unless a signed agreement has been established between the WIC State Agency and the party in question. Such agreements will be made with the approval of DC Health. Such agreements may only be between the WIC Program and agencies that serve the WIC-eligible population. Participant records may be released to the participant, or parent/legal guardian of a participant. If the participant or parent/legal guardian wishes to share information from WIC records with a third party, they may do so without involving the WIC LA. II. Components of the Certification

a. Intake / Eligibility Screening o Physical Presence o Identity Verification o Residency Verification o Income Verification o Categorical Eligibility o WIC Rules and Regulations / Participant Rights and Obligations

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.001-2 Discussion III. Separation of Duties In order to maintain the integrity of the WIC Program, adequate safeguards must be in place to prevent fraud and abuse. At minimum, the staff person who determines income eligibility and medical or nutritional risk cannot be the same person. Either person may issue food benefits. This policy ensures that one employee does not solely perform certification and issuance food benefits. In instances where adherence to this policy is not achievable, such as sites with only one staff member on duty, the LA WIC Director or Nutrition Coordinator must perform a supervisory review of all non- breastfeeding infant certification records (food packages that contain infant formula), and at least 20% of a random sample of the remaining certification records, within two (2) weeks of certification. It is recommended that staff rotate so that the same staff person is not the only person that is known to the satellite service site. Documentation of file reviews must be maintained at the LA for review during Management Evaluations. IV. Certification of WIC Staff and/or Family Members LA staff and/or their family members may apply for WIC benefits at a service site where they, or their family member, are employed. In these cases, additional Program integrity measures must be implemented. LA staff: a. Shall not conduct any aspect of the eligibility determination or certification process for immediate family members, or themselves b. Shall not certify immediate family members, or themselves c. Shall not issue food benefits to an immediate family member, or to themselves d. May not be an AAR for more than two individuals at any given WIC service site, either for immediate family members or non-related persons Failure to adhere to this policy will result in a serious offense, subject to the maximum sanctions allowed by Federal regulations.

V. Eligibility Determination LA Staff determine if the applicant meets each of the following eligibility criteria: a. Residence b. Income c. Category d. Nutrition Risk

Image 1. Visual Map of the WIC Certification Process

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.001-3 VI. Basic Certification Guidelines The following guidelines pertain to certification appointments. a. All certification data for each applicant certified shall be documented in the participant’s HANDS record. b. All applicants must be physically present. See Policy 8.003 – Physical Presence and Identification, for more information. c. Every applicant or caretaker shall be informed of the illegality of dual participation. d. Every applicant or caretaker shall read, or have read to them, the “Rights and Obligations” statement. See Policy 8.002 – Intake Guidelines, for more information. e. During the initial certification, each participant, parent, or caretaker shall receive an explanation of how the local food delivery system operates and shall be advised of the types of health services available, where they are located, how they may be obtained, and why they may be useful. f. LAs must obtain anthropometric measurements (height or length and weight), hematological tests (blood work), and dietary and medical information using the ABCDE process for VENA appointments. g. The CPA/CPPA must analyze the following to identify appropriate nutritional and/or medical risk factors to assign corresponding risk codes and priority: o Anthropometric data using appropriate growth or weight grids o Hematological test results o Other health and dietary information obtained through the VENA process h. The CPA/CPPA will provide basic nutrition education and referrals based upon the comprehensive VENA results and identified medical/nutritional risks. i. The CPA/CPPA will tailor the food package based on risks, nutritional needs, and participant preference. j. Participants shall be issued appropriate food benefits during initial certifications and subsequent visits, which they can use at DC WIC authorized vendors. Food benefits may be issued remotely. k. LAs shall allow a 30-day certification period for individuals who do not present the necessary proof of residency, identity, or income at the time of assessment. Therefore, 30 days of food benefits should be provided to the participant. If the participant has not submitted the required documentation within the 30 days provided, they shall be terminated. l. Applicants failing to provide verification of eligibility data within the 30-day grace period will be denied participation in the program. They may reapply as soon as they have the necessary documentation. m. LAs shall provide a 15-day written or oral notice of certification due date for the participant. n. LAs will schedule applicants/participants for appropriate follow-up appointment(s). o. LAs shall attempt to contact all applicants who miss appointments. Contact attempts shall be made only if they have agreed to receive communication from the WIC Program.

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.001-4 VII. Certification Timeframes A: Will be certified for: Pregnant Woman (PG) Up to six (6) weeks postpartum. A pregnant woman enrolled in WIC who has had an abortion, spontaneous (miscarriage) or therapeutic, is eligible to receive food benefits up to six (6) weeks past the date the pregnancy ended and can continue up to six (6) months from the date her pregnancy ended as a postpartum participant. A pregnant woman who would have been eligible for the program during her pregnancy, who has had an abortion, spontaneous (miscarriage) or therapeutic, can also apply for food benefits. She is eligible for a total of six months of food benefits from the date the pregnancy ended. Postpartum Woman (P) Up to six (6) months postpartum. Breastfeeding Woman Exclusively Nursing (EN) Partially Nursing (PN) Partially Nursing Plus (PN+) Up to the infant’s first birthday or until the woman ceases breastfeeding, whichever occurs first. A breastfeeding woman who requests, after the sixth month postpartum, more than the maximum amount of formula allowed for a mostly-breastfed infant will no longer receive supplemental foods, but will continue to count as a WIC participant receiving nutrition and breastfeeding education, support, and referrals. If a woman ceases to breastfeed prior to six months postpartum, she shall have her category changed to a postpartum woman. Staff shall update the Breastfeeding Surveillance screen and the postpartum woman shall be reassessed to identify Risk Codes. Infant (I) Approximately every six (6) months. LAs may certify an infant under six (6) months of age up to the last day of the month in which the infant turns one (1) year old, if the quality and accessibility of health care services are not diminished. Child (C) Approximately every six (6) months ending with the last day of the month in which a child reaches their fifth (5th) birthday. LAs may certify a child for a period of up to one (1) year, provided the LA ensures that the child receives the required health and nutrition assessments, as set forth in § 246.11(e)(3).

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.001-5 Special Conditions The certification period may be adjusted from the original ending certification date for several reasons. It can be shortened as much as needed or extended by 30 days. Some reasons for adjusting certification end dates include:

i. Difficulty in appointment scheduling or getting to the service site for certification due to extreme hardship, e.g., illness, imminent childbirth, inclement weather conditions, distance to travel, high cost of travel, or documented physical disability that prevents travel ii. Holiday schedules impacting service site operations or the participant’s ability to make it to the service site If the participant is found eligible to continue receiving program services, the new certification period begins on the date the participant is certified again and receives the first set of food benefits in the new certification period. VIII. Priority All participants will automatically be assigned a priority level, triggered by the risk codes assigned by the MIS system or manually assigned by the CPA/CPPA. The priority which indicates the greatest level of risk will be used to certify the applicant. A detailed list of DC WIC risk codes and their priorities are located on the Local Agencies page of the DC WIC website at dcwic.org. Priority levels are described below: Priority I Pregnant women, breastfeeding women, and infants at risk based upon hematological or anthropometric measurements, or other documented nutrition- related medical conditions. Women who are breastfeeding Priority I infants with risk other than 702, or infants breastfed by Priority I women with risk other than 601. Out-of-state VOC are priority 0, all VOC are Priority I if there is waiting list in effect. Priority II Infants up to 6 months of age whose mothers participated in WIC during pregnancy. Infants up to 6 months of age born to women who would have been WIC-eligible based upon hematological or anthropometric measurements or other documented nutrition-related medical conditions. Women who are breastfeeding a Priority II infant with risk other than 702, or breastfeeding women who are eligible due to inadequate dietary patterns. Priority III Children at risk based upon hematological or anthropometric measurements or other documented nutrition-related medical conditions. High-risk postpartum women. Priority IV Pregnant women, breastfeeding women, and infants at risk due to inadequate dietary patterns. Priority V Children at risk because of an inadequate dietary pattern. Priority VI Postpartum women at nutritional risk. Priority VII Individuals certified for WIC solely due to homelessness or migrancy. Previously certified participants who might regress in nutrition status without continued provision of supplemental foods.

NOTE: Regression may not be used for initial certification, may not be used for infants, and may not be used consecutively as a reason for subsequent certification. Regression can only be used twice in a five-year period.

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.001-6 IX. Service Timeframes Applicants who fall into identified categories must be informed of their eligibility, ineligibility, or placement on a waiting list within the following number of days following the date of their request for WIC services: 10 Days 20 Days Priority I pregnant women All other applicants Infants < 6 months of age Homeless Migrants

X. Waiting Lists The CPA/CPPA shall begin a waiting list after the LA has reached its maximum participation level by applying priority system described above to the LA’s wait list. Further restrictions of categorical eligibility beyond that permitted by this policy is not allowed. See policy 7.007 for more information on waiting lists. Visit Local Agencies, Policies & Forms at dcwic.org for the Waiting List Form. XI. Food Delivery Discussion At certification, LA staff shall discuss the food delivery system with the participant/AR in their preferred language. This discussion shall include the following:

i. Which foods are authorized for purchase with WIC food benefits ii. Encourage the participant to look for the ‘We Accept DC WIC’ decal when going to a vendor to use their eWIC card. If the participant would like to see the list of currently authorized vendors, they may view it on the “Locations - Vendors” section of www.dcwic.org, or the “Vendor Search” section of the EzWIC App. If the participant requests a printed version of the vendor list, staff shall provide a current printed list of vendor names, addresses, and phone numbers. iii. How to use their food benefits – see policy 9.001 for more information

Staff shall assess participants’ understanding of allowable WIC foods and the proper use of food benefits. For additional details regarding frequency of discussing the Food Delivery System requirements, refer to Policy 9.001.

XII. DC WIC Program eWIC Card Participants will be issued one eWIC card per family. Participants will select a 4-digit personal identification number (PIN). The eWIC card and PIN can be used at all DC WIC authorized vendors to access assigned food benefits. Refer to policy chapter IX. Food Delivery, for more information on eWIC cards. Note: If the family includes a foster child, please refer to Policy 8.008 - Eligibility and Certification for Special Cases, for additional details regarding issuance of eWIC cards to families with foster children.

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.001-7 XIII. Infant/Child with Safety Plan A family with a child may present with a safety plan. A safety plan is a written agreement that a social worker from the Child and Family Services Agency (CFSA) developed with the family which clearly describes the safety services that will be used to manage threats to a child’s safety for a temporary period of time. This child is not considered a foster child and shall be included in the family’s eligibility determination. Up to two months (60 days) of food benefits may be issued and eligibility shall be reassessed at the next appointment. The safety plan shall be scanned into the participant’s HANDS record. Note: After the safety plan expires, the participant may present as a foster child with a Notice to Provider or may return to a parent’s custody. If they return to a parent’s custody, documentation may not exist as the safety plan expires. See policy 8.008 for additional details. XIV. WIC Education, Rules and Regulations Education WIC staff will follow the Nutrition Education guidelines as outlined in the policies of Section II. Nutrition Services. This section includes: Program Education Requirements for Participants; Participant- Centered Nutrition Education for Participants; Nutrition Education Care Standards; and High-Risk Nutritionist Consults.

At each certification, participants will be informed of the WIC Rules and Regulations, which include:

• The duration of the Certification period • The participant is qualified due to income, category, and nutrition risk • Option to register to vote • An explanation of the food package and how these foods can improve their health status • Food Benefits, VOC, and eWIC card security • Option to report problems with a DC WIC authorized vendor, WIC participant, WIC employee, or WIC fraud by calling: 202-442-9397, emailing info.vendor@dc.gov, or completing the online form at www.dcwic.org/contact-us • Participants/ARs will keep scheduled appointments or notify LA staff if unable to do so • Verification of marks if the applicant cannot write his or her name (See Appendix A)

XV. Referrals Documentation of referrals shall be performed at every certification by selecting the “referred” status for mandatory referrals (generated by the mandatory referral list) in the Referral section of the Care Plan screen in HANDS. By documenting “referred,” staff confirm that they have discussed referral programs with the participant or AR.

Refer to Policy 8.018 - Referrals Overview, and 8.020 - Substance Use Screening, Education, and Referrals for additional details regarding required referrals.

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.001-8 XVI. Release of Information

An applicant or participant requesting for information to be sent to a third party or organization (e.g., a doctor or a health maintenance organization) shall sign a release form. The release form shall not be signed until the Certification process is completed and the applicant has been informed of their eligibility determination.

Refer to Section 12 of the Local Agency Policy & Procedure Manual for more information on releasing WIC client information.

body:
DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.002 1 | P a g e

Title: Separation of Duties Category: Certification CFR Reference: 7 CFR 246.4(a)(27) Policy Number: 8.002 Effective Date: 7/28/2016 Revised Date: 6/15/2026

POLICY STATEMENT: The Local Agency must ensure: 1. That each participant certification is performed with separation of duties, meaning that the staff person who determines income, categorical, and residential eligibility and the staff person who determines medical or nutritional risk and issues food benefits cannot be the same person. It is prohibited for one employee to determine eligibility for all certification criteria and issue food instruments, cash-value vouchers or supplemental foods for the same participant. 2. A staff member must not certify themselves for WIC services. 3. A staff member must not certify relatives or friends for WIC services. These actions are to prevent Program abuse and fraud in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.015 Violations and Sanctions. PROCEDURE Separation of Duties for Certifications The Local Agency will designate one staff member to determine income, categorical, and residential eligibility and a different staff member to determine nutritional risk and issue food benefits at each WIC clinic site when possible (see below for when separation of duties is not possible). The State Agency recommends each WIC clinic site designate a CPA and/or CPPA, to ensure timely determination of nutritional risk and food package tailoring and issuance, in accordance with 9.001 Food Benefit Issuance Overview. When Separation of Duties is Not Possible When separation of duties is not possible due to staffing limitations and/or conducting remote WIC services, the Local Agency must designate a staff member with a supervisory role (i.e. Local Agency Director, Nutrition Coordinator, Breastfeeding Coordinator, etc) to conduct a record review of all Infant Formula Feeding (IFF) certifications performed and at least 20 percent of a random sample of the remaining certification records within two weeks of the certifying period performed without separation of duties, in accordance with WIC Policy Memorandum #2016-5 Separation of Duties at WIC Local Agencies. Attachment 8.002A Separation of Duties Audit Form must be completed for each audit, maintained at the local agency for three years, and be made available for State Agency review as requested. Each completed record audit must have a note entered by the performing audit staff stating the record review has been completed. This audit list can be accessed by the “Cert List for Audit” in HANDS > Reports > Program Integrity. Staff Certifying Themselves, Relatives or Friends These actions are prohibited for all WIC staff. If a WIC staff member requests to be certified in DC WIC, the State Agency recommends that the staff member be certified in a different local agency other than the local agency from which they are employed.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.002 2 | P a g e

Certification Monitoring Each quarter, the State and Local Agency will review staff activity utilizing the following reports in HANDS: • Average Certifications Per Day • Certifications By User • eWIC Benefits Issued Outside of Business Hours • Families With Five or More • Multiple Births

REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.4(a)(27) WIC Policy Memorandum #2016-5 Separation of Duties at WIC Local Agencies DC WIC policy 8.015 Violations and Sanctions, 9.001 Food Benefit Issuance Overview ATTACHMENTS & FORMS 8.002A – Separation of Duties Audit Form

body:
DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.003 1 | P a g e Title: Physical Presence and Identification Category: Certification CFR Reference 7 CFR § 246.7(c) 7 CFR 246.7(c)(2)(i) 7 CFR 246.7(o)(1) Policy Number 8.003 Effective Date: 08/01/2021 Revised Date: 8/15/23

POLICY STATEMENT Applicants to the WIC Program are required to be physically present at the time of certification in accordance 7 CFR 246.7(o)(1). In special cases, applicants meeting one of the exception criteria below may be certified without being physically present at the time of certification.

Applicants must present proof of identity (ID) at the time of certification. For infants and children, the ID of the Authorized Representative (AR) or Alternate Authorized Representative (AAR) must also be checked.

PROCEDURE Exceptions In special cases, applicants who meet one of the exceptions below may be exempt from being physically present at the time of certification: a. Infants less than 8-weeks-old – if they cannot be present at the time of certification for a reason determined appropriate by the Local Agency and for whom all necessary certification information is provided. b. Disabilities – applicants or applicants whose parents or caretakers have a disability and are unable to be physically present because of the disability. Examples include: • A condition which requires medical equipment that is not easily transportable • A medical condition that requires confinement to bed rest • A serious illness that may be exacerbated by coming to the WIC clinic • A serious or contagious illness c. Receiving ongoing health care – Only if an infant or child was present at their initial WIC certification and has documented ongoing health care from a provider other than the WIC Local Agency, they may be exempt if being physically present would pose an unreasonable barrier.

d. Working parents or caretakers – an infant or child who was present at the initial WIC certification and was present at a WIC certification or re-certification determination within the 1-year period ending on the date of the most recent certification or re-certification determination (example – present for initial certification in July 2021 and present for recertification in July 2022, they could be exempt from physical presence for recertification in July 2023 [if all other criteria is met and proofs provided]); and is under the care of one or more working parents or one or more primary working caretakers whose primary working status presents a barrier to bringing the infant or child into the WIC clinic.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.003 2 | P a g e NOTE: If an applicant is hospitalized on an in-patient basis at the time of certification, they may not be issued food benefits.

Physical Presence for Mid-Certification The Local Agency may offer hybrid services for mid-certification appointments as outlined in attachment 8.003A Hybrid Services. Anthropometric and hematological data must be obtained in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.010 Anthros and Bios. Documentation of Exceptions If the applicant meets an exception and is not physically present at the time of certification, staff must document this accordingly under the “Reason Client Not Present” on the Cert screen in HANDS.

Applicants may provide referral anthropometric (within the past 60 days) or hematological (within the past 90 days) at the time of their certification in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.010 Anthros and Bios.

Acceptable forms of anthropometric and/or hematological documentation include: • Doctor’s prescription form • Doctor’s letterhead with prescription • DC WIC medical prescription form • Printed medical records from a provider that includes the date of measurements and the provider’s name • Verbal medical data from a provider

NOTE: Self-reporting of height and weight is not permitted, except in the case of infant birth data. Infant birth data can be self-reported by a caregiver or obtained from hospital records/crib card and can be used for the certification of an infant if they were taken less than 60 days prior to certification. Measurements must be entered in the MIS using the date the measurement was initially taken. Documentation of Identity Applicants must present proof of ID at the time of certification. For non-certification appointments (e.g. mid-certification, CPA follow-up, etc.,) staff must verify identity by either reviewing the AR/AAR’s ID or using identifiers such as having the AR/AAR verify their date of birth, address, and/or phone number. The eWIC card is not an acceptable form of ID. Acceptable proofs of ID are listed below: Documents Accepted for Proof of ID Birth Certificate or Baptismal Certificate Military Records / ID Cards or Discharge Papers Clinic / Hospital record or ID Notice to Provider / CFSA Paperwork Driver’s License / Government ID / State ID Passport / Visa / other country ID** Immigration or Naturalization Record School Photo ID Immunization Record* Voter Registration Marriage License Verification of Certification (VOC)

* Participant name and DOB may be completed by the AR. ** A passport/visa/other country ID that lists the name field as First Name Unknown (FNU) or Last Name Unknown (LNU) is an acceptable form of documentation.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.003 3 | P a g e

Applicants with No Proof of Identity If at the time of certification an applicant did not provide proof of ID, they may receive up to one month of food benefits and must provide proof of ID before subsequent months of food benefits are issued. The applicant or AR/AAR must sign for the missing proof under “Forgot Documentation” in HANDS. The AR/AAR must provide the proof within 30 days from the date of the certification. If an applicant has no proof of ID for reasons such as theft, loss, disaster, or an asylum seeker/refugee or recent immigrant, then the applicant or AR/AAR must sign for the lack of proof under “No Proof Exists” in HANDS. The applicant, if otherwise determined to be eligible for WIC, may receive normal issuance of food benefits for their certification period. REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.7 DC WIC policy 8.010 Anthros and Bios DC WIC attachment 8.003A Hybrid Services

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.004 - 1 8.004 Categorical Eligibility CFR 246.7 (C) Eligibility Criteria I. Policy Statement To qualify for the Program, infants, children, and pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding women must reside within the jurisdiction of the District of Columbia and meet the income and nutritional risk criteria as outlined in Policies 8.005, 8.006 and 8.007, respectively. II. Categories for Eligibility

Category Description Pregnant Woman A pregnant woman. Proof of pregnancy is not required. If there is reason to suspect that a participant has falsely claimed to be pregnant, the Local Agency can request proof of pregnancy be provided within 60 days of certification. Staff will have to choose “bi-monthly issuance” in the Issuance tab under the Benefits screen in HANDS. Breastfeeding Woman A woman who breastfeeds an infant at least one time per day, up to infant’s first birthday or until she completely stops breastfeeding before the infant turns one year old.

A breastfeeding assessment shall be done before the issuance of food benefits at each certification, mid-cert assessment, when a breast pump is issued, and/or whenever the amount of formula the woman is requesting changes. The results of the assessment shall be documented in Notes in TGIF format, be used to provide individualized breastfeeding support, and to determine the appropriate food packages for her and her infant.

NOTE: When a breastfeeding woman who is more than 6 months postpartum stops breastfeeding, she becomes categorically ineligible. Postpartum Woman Postpartum non-breastfeeding women up to 6 months after the birth or the end of the pregnancy.

See below for more information on categorical eligibility for women who present after fetal or neonatal loss. Infant An infant until their 1st birthday (age one).

Child A child between the ages of one year and the last day of the month in which the child turns five (5) years old. NOTE: Participants shall be verbally informed of the length of certification at the time of certification. If the length of certification changes (i.e. change to estimated or actual delivery date) or if the category changes (i.e. breastfeeding category change), participants shall be verbally informed of the revised length of certification when it occurs.

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.004 - 2 III. Cases of Fetal or Neonatal Loss If a woman presents with a case of spontaneous abortion (miscarriage), induced abortion, fetal death or neonatal death, the applicant/participant may receive 6 months of food benefits from the date of loss. Definitions: • Fetal Death – Spontaneous termination of gestation at > 20 weeks • Induced Abortion – Elective termination of pregnancy • Neonatal Death – The death of an infant within 0-28 days of life • Spontaneous abortion – Spontaneous termination of a gestation at < 20 weeks, or a fetus that weighs < 500 grams Policies related to classifying women with fetal or neonatal loss as Postpartum Woman: • Proof of loss (i.e. doctors note) is preferable, and can be mandatory at the LA’s discretion. • A participant arriving to the LA post-loss may be recertified as a Postpartum Woman to receive benefits up to 6 months from the date of loss, as noted on proof of loss or as stated by the participant if no proof is available. • LAs reserve the right to refuse benefits and services to participants with suspected, or with a past history, of Program abuse. • If the participant was certified as pregnant without proof, and then returns to certify as post- loss, proof of either pregnancy or loss will be required. • Risk Code 321 shall be assigned to women who have had a spontaneous abortion, fetal death, or neonatal death. These participants are considered high-risk; refer to policy 8.007 for guidance on high-risk participants.

IV. Participants who misrepresent themselves as pregnant or postpartum

Policy 8.015 – Participant Violations and Sanctions indicates that misrepresenting oneself as pregnant and/or as having incurred the loss of a pregnancy (or infant) is considered a misrepresentation of health status - the participant could be sanctioned with having to repay the monetary value of benefits received and incur a one-year disqualification from Program eligibility.

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.004 - 3 Table 1. Summary of HANDS participant category codes Pt Code Description PG1 Pregnant woman < 18 years old

PG2 Pregnant woman > 18 years old

P Post Partum Woman

EN Woman Exclusively Nursing

IEN Infant Exclusively Nursing

IPN Infant Partially Nursing

IPN+ Infant Partially Nursing Plus (More formula provided than PN) IFF Infant Fully Formula Feeding

C1 Child 12-23 months old

C2

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.005 - 1 8.005 Residency Eligibility CFR 246.7 (C) Eligibility Criteria

I. Policy Statement At each certification appointment, each applicant is required to present proof of residency within the District of Columbia. This is the location or address where a potential participant routinely lives or spends the night. NOTE: Staff shall not make photocopies of an applicant’s proof of residency, nor scan residency documentation into HANDS. LAs shall not require an applicant to be a citizen or have residency status in the United States. LAs shall not attempt to determine an immigrant’s status or to confirm their status with the Immigration and Naturalization Service (INS). II. Acceptable Documents to Verify Residency Documentation of residency is required at each certification and when there is a change of address during a certification period. PO Boxes are not acceptable proof residency. The following documents may be used to verify an applicant’s residency within the District of Columbia. Address Confidentiality Program Income Tax Return / W-2 Rent or Mortgage Receipts (Housing) (From within 60 days) Bank Statements (From within 60 days) Letter from homeowner that person resides in their home (Issued within 60 days) Shelter Letter on Letterhead (Issued within 60 days) Bill (Utility, Cable, Phone, etc) (Issued within 60 days) Mail with postmark (no PO box) TANF/SNAP Award Letter Clinic / Hospital Record or ID Notice to Provider / CFSA Paperwork Vehicle Registration Driver’s License / Government or State issued ID Pay stubs with current address (Issued within 60 days) Voter Registration Card

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.005 - 2 III. Residency Considerations

a. DC Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

If the participant provides an ACP card for proof of residency, staff shall: - Document the new address as listed on the ACP card in the Mailing and Street Address fields in HANDS. If no address is listed, staff shall use the service site’s address - Select “Address Confidentiality Program” for Proof of Address - Verify phone number and request permission to contact them if necessary - If applicable, breast pump release forms (loan agreements) for a family will be completed using the ACP card address, or if applicable, the service site’s address

NOTE: Staff may not ask ACP participants to disclose their actual address

b. Institutional Residence If the participant resides in an institution (e.g., homeless shelter, shelter for victims of domestic violence, penal institution), the following conditions shall be met: - WIC foods benefit the participant, not the institution (i.e., the institution shall not accrue financial or in-kind benefit from the resident’s participation in WIC) - WIC foods are used by the WIC participant only - The institution allows and encourages the participant to purchase and consume WIC foods, and participate in all associated WIC services made available to participants by the Local Agency (e.g., education, referrals)

c. Non-Compliant Institutions If the institution where a participant is staying is found to be noncompliant with any of the above three conditions: - During the initial certification, the participant will continue to receive all WIC benefits - The participant applies for continuing benefits and still resides in the institution, the LA will discontinue provision of food items other than infant formula and the participant will continue to be eligible for WIC education and health care referrals - The LA will refer the participant to other accommodations, if possible - The State Agency will inform the institution of the required conditions listed above and that eligible residents will not be able to participate on WIC unless the conditions are met

d. Applicants with No Proof of Residency at Certification (Forgot Documentation) When an applicant has proof of residency but did not bring it to the certification appointment and is found eligible to receive benefits, they are to be informed that they can receive benefits for one month and will need to provide proof of residency before more benefits are issued. The applicant shall sign the “Forgot Documentation – ID/Address/Income” signature type accessible through the Family, Client, or Income screens. They are to be issued one month of food benefits and shall provide proof of residency within 30 days.

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.005 - 3 e. No Proof of Residency due to Theft, Loss, or Disaster When an applicant has no proof of residency as a result of being a victim of theft, loss, or disaster, the applicant shall sign the “No Proof Exists – ID/Address/Income” signature type found on the Family screen in HANDS. Staff will choose “No Proof Exists- ID/Address/Income” as the type of residency documentation. Staff may issue up to three months of Food Benefits. Note: Food benefits shall not be withheld for failure to provide updated proof of residency during a certification. f. Homeless Applicants/Participants For homeless applicants/participants, the address of a friend, relative, or homeless institution through which the applicant/ participant could be contacted shall be collected, if possible. If this is not possible, the word “HOMELESS” or the service site’s address shall be used. When an applicant has no proof of residency as a result of homelessness, the applicant shall sign the “No Proof Exists – ID/Address/Income” signature type found on the Family screen in HANDS, which will become a part of their permanent record. Staff will choose “No Proof Exists-ID/Address/Income” as the type of residency documentation. Staff may issue up to three months of food benefits. Note: Food benefits shall not be withheld for failure to provide updated proof of residency during a certification. g. Refugees In order to meet the WIC Program residency requirement, an applicant must live in the District of Columbia at the time of application. Refugees may not have a permanent place to live and, therefore, may be considered homeless. The applicant shall sign the “No Proof Exists – ID/Address/Income” signature type found on the Family screen in HANDS. Staff will choose “No Proof Exists-ID/Address/Income” as the type of residency documentation. Staff may issue up to three months of food benefits. h. Applicants with a Change of Address during a Certification If there is a change of address during a certification period and the participant does not have proof of the new address with them, staff shall enter the new address and select “Forgot Documentation” as the proof of residency. The participant shall sign the “Forgot Documentation – ID/Address/Income” signature type accessible through the Family, Client, or Income screens. Staff may issue up to three months of food benefits and have the participant provide proof at the next appointment. When proof of the new address is provided, staff shall update the proof of residency with the type of documentation provided. Note: Food benefits shall not be withheld for failure to provide updated proof of residency during a certification. IV. Procedures The following procedure shall be followed to determine and document residential eligibility: 1. Determine residential eligibility based on the above criteria 2. Record the type of documentation provided on the Family screen in the participant’s HANDS record

body:
VIII. Certification August 2021 8.006 - 1 8.006 Income Eligibility CFR § 246.7(d) Income Criteria and Income Eligibility Determinations SFP 02-080 WIC Income Eligibility Determining for Households Affected by Privatization of On-base Military Housing

I. Policy Statement The State Agency must establish income guidelines, definitions, and procedures for LAs to use when determining an applicant’s income eligibility. WIC applicants will have their income evaluated at each certification using procedures outlined in this policy.

The State Agency will adopt the income standard of 185% of the current Federal Poverty Guidelines as its eligibility standard. LAs will implement the federally-established income eligibility standards for their program (see Appendix 8.006A – Income Eligibility Guidelines).

All data used to determine income eligibility will be reflective of the applicant’s total household income and applicant’s status at the time of certification. All applicants will provide documentation of income through:

a. Proof of participation in an adjunctively eligible program, or b. Proof of income

II. Determining Household Size / Economic Unity Household/economic unit is defined as a group of related or non-related individuals who are living together as one economic unit.

Household/economic unit members share economic resources and consumption of goods and/or services. The terms “economic unit” or “household size” can be used interchangeably. However, “economic unit” is a more appropriate term to use because it conveys that familial relationship is not relevant to the determination of family size and income. The following are examples of how the economic unit discussion can be framed to gather more accurate information from the applicant:

• If the applicant(s) lives with their parent(s) or other family member(s) and they provide financial support such as food, bills, etc., include them in the household/economic unit. • If the applicant(s) lives with others who provide financial support such as food, bills, etc., include them in the household/economic unit. • If the applicant(s) lives with their boyfriend, girlfriend, fiancé, domestic partner, etc., and share any expenses, include him or her in the household/economic unit. Include opposite and same sex partners. • If the applicant(s) lives with their parents or other family member(s) and they do not provide financial support such as food, bills, etc., do not include them in the household/economic unit. • If the applicant(s) lives with others who do not provide financial support such as food, bills, etc., do not include them in the household/economic unit. • If the applicant(s) lives with their boyfriend, girlfriend, fiancé, domestic partner, etc. and do not share any expenses, do not include him or her in the household/economic unit. Include opposite and same sex partners.

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.006 - 2 III. Household/Economic Unit Considerations The following guidelines serve to direct LA staff on specific household/economic unit income circumstances. a. Adopted Child When a child has been adopted by a family, the child is counted in the household of the family. The size and total income of that economic unit will be used to determine if the child is income eligible for WIC. b. Foster Child If an infant or child is in the care of foster parents, the Child & Family Services Agency (CFSA), or other child welfare authorities, the infant or child will be considered a family of one; this income is to be documented in the Income screen in HANDS. The foster child will be the only family member selected to which the income will apply. If the foster child is the only participant in the file, the family size will be one. HANDS will automatically count the foster child as a family of one when the ‘Foster Care’ box is checked. The placement paper, commonly called “Notice to Provider,” or an official notification of placement from a temporary adoption organization is required to make the foster parents the Authorized Representatives. The payments made by the welfare agency or received from other sources for the care of that child will be considered to be the only income. This documentation can be scanned and saved in the participant’s file for future reference. If a foster parent has not yet received payments from the welfare agency or from other sources for the care of the child, staff shall document $1 as the income amount for that child and create a Staff Alert in the Notes screen to have WIC staff ask about changes in income at each recurring appointment, or until it is determined that no income will ever be received on behalf of the foster child. NOTE: If the foster child is a member of a WIC family with other non-foster children, the family size for the non-foster children applying for WIC will be the actual size of the AR’s family minus the foster child. HANDS will automatically count the foster child as a family of one when the ‘Foster Care’ box on the Client screen is checked, regardless of number in the Family Size field.

NOTE: Families with multiple foster children can share a Family ID number and eWIC card in HANDS. Each foster child will have a separate income documented in the Income screen as a household size of one. If the foster parent prefers, each foster child can be divided into separate family files and have individual eWIC cards issued. See Policy 9.001 for additional details.

c. Military Families Military personnel serving overseas or assigned to a military base, even though they are not living with their families, shall be considered members of the economic unit. Military dependents (i.e., infant, child, or woman) placed in the temporary care of friends or relatives who are dependent on that household to provide food, utilities, etc., shall be considered a part of that household/economic unit during certification. If the applicant receives funds to sustain themselves (beyond in-kind housing), they may be counted as a separate economic unit. When military personnel use alternative methods of depositing paychecks (waiving military income documentation) and/or receive combat/hazardous duty pay, the income over the last 12 months can be used. NOTE: Basic Allowance for Housing (BAH) is not considered income.

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.006 - 3 d. Pregnant Woman A pregnant woman’s household is assessed by increasing it by the number of expected infants (unless the applicant has religious or cultural objections which preclude this). e. Resident of Institutions The resident of an institution is assessed as a separate economic unit from the institution. The institution shall meet the conditions as outlined in the previous section on institutional residency. f. Co-living Two separate households/economic units residing at the same address under the same roof shall be considered separate households/economic units. Each household shall have an adequate source of income to cover expenses, such as rent, food, utilities, and other, to be determined as separate households/economic units. When unmarried individuals reside together as an economic unit, the income and household size of both parties shall be used in determining income eligibility. g. Separated Family When a family separates, the child is counted in the family with whom the child lives. h. Custody The parent(s) with whom the child spends a majority of their time can claim the child in reporting household size. Child support payments are considered income for the family with whom the child lives, but cannot be deducted from the income of the person making the payments. i. Teen An applicant who is under 18 years of age will have her income eligibility assessed following the rules which apply to any other economic unit (see Determining Household/Economic Unit above). j. In-stream Migrant Worker In-stream migrant farm workers with expired Verification of Certification (VOC) cards are income eligible as long as their income is determined at least once every 12 months. k. Refugees As part of the assessment process, LA staff will ask clarifying questions to determine the size of the economic unit for refugee applicants living in the residence of another individual. LAs shall require all applicants to provide documentation of income at the time of certification. If this requirement would present an unreasonable barrier to participation in the WIC Program, a self- declaration of income may be accepted. l. Qualified Aliens The LA shall not count the income of sponsors of qualified aliens (as the term is defined in the Immigration and Nationality Laws (8 U.S.C. 1101 et seq.) in determining the income eligibility of the qualified alien, except when the alien is a member of the sponsor’s family or economic unit. IV. Adjunctive Eligibility

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.006 - 4 When an applicant or a household family member participates in a federal or state program with eligibility guidelines that are equal to or below the WIC income guidelines, the applicant is allowed to enroll in the WIC Program without duplication of their initial income screening.

An applicant is adjunctively income eligible for WIC if documentation shows that the individual or an immediate household member is certified as fully eligible to receive benefits from:

- Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP/Food Stamps) - Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program - Medicaid (Pending adjunctive eligibility) o DC Medicaid Programs exist which apply higher income eligibility guidelines than allowed by WIC. DC WIC is working with the Department of Healthcare Finance (DCHF) to allow WIC clinic staff limited access to the DCHF eligibility system so they can verify the Medicaid beneficiaries’ household income. An applicant is automatically eligible for WIC if documentation shows that the individual or an immediate household family member is certified as fully eligible to receive benefits from:

- The National School Lunch Program (NSLP)

Documentation of Adjunctive Eligibility Applicants determined to be adjunctively or automatically income eligible are required to provide documentation of their participation in one or more of the programs listed above. The Adjunct Eligibility table in HANDS can only be updated on the date of certification. Acceptable forms of adjunctive eligibility documentation (which must include eligibility dates) are: o TANF approval letter o SNAP (Food Stamps) – most recent certification letter o Medicaid (pending adjunctive eligibility, may not be used until further notice) o NSLP – most recent certification letter

NOTE: TANF/SNAP cards are not proof of adjunctive program participation unless the card shows a current period of eligibility.

Procedure to Document Adjunct Eligibility: 1. Open the Adjunct Eligibility screen under the Income screen in HANDS 2. Select “Part. Proof” for each of the adjunct eligibility programs the applicant shows proof of participation in 3. If they show documentation that a member of their household is a TANF recipient, select “Fam Elig Proof” for those programs

NOTE: Documentation showing proof of participation in adjunctive eligibility programs may be used within 30 days as documentation of income. In addition, self-declaration is not allowed for adjunctive eligibility.

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.006 - 5 V. Reportable Income Types Income for the purposes of this part means gross cash income before deductions for income taxes, employees' social security taxes, insurance premiums, bonds, etc. LA staff shall consider all of the following to determine reportable income: a. Monetary compensation for services, including wages, salary, commissions, or fees b. Net income from farm and non-farm self-employment c. Social Security benefits d. Dividends or interest on savings or bonds, income from estates or trusts, or rental income e. Public assistance or TANF / welfare payments f. Unemployment compensation g. Government civilian employee or military retirement or pensions or veterans’ payments h. Private pensions or annuities i. Alimony or child support payments j. Regular contributions from persons not living in the household k. Net royalties l. Other cash income – includes, but is not limited to, cash amounts received or withdrawn from any source including savings, investments, trust accounts, and other resources which are readily available to the family

VI. Documentation of Income Acceptable types of documentation of income include, but are not limited to: Employment pay stubs (Issued within 30 days) Alimony or child support award letter Tax reporting forms showing total gross income Income tax return/W-2 forms Foster care placement letter Retirement pension letter/stub

Unemployment letter/notice Social Security benefits letter

Contribution letter

Statement signed and dated by employer Military pay stubs/LES

Adjunct Eligibility Program enrollment notification Note: staff shall not make photocopies or scan applicant’s proof of income.

Documentation Procedure Staff shall document income eligibility in the Income screen in HANDS as follows:

1. Enter the appropriate family size (economic unit) 2. Enter name or source of income provider if desired, or leave default as “Primary Provider” 3. Enter the dollar amount of current gross income based on income documentation provided 4. Enter the interval for that amount of income (i.e., hourly, weekly, monthly, annually) 5. If hourly is selected, enter the number of hours per week 6. Enter correct type of income documentation from drop-down menu 7. If income proof is brought in, select all family members to which the income applies, regardless of whether they are being certified today 8. If the AR forgot to bring income proof to certification, “Forgot Documentation” is to be selected and staff shall only apply income to the applicant(s) being certified today

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.006 - 6 NOTE: Do not apply income to a participant who has less than 90 days left in their certification period, unless they are being recertified.

If applicant presents multiples of the same income documentation type (e.g., employment pay stubs), staff shall utilize the “Income Averaging” feature on the Income Screen in HANDS. VII. Applicants with No Proof of Income If an applicant does not provide proof of income on the day of certification because they forgot it, the applicant is to self-declare their current income amount and corresponding interval; the applicant will be certified and receive only one month of food benefits if they are within income guidelines. They will be instructed to provide proof of income to the service site within the next 30 days. This will be documented in the Income screen in HANDS by selecting “Forgot Documentation” from the drop-down menu as the type of income documentation. The participant will then sign the “Forgot Documentation- ID/Address/Income” signature type accessible from the Family, Client, or Income screen.

If the applicant provides proof of income within 30 days, WIC staff will verify the amount and update the documentation type by editing the income line in the Income screen in HANDS and may issue multiple months of food benefits. VIII. Exceptions Lack of income documentation cannot be a barrier to receiving WIC services, such as in the case of the homeless, migrant farm workers, or people who work for cash. If the applicant cannot provide documentation of income, the applicant shall sign the “No Proof Exists-ID/address/income” signature type accessible from the Income screen. This signature serves as income documentation for the entire certification period and will allow more than one month of food benefits to be issued. This will be recorded in HANDS under the documentation type by selecting “No Proof Exists/Zero Income Signature Form” from the drop-down menu. IX. Zero Income If an applicant reports zero income or declares no income exists, the applicant shall be asked to describe, in detail, their living circumstances and how they obtain basic living necessities such as food, shelter, medical care, and clothing to determine if they shall be counted as part of a larger economic unit. If it is determined that the applicant is truly without resources, the applicant shall sign the “Zero Income” signature type accessible from the Income screen. This will be recorded in HANDS under the documentation type by selecting “No Proof Exists/Zero Income Signature Form” from the drop-down menu. X. Migrant Farm Workers Determination of income eligibility will be made once every 12 months for migrant field workers and their families. The migrant status will be documented in HANDS, indicating exemption from having income determination repeated within a 12-month period.

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.006 - 7 XI. Reassessment of Income The participant’s income eligibility during a current certification shall be reassessed if: • The Program receives information indicating the individual may have misrepresented income and/or household size when applying for services • The Program receives new information indicating the participant’s income has changed • The participant reports a change in income or household size, while in an active certification • The LA receives information that the participant(s) is no longer adjunctively eligible • The LA receives information that there is a change in custody which results in change of income or household size If the reassessment indicates the family is over income and has > 90 days remaining in their certification period, they are to be provided one month of food benefits, and provided a Notification of Ineligibility. Refer to Policy 8.014 or additional information about the Notification of Ineligibility. If there are < 90 days before the certification period expires, WIC staff shall issue the remaining food benefits through the end of the certification. NOTE: When a participant is in a current certification and there is reason to suspect that they have provided false information, the LA shall report the concern to the State Agency Nutrition Services team for further investigation. Reassessment of Income During an Existing Certification and Adding New Family Members When a new family member is certified while there are existing certifications for other members within the household, the proof of income shall be applied to all participants within the household unless the participant has < 90 days remaining in the certification. Refer to” Reassessment of Income” section above if the family has > 90 days remaining in their certification period. No Longer Adjunctively Eligible During a Certification Period A reassessment may identify that a participant/household is no longer adjunctively eligible. However, such persons cannot be disqualified from WIC solely on the basis of cessation of benefits from TANF, SNAP, or other State-administered programs. They will be reassessed under other income criteria before being disqualified. XII. Household Income Ineligible Termination If a LA evaluates income for another member of the participant’s household, and the evaluation indicates that household income is above the income guidelines, all members of the household shall be terminated from WIC services to include participants in a current certification (refer to Reassessment of Income section). The participants in a current certification are eligible for one month of food benefits. The applicants are not eligible for food benefits. All participants and applicants in the family will be provided with a Notification of Ineligibility and informed of their right to a fair hearing. NOTE: If a participant’s current certification period has < 90 days before it expires, they shall not be terminated and may receive their remaining food benefits until their certification expires.

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.006 - 8 XIII. Non-Eligible Income Sources The following sources of income must be excluded when determining income eligibility: a. Basic Allowance for Housing (BAH) received by military services personnel residing on or off of military installations b. Cost-of-living allowance provided under 37 U.S.C. 405, to a member of a uniformed service who is on duty outside the contiguous states of the United States c. The value of in-kind housing and other in-kind benefits d. Payments or benefits provided under certain Federal programs or acts, including (but not limited to): i. Reimbursements from the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970 ii. Any payment to volunteer under Title I (VISTA and others) and Title II (RSVP, foster grandparents, and others) of the Domestic Volunteer Service Act of 1973 to the extent excluded by that Act iii. Payment to volunteers under section 8(b)(1)(B) of the Small Business Act iv. Income derived from certain sub-marginal land of the United States that is held in trust for certain Indian tribes v. Payments received under the Job Training Partnership Act vi. Income derived from the disposition of funds to the Grand River Band of Ottawa Indians vii. Payments received under the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act viii. The value of assistance to children or their families under the National School Lunch Act, as amended, the Child Nutrition Act of 1966, and the Food Stamp Act of 1977 ix. Payments by the Indian Claims Commission to the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakima Indian Nation or the Apache Tribe of the Mescalero Reservation x. Payments to the Passamaquoddy Tribe and the Penobscot Nation or any of their members received pursuant to the Maine Indian Claims Settlement Act of 1980 xi. Payments under the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Act, as amended xii. Student financial assistance received from any program funded in whole or part under Title IV of the Higher Education Act of 1965, including the Pell Grant, Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant, State Student Incentive Grants, National Direct Student Loan, PLUS, College Work Study, and Byrd Honor Scholarship programs that is used for costs described in section 472 (1) and (2) of that Act xiii. Payments under the Disaster Relief Act of 1974 as amended by the Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Amendments of 1989 xiv. Effective July 1, 1991, payments received under the Carl D. Perkins Vocational Education Act, as amended by the Carl D. Perkins Vocational and Applied Technology Education Act Amendments of 1990 xv. Payments pursuant to the Agency Orange Compensation Exclusion Act xvi. Payments received for Wartime Relocation of Civilians under the Civil Liberties Act of 1988 xvii. Value of any childcare payments made under section 402(g)(1)(E) of the Social Security Act, as amended by the Family Support Act

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.006 - 9 xviii. Value of any “at-risk” block grant childcare payments made under section 508 of Pub. L. 101-508, which amended section 402(i) of the Social Security Act xix. Value of any childcare provided or paid for under the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act, as amended xx. Mandatory salary reduction amount for military service personnel that is used to fund the Veteran’s Educational Assistance Act of 1984 as amended xxi. Payments received under the Old Age Assistance Claims Settlement Act, except for per capita shares in excess of $2,000 xxii. Payments received under the Cranston-Gonzales National Affordable Housing Act, unless the income of the family equals or exceeds 80 percent of the median income of the area xxiii. Payments received under the Housing and Community Development Act of 1987, unless the income of the family increases at any time to not less than 50 percent of the median income of the area xxiv. Payments received under the Sac and Fox Indian claims agreement xxv. Payments received under the Judgment Award Authorization Act, as amended xxvi. Payments for relocation assistance of members of Navajo and Hopi Tribes xxvii. Payments to the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewas, Arizona xxviii. Payments to the Blackfeet, Grosventre, and Assiniboine tribes (Montana) and the Papago (Arizona) xxix. Payments to the Assiniboine Tribe of the Fort Belknap Indian community and the Assiniboine Tribe of the Fort Peck Indian Reservation (Montana) xxx. Payments to the Red Lake Bank of Chippewas xxxi. Payments received under the Saginaw Chippewa Indian Tribe of Michigan Distribution of Judgment Funds Act xxxii. Payments to the Chippewas of Mississippi xxxiii. Military Combat Pay is excluded when it is considered income as a result of deployment to a combat zone under FDPIR (FD-042: Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations- Pay Received by Military Personnel as Result of Deployment to a Combat Zone. Combat pay is excluded if it is: 1. Received in addition to the service member’s basic pay, 2. Received as a result of deployment to or service in an area designated as a combat zone, and 3. Not received prior to the service member’s deployment

body:
VIII. Certification August 2021 8.007 - 1 8.007 Risk Code Identification CFR § 246.7 (e) and WIC Policy Memorandum May 2011, Transmittal of New and Revised Nutrition Risk Criteria I. Policy Statement DC WIC has adopted the risk criteria developed by the Risk Identification and Selections Collaborative (RISC) Committee for the National WIC Association (NWA) and the Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) divisions of the USDA. DC WIC implements the Nutrition Risk Criteria located on the Local Agencies > Trainings page at www.dcwic.org. Applicants will be assigned all risk codes that apply, according to HANDS and the Nutrition Risk Manual. To ensure participant-centered education, it is highly recommended for staff NOT to tell participants their risk(s) directly; instead, it is preferred for staff to offer nutrition education topics related to the risk(s). II. Staff Responsible for Determining Nutrition Risk LA Staff responsible for determining nutrition risk include: a. Competent Professional Authorities (CPAs) – may determine risk, provide nutrition education, and prescribe supplemental foods for all participants; must counsel participants indicated as high-risk. b. Competent Para-Professional Authorities (CPPAS) – may determine risk, provide nutrition education, and issue supplemental foods to low-risk participants. If a CPPA identifies a participant as high-risk during any part of the health and nutrition assessment, they must refer the participant to the CPA for follow-up.

III. Procedures for Determining Nutrition Risk The Nutrition Risk Manual (NRM), located on www.dcwic.org under Local Agencies > Trainings, is a comprehensive guide to each nutrition risk code. LA staff may refer to this manual online, or may print it for on-site reference if desired. In addition to the NRM, which is over 350 pages, there are “cheat sheets” for LA staff to use with the expectation that staff are familiar with risk code indications. If staff have questions related to risk code descriptions or indications, they should refer to the NRM and to their Local Agency Director, as needed. The CPA shall use the “CPA Risk Codes Cheat Sheet (Appendix 8.007A) for determining nutritional/medical risk for program eligibility. The CPPA shall use the “CPPA Risk Codes” (see Appendix 8.007B) for determining nutritional/medical risks for program eligibility. NOTE: Risk codes are not final in the participant’s record until they clicks “Complete Assessment” in the Nutrition Care Plan screen. Risk codes can be added at any time throughout the certification as they are identified as HANDS will capture the date the risk was added to the record.

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.007 - 2 IV. Self-Reporting or Self- Diagnosis Self-reporting of a diagnosis by a medical professional shall not be confused with self-diagnosis, where a person reports to have or have had a medical condition, without any reference to a professional diagnosis. A self-reported medical diagnosis such as, “My doctor says that I have/my son or daughter has…” shall prompt the CPA to validate the presence of the condition by asking more in-depth questions related to the diagnosis. Self-reporting of “History of” conditions shall be handled in the same manner as self-reporting of current conditions that require a physician’s diagnosis. The applicant may report to the CPA that they were diagnosed by a physician with a given condition in the past. Again, self-diagnosis of a past condition shall not be confused with self-reporting. V. Determining Nutrition Risk The participant’s health and nutrition assessment, including collection of anthropometric and biochemical data, identifies the nutritional needs and interests of the participant. The nutrition assessment provides the basis for the nutrition care plan, including nutrition education/counseling, food package assignment, referrals, and follow-up plans. During the assessment process, heights, weights, biochemical information, dietary information, medical information, and family situation are assessed and any potential risk codes are identified. Individuals applying for enrollment in DC WIC must have at least one risk code to be eligible for participation. Women’s Nutrition Risk Determination: All data used to determine nutritional risk will be reflective of the woman’s categorical status at the time of certification. For example, a woman certified during pregnancy as at risk for anemia cannot be certified in the postpartum period using any hemoglobin or hematocrit value that was obtained during her pregnancy.
