body:
VIII. Certification August 2021 8.008 - 1 8.008 Eligibility for Special Cases CFR § 246.7(c) Eligibility Criteria and Basic Certification Procedure I. Policy Statement The State Agency must have a plan to provide Program benefits to unserved infants and children under the care of foster parents, protective services, or child welfare authorities, including infants exposed to drugs perinatally. Infants and children living with temporary caretakers, and minors (under age 18) seeking WIC services and benefits are also covered in this policy. II. Children in Foster Care or Protective Services Local Agencies shall provide WIC benefits to children in foster care or protective services who meet the eligibility criteria for the Program. The foster parent(s) with whom the child is placed must reside in the District of Columbia. The LA shall accept only official documents from the Department of Human Services, the Child and Family Services Agency, or other appropriate agency indicating that the child has been placed in their care. The child’s monthly foster care stipend shall be used to determine income eligibility, not that of the foster parent(s). The child shall be considered a “family of one.” The foster care or protective services parent(s) shall be the AR(s) for the child participant, with all the rights and responsibilities assigned to that position. Children in foster care who are residents of the District of Columbia, but have been placed in homes in Maryland, Virginia, or another state must apply for WIC benefits in that state. Children in foster care who are residents of the District of Columbia and live in Maryland or Virginia, but receive primary health care in the District of Columbia may be served by DC WIC.

a. A letter from the participant’s doctor must be sent to the designated clinic prior to the delivery of WIC services.

Note: For changes in custody that take place during a valid certification period, see policy 8.012– Authorized Representatives.

LA Staff shall contact the State Agency for guidance in cases where custody is questioned or challenged by a biological parent. Procedures: 1. Use the child’s monthly foster care stipend to determine income eligibility – see policy 8.006 for more information 2. Verify and document the foster parent’s identity and residency

III. Legal Guardians LAs shall provide WIC benefits to children who reside with a legal guardian other than the parent and meet the eligibility criteria for the Program. The legal guardian with whom the child lives must reside in the District of Columbia and provide proof of residency. The legal guardian must prove that the child resides with them. This documentation must be a notarized statement from the court or an attorney, and must be scanned into the participant’s HANDS record at the time of certification.

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.008 - 2 The child’s income shall be used to determine income eligibility, not that of the legal guardian. The child shall be considered a “family of one.” The legal guardian shall be the AR for the child participant, with all the rights and responsibilities assigned to that position. Note: For changes in custody that take place during a valid certification period, see policy 8.012 – Authorized Representatives. LA staff shall contact the State Agency for guidance in cases where custody is questioned or challenged by a biological parent.

Procedures: 1. Use the child’s sources of income to determine income eligibility 2. Verify and document the legal guardian’s identity, residency, and custody 3. Scan the legal guardian’s custody documentation into the child’s HANDS record IV. Temporary Caretaker LAs shall make every effort to provide WIC benefits to children who reside with a temporary caretaker and meet the eligibility criteria for the Program. The temporary caretaker must provide documentation indicating that they are providing for the child due to the parent or legal guardian not being able to care for the child, and that the child is residing with the caretaker. Documentation must indicate the length of this arrangement and be one of the following: a. Notarized statement from the child’s parent; OR b. Proof of a child’s Medicaid, TANF, or SNAP benefits mailed in care of the caretaker; OR c. Written statement from a social service or health care agency to include (1) the name and address of the child, (2) the name, address, and telephone number of the caretaker, and (3) the length of time that the child will be in the care of the caretaker The temporary caretaker with whom the child lives must reside in the District of Columbia and provide proof of residency. This child is not considered a foster child and shall be included in the family’s eligibility determination. One month of food benefits shall be issued and eligibility shall be reassessed at the next appointment. The temporary caretaker shall be the AR for the child participant, with all the rights and responsibilities assigned to that position. LA staff shall contact the State Agency for guidance in cases where custody is questioned or challenged by a biological parent. Procedures 1. Obtain documentation that the temporary caretaker has legal custody of the child 2. Verify the identity and residency of the temporary caretaker 3. Use the child’s source(s) of income to determine income eligibility

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.008 - 3 4. Scan the temporary caretaker’s documentation of custody into the child’s HANDS record Note: If the temporary caretaker does not have documentation that the infant/child has been knowingly and willingly placed in their care by the court or the child’s parent/legal guardian, staff may issue 1- month (30 days) of benefits. In this case, the temporary caretaker must sign the “Self-Declaration of Relationship to Minor” form and must provide appropriate documentation of custody – either legal custody or temporary custody - within 30 days, at which point the full certification can be completed and additional benefits issued. Add a staff alert in the participant’s HANDS record that documentation of guardianship is needed. “Self-Declaration of Relationship to Minor” forms must be scanned into the infant/child’s HANDS record. Note: For changes in custody that take place during a valid certification period, see policy 8.012 – Authorized Representatives.

V. Ward of the District of Columbia LAs shall provide WIC benefits to children who are “Wards of the District of Columbia” and reside in DC. In situations where children in the DC foster care program are placed in homes in Maryland or Virginia, but receive primary health care in the District of Columbia they may be served by DC WIC. A letter from the participant’s doctor must be sent to the designated service site prior to delivery of WIC services. The same procedure for shall be followed for “Wards of the District of Columbia” as stated in section II of this Policy (Foster Children). VI. Minors LAs shall provide WIC benefits to applicants who are minors and meet the eligibility criteria. A minor who is not receiving support from their family shall be considered a separate economic if they can provide documentation of majority of financial support for himself/herself. A minor would be considered an "Emancipated minor" which is defined as any minor who is living separate and apart from their parent(s) or legal guardian, with or without the consent of the parent(s) or legal guardian and regardless of the duration of such separate residence, and who is managing his or her own personal and financial affairs, regardless of the source or extent of their income. A minor shall be considered part of an economic unit other than their parent(s) if he/she shares income, and goods and services generated by that income with those persons. LA Staff shall accept the standard proof of eligibility criteria, including exceptions for assessment of minors. Contact the State Agency for guidance if there are questions concerning eligibility for WIC for an emancipated minor.

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.008 - 4 VII. Military Temporary Care of Friends/Relatives LAs shall provide WIC benefits to children in temporary care of friends and/or relatives due to military obligations of their parent(s). The child’s income shall be calculated based on the economic unit. The economic unit shall be determined by using one of the following: a. The child and their military parent(s) may be considered an economic unit and the gross pay of the parent(s) therefore determines the income. The caretaker must provide adequate documentation that the parent(s) is sending money to support the child(ren) and that this support is sufficient to provide for the majority of support. b. The child(ren) may be considered as a separate economic unit if the child’s source of income provides the majority of support and it is adequate to sustain them as a separate economic unit. LA Staff shall use the monetary guidelines of the Department of Human Services Foster Care Program to determine the adequacy of the child’s income. c. The child(ren) may be considered as part of the economic unit of the temporary caretaker with whom they reside - the gross pay of the temporary caretaker therefore determines the income. Staff shall consider all sources of income for military families, except those excluded in Policy 8.006. The LA shall accept standard proof of income documentation, including exceptions, for military families listed in Policy 8.006. LAs shall consider the past 12 months of income for a military family whose income temporarily increases due to short-term hazardous duty, combat or other temporary situations. The current rate of income shall be considered when a military family’s income decreases due to a temporary situation. Military families are eligible for DC WIC if they physically live in the District of Columbia, but do not have to be residents of the District of Columbia.

VIII. Certification August 2021 8.008 - 5 Table 1. Summary of Special Cases Documentation and Certification Lengths Situation Documentation Required Certification Length No documentation of legal guardianship / temporary placement Signed “Self-Declaration of Relationship to Minor” form 30 days AR must follow up with appropriate documentation of legal guardianship or temporary custody Legal Guardian Notarized statement from court or attorney Full certification Temporary Caretaker Notarized statement from court or legal guardian; OR Proof of a child’s Medicaid, TANF, or SNAP benefits mailed in care of the caretaker Full Certification

Written statement from a social service or health care agency to include: 1. Child’s name and address 2. Caretaker’s name, address, phone number 3. Length of time the child will be in the care of the caretaker This can include “Safety Plans” from CFSA, provided the above information is included. The length of the caretaker’s arrangement, at which point the caretaker can provide documentation of extension or change in status to legal guardian, or the new guardian will need to provide their information and appropriate documentation. Foster Care or Protective Services Paperwork from appropriate Government agency. Full certification Ward of the District Paperwork from appropriate Government agency. Letter from child’s healthcare provider if guardians live outside DC. Full certification Note: See policy 8.012 – Authorized Representatives, for procedures on updating an infant or child’s primary AR during a certification period, in cases when there is a change of legal guardianship or custody.

body:
VIII. Certification September 2021 8.009 - 1 8.009 Certification of Homeless, Migrants, Refugees CFR § 246.7(n) Certification of persons in homeless facilities and institutions I. Policy Statement Pregnant, breastfeeding and postpartum women, infants and children who meet WIC eligibility criteria and who live in a homeless facility, shelter, or institution shall be considered eligible for the WIC Program and shall be treated equally with all other eligible applicants at the local agency where they apply for WIC benefits. Refugees without residence and income may be certified along the guidelines for certifying homeless applicants, including refugees residing with sponsors as long as the sponsor is not providing the refugee with financial support. II. Procedures Regarding Facilities, Shelters, or Institutions that House WIC Participants

A. LAs shall take reasonable steps to:

• Establish to the extent practicable that the facility, shelter, or institution meets the following conditions with respect to resident WIC participants: i. The facility, shelter, or institution does not accrue financial or in-kind benefit from a person’s participation in the Program ii. Foods provided by the WIC Program are not included in a communal food service, but are available exclusively to the WIC participant for whom they were issued iii. The facility, shelter, or institution places no constraints on the ability of the participant to partake of the supplemental foods and nutrition education made available by the Program • Contact the facility, shelter, or institution periodically to ensure continued compliance with these conditions • Request the facility, shelter, or institution to notify the State or Local Agency if it ceases to meet any of these conditions B. LA staff shall inform participants who reside in facilities, shelters, or institutions that WIC food:

• Must only be consumed by the participant; • Must not be used by any other residents, and • Must not be stored in the facility or institution’s general storage area

C. LAs shall attempt to establish, to the best of its ability, whether a facility, shelter, or institution complies with the conditions set forth above with respect to the WIC participants.

D. If a homeless facility or institution has been determined to be non-compliant during the course of a participant’s initial certification period, participants applying for continued benefits may be certified again but LA staff shall not issue WIC food benefits except infant formula until the accommodation’s compliance is achieved or alternative shelter arrangements are made. If certified, such participants

VIII. Certification September 2021 8.009 - 2 shall continue to be eligible to receive all other WIC benefits, such as nutrition education and health care referral services.

E. Upon determination that a facility, shelter, or institution does not meet the conditions set forth above, LA staff shall refer all participants using such accommodation to any other accommodations in the area which meet these conditions.

F. The State Agency will notify LAs if it becomes aware that a facility, shelter, or institution does not comply with the conditions set forth above.

G. Correspondence from a facility, shelter, or institution shall be accepted as proof of residency.

H. LA Staff shall use the HANDS codes “does not exist” for proof of residency, identification, and/or if the homeless, migrant or refugee applicant cannot produce documentation. See policies 8.002 to 8.007 for more information on intake documentation.

I. LA Staff are not required to document a nutritional risk for homeless, migrant, or refugee applicants other than the risk code for homelessness (801).

J. LA Staff shall consider the cooking and storage capabilities of facilities, shelters, or institutions when prescribing supplemental foods and may tailor the food prescription as needed. K. LA staff must instruct the AR(s) of infants residing in facilities, shelters, or institutions regarding sanitary procedures to use in formula preparation and storage.

body:
DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.010 1 | P a g e Title: Anthropometric and Biochemical Data Collection Category: Certification CFR Reference: 7 CFR 246.7 Policy Number 8.010 Effective Date: December 1st 2021 Revised Date: April 30th 2024

POLICY STATEMENT: Anthropometric and Biochemical Collection Height, weight, and hemoglobin measurements must be performed and/or documented in the applicant’s record at the time of certification in accordance with 7 CFR 246.7(e)(1)(i)(A). Additional anthropometric and hemoglobin screening may be required depending on the participant’s category, certification length and/or nutritional risk. See Procedures section below for assessment frequency. Data submitted by a healthcare provider may be used to establish nutritional risk but must have been taken within the last 60 days for anthropometric data or last 90 days for blood work data. Hemoglobin screening may be deferred at the time of certification only if another qualifying nutritional risk is identified (see DC WIC Nutritional Risk Manual) and the participant or Authorized Representative (AR) agrees to submit the results of an outside blood test performed within 90 days of the certification. For women participants, the anthropometric and hemoglobin measurements must be reflective of her status (i.e., pregnant women must have their data taken during pregnancy; postpartum women must have data taken following the termination of pregnancy). Acceptable forms of anthropometric and biochemical documentation include: • Medical provider’s prescription form • Medical provider’s letterhead with measurements • DC WIC Medical Prescription Form • Medical records that include the date of measurements and the provider’s name • Verbal measurements from a medical provider The Local Agency staff must include the name of the provider organization in which the anthropometric and/or biochemical data was obtained in the “I” portion of the TGIF note. Blood Lead Screening and Referral Local Agency staff are to screen for blood lead testing for all participants at the time of certification. If the blood lead value is known, this value is to be documented in the participant’s record as part of the TGIF note. If the blood lead value is unknown or if a blood lead test has not yet been performed for a child participant, then a referral to the participant’s healthcare provider must be made in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.018 Referrals Overview.

Risk code 211 Elevated Blood Lead should be assigned if the blood lead value is higher than established cut-offs (see DC WIC Nutrition Risk Manual for more details).

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.010 2 | P a g e Clinic Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) Certificate A current CLIA certificate must be posted in each WIC clinic where hemoglobin assessments are performed. For WIC clinics with more than one lab, only one CLIA certificate needs to be posted. WIC clinic sites must have one of two types of CLIA certificates posted in laboratory space where hemoglobin screening is performed. The Local Agency should obtain a copy of the certificate from DC Health or the Local Agency’s lab director. Visit https://www.cms.gov/regulations-and-guidance/legislation/clia?redirect=/clia/ for more information on CLIA certificates and waivers. PROCEDURE Medical Consent Before taking anthropometric measurements and/or conducting a hemoglobin screening, the Local Agency staff member must inform the participant or AR the reason for performing these actions and obtain consent. The Local Agency staff member will collect the participant or AR’s signature under “Consent” on the Medical Screen in HANDS. If a participant or AR does not consent to the anthropometric collection or hemoglobin screening, then the Local Agency staff must request that these measurements be provided in accordance with this policy, or the participant may risk a delay in receiving WIC services. Anthropometric Collection Refer to the DC WIC Anthropometrics Manual for performing and collecting anthropometric measurements. All infant, children, and breastfeeding women must have height and weight measurements collected at certification and mid-certification appointments (approximately six months from the certification date) unless one of the exception criteria is met in DC WIC policy 8.003 Physical Presence. Biochemical Data Collection Refer to the DC WIC Lab Procedure Manual for performing hemoglobin testing for DC WIC participants. Frequency of Assessment Additional anthropometric and hemoglobin assessments are required at minimum based on the category and age of participant below (next page):

Biochemical Data Collection Chart Category Infant’s age at time of certification Frequency of hemoglobin testing Exceptions to Certification Blood Work Required

For all categories – at least one qualifying nutritional risk is present at certification and blood test result is obtained within 90 days of certification. Pregnant Women N/A One blood test per certification

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.010 3 | P a g e Postpartum Women 0-6 months *One blood test per certification, ideally between 4 to 6 weeks after end of pregnancy Breastfeeding Women 0 - 5 months One blood test per certification, ideally between 4 to 6 weeks after end of pregnancy

6 – 12 months No blood test required if a test was taken after end of pregnancy (documentation needed) Staff may accept a blood test result more than 60 days old (7 CFR 246.7(e)(1)(ii)(B)(3)). Infants 0-5 months Not required

6-8 months Not required at time of certification. The blood test may be performed after the infant is at least 9 months of age 9-11 months One blood test per certification

Children 12-24 months N/A Two blood tests needed by 24 months of age

If an infant blood test was performed, then only one additional blood test needed per certification

Children 24-60 months N/A At least one blood test per certification

Women less than 4 weeks postpartum Local Agency staff must use the pending lab code “LESS THAN 4 WEEKS POSTPARTUM” for women less than four weeks postpartum as HANDS does not allow a hemoglobin value to be entered at this time. The Local Agency may choose to perform the following: • Request the participant return between four to six weeks postpartum to have a hemoglobin test performed. • Request the participant submit hemoglobin test results obtained within 90 days of certification. • Perform the hemoglobin test at the time of certification and document this value in the participant’s TGIF note. Once the participant is more than four weeks postpartum, the Local Agency staff may enter this value into the participant’s Medical screen in HANDS using the date the test was initially performed.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.010 4 | P a g e Low Hemoglobin Readings If the hemoglobin reading is below 10.0 g/dL, the Local Agency staff must perform a subsequent hemoglobin test. The subsequent test must be performed at a different site, preferably with a finger on the other hand. The higher of the two hemoglobin values is entered into HANDS and should be used for referral purposes.

Frequency of Testing for Low Hemoglobin Results A hemoglobin reading at or below 7.0 g/dL requires an immediate referral to the CPA and for medical attention. The CPA must ensure appropriate nutrition education and referrals are provided to address the low hemoglobin reading and conduct a high-risk follow-up appointment for retesting of the hemoglobin value in accordance with 2.008 Serving High Risk Participants. Exemptions from Hemoglobin Testing Hemoglobin testing may be waived for a participant that has one of following: • Religious objection • Medical condition such as hemophilia, thalassemia, or sickle cell anemia • If performing the test will cause physical harm to the participant or staff member If a participant meets the exemption criteria, the CPA/CPPA must document this in the participant’s TGIF note in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.005 Nutrition Education Overview. Blood Work Data Not Received in 90 Days If a participant is not able to provide the required hematological data within 90 days of certification, the Local Agency must require the participant to come to the clinic to obtain this data unless the participant falls under the existing exemptions in DC WIC policy 8.003 Physical Presence and Identification.

The participant will not be terminated for failure to provide the hematological data within 90-day time frame, provided that the CPA/CPPA has identified a nutrition risk for eligibility, in accordance with FNS WIC Policy Memo 2001-2 WIC Bloodwork Requirements and DC WIC policy 8.001 Certification Overview. body:
VIII. Certification September 2021 8.011 - 1 8.011 Certification Risk Determination & Considerations CFR § 246.7(e)(1) and (g) Nutritional Risk and Certification Periods; CFR § 246.2 Definitions

This policy provides considerations and reminders for each category of applicable WIC participants. Please see the DC WIC Program Certification Map for a full description of each step in the certification process, including rationale for each of the requirements.

I. Road to Certification Step Description Part of the: Notes & Greeting Begins the applicant’s appointment Intake & Eligibility Screening Intake / Eligibility Collecting, determining, and documenting eligibility based on category, residency, and income A, B, C, & E Anthropometric, Biochemical, Clinical, and Environmental data gathering Health & Nutrition Assessment D Diet/nutrition data gathering

Nutrition Education & Goal Setting Providing participant centered nutrition education based on the Health and Nutrition Assessment VENA / Participant Centered Counseling Summarize / New Appt Closing out the Assessment and planning for the next visit Food Package Assigning, tailoring, and issuing the food package; Discussing where and how to use WIC benefits Food Benefits Delivery TGIF Documenting in the participant’s HANDS record

Closeout

VIII. Certification September 2021 8.011 - 2 II. Pregnant women (PG1/PG2) Intake & Eligibility Screening i. A pregnant woman does not have to prove she is pregnant. If the LA has good reason to suspect the applicant of fraud or abuse, or if the applicant has a history or fraud or abuse, the LA may refuse service to the applicant. ii. A pregnant woman’s household is assessed by increasing it by the number of expected infants (unless the applicant has religious or cultural objections which preclude this). iii. Pregnant applicants under the age of 18 years must be assessed for income eligibility using income information from their parent(s), guardian(s), or other household members that provide financial support to the applicant, if possible. Health & Nutrition Assessment iv. Anthropometric and biochemical assessments shall reflect the applicant’s current participant status (i.e., pregnant women should have height, weight, and hgb assessed while pregnant) v. Evaluate maternal weight status using the prenatal weight grid (see the DC WIC Anthropometrics Manual, or Table 1., below) a. Weight status assessment and weight gain recommendations for pregnant teenagers will be based on the IOM’s nutrition during pregnancy Body Mass Index (BMI) categories vi. Income-eligible pregnant women are presumed to be at nutritional risk and can be certified immediately to receive program benefits for 60 days if the initial certification does not include a health & nutrition assessment. However, the health & nutrition assessment must be performed within 60 days and include anthropometric and hematological data vii. A pregnant woman shall be considered at risk if she meets at least one risk code criterion described in Policy 8.007 – Determining Nutrition Risk. If no risk is found after a complete assessment has been performed (including risk #427 - Inappropriate Nutrition Practices for Women), risk #401 - Failure to Meet Dietary Guidelines for Americans, must be assigned. Participant Centered Counseling viii. Offer an appointment and/or class with a breastfeeding peer counselor ix. Consider the applicant’s due date when scheduling their next appointment(s) Food Benefits x. Women pregnant with multiples and Pregnant women who are also breastfeeding an infant from a previous pregnancy receive the “fully breastfeeding” food package.

Table 1. Prenatal Weight Gain Grid Pre-pregnancy BMI : Underweight (BMI <18) Normal Weight (BMI 18-25) Overweight (BMI 25-30) Obese (BMI >30) A woman pregnant with one baby should gain: 28-40 lb 25-35 lb 15-25 lb 11-20 lb A woman pregnant with twins should gain: 50-62 lb 37-54 lb 31-50 lb 25-42 lb Source: https://www.cdc.gov/reproductivehealth/maternalinfanthealth/pregnancy-weight-gain.htm

VIII. Certification September 2021 8.011 - 3 III. Breastfeeding Women (EN, PN, PN+) Intake & Eligibility Screening No special notes Health & Nutrition Assessment i. Anthropometric and hematological data submitted by a health care provider may be used to establish nutritional risk but must be taken during the postpartum period and within 60 days of the certification date. ii. A breastfeeding woman may be determined to be at nutritional risk if her breastfed infant has been determined to be at nutritional risk. Select the highest priority level for which a mother or infant is qualified for the mother-infant dyad. iii. If no risk is found after a complete assessment has been performed (including for risk #427 - Inappropriate Nutrition Practices for Women), risk #401 - Failure to Meet Dietary Guidelines for Americans, must be assigned. iv. A breastfeeding assessment shall be performed before the issuance of Food Benefits at every visit. The results of the assessment shall be used to provide individualized breastfeeding support and to determine the appropriate food package. v. Review breastfeeding notes, as well, and refer participants to BPCs as needed Food Benefits vi. Breastfeeding women are eligible for the “fully breastfeeding” food package or the “partially breastfeeding” food package depending on the number of daily breast milk feedings provided to the infant.

IV. Postpartum Women (P) Intake & Eligibility Screening i. A woman who would have been eligible for the Program during her pregnancy who has had an abortion, spontaneous (miscarriage) or therapeutic, can also apply for Food Benefits. She is eligible for a total of six (6) months of food benefits from the date the pregnancy ended. Health & Nutrition Assessment ii. Anthropometric and hematological data submitted by a health care provider may be used to establish nutritional risk but must be taken following termination of pregnancy and within 60 days of the certification date. iii. A postpartum woman shall be considered at nutritional risk if she meets at least one risk criterion described in Policy 8.007- Determining Nutrition Risk. If no risk is found after a complete assessment has been performed (including for risk #427 - Inappropriate Nutrition Practices for Women), risk #401 - Failure to Meet Dietary Guidelines for Americans, must be assigned. Food Package No special notes

VIII. Certification September 2021 8.011 - 4 V. Infants (IEN, IPN, IPN+, IFF) Intake & Eligibility Screening i. Infants < 6 months of age shall be certified until their first birthday. Infants 6 to 12 months of age are certified for a 6-month interval. ii. Hospitalized infants cannot receive WIC benefits until discharged. Health & Nutrition Assessment iv. Anthropometric data submitted by a health care provider may be used to establish nutritional risk, but must be taken within 60 days of the certification date. v. All infants > 9 months of age and older shall have a hematological screening performed between 9-12 months of age if not previously conducted. Results may be obtained from a referral source. This hematological screening does not have to occur within 90 days of the certification date. vi. If an infant does not receive hematological screening during the infant certification period, the screening performed for the first child certification may be used to satisfy the requirement but must be performed by the age of 15 months. When this substitution is used, the screening data cannot be counted for the child certification period. vii. A breastfed infant can be certified based on the mother’s health & nutrition assessment. Staff should assign a breastfeeding mother and her infant to the highest priority level for which either is qualified. viii. An infant < 6 months of age may be determined to be at nutritional risk if the infant’s mother was a WIC participant during pregnancy or if medical records document that the woman was at nutritional risk during pregnancy due to detrimental or abnormal nutritional conditions detectable by biochemical or anthropometric measurements or other documented nutritionally related medical conditions. ix. An infant shall be considered at-risk if they meet at least one of the risk codes described in Policy 8.007 Determining Nutrition Risk. If no risk can be identified following a complete assessment (including for risk #411 - Inappropriate Nutrition Practices for Infants), risk #428 - Dietary Risk Associated with Complementary Feeding Practices, must be assigned for infants 4-12 months old. The CPA/CPPA must identify which Complimentary Feeding Practices are of concern in the participant’s HANDS record. Food Benefits x. Infants may receive standard infant formula tailored to their level of breastfeeding. For more information on breastfeeding assessment, see policy 9.006 xi. All special formulas require a prescription – see policy 9.009 xii. Powder formula should be issued unless the infant or caregiver meets conditions listed in policy 9.009; when RTU formula is issued, the reason must be documented in HANDS. xiii. At 6 months of age, infants may begin to receive infant food fruits, vegetables, and cereal; infants who are fully breastfed may also receive infant food meats. xiv. Infants 9-11 months of age receive CVB dollars in lieu of ½ the benefit of infant food fruits and vegetables ($4 CVB for infants fed formula, $8 CVB for fully breastfed infants) Medical Updates Medical updates shall be scheduled ~ 6 months following the initial certification for an infant who was certified at < 6 months of age. Income and eligibility do not need to be assessed at this appointment, but a complete health & nutrition should be performed. If the infant is determined to be high-risk by a CPPA during this appointment, a follow-up by a CPA is necessary.

VIII. Certification September 2021 8.011 - 5 VI. Children (C1 – C4) Intake & Eligibility Screening i. For children who reside with someone other than their biological parent, see Policy 8.006 for information about income eligibility. The child may either be counted as a household of one (1) or be included in the household of the guardian (legal or temporary). ii. Children enrolled in Free and Reduced Meal programs, such as the National School Lunch Program, are considered adjunctively eligible. Health & Nutrition Assessment iii. Anthropometric and hematological data submitted by a health care provider may be used to establish nutritional risk, but must be taken within 60 days of the certification date. iv. Staff shall evaluate the growth grids available in HANDS during the health assessment v. A child shall be considered at nutritional risk if they meet at least one risk criterion described in Policy 8.007 Determining Nutritional Risk. vi. If no risk is found after a complete assessment, to include for risk #411 - Inappropriate Nutrition Practices for Infants and #425 - Inappropriate Nutrition Practices for Children, then one of the following risk codes must be assigned: a. Risk #428 - Dietary Risk Associated with Complementary Feeding Practices (age 1-2), or b. Risk #401 - Failure to Meet Dietary Guidelines for Americans (ages 2-5)

Food Benefits Delivery vii. Children 12-24 months: a. Receive whole milk and yogurt unless contraindicated by a CPA’s assessment b. May receive peanut butter – staff should discuss the signs of peanut allergy with caregivers viii. Children 2-5 years: a. Receive low-fat milk (1% or skim) and yogurt unless the CPA assessment indicates the need for 2% milk (no Rx needed) or whole milk (Rx from medical provider is needed)

body:
VIII. Certification December 2021 8.012 - 1

8.012 Authorized Representatives CFR § 246.7(j) Notification of participant rights and responsibilities; CFR § 246.12(r)(l) Parents/Caretakers and proxies I. Policy Statement

An Authorized Representative (AR) may apply for Program benefits for themselves or on behalf of an infant or child applicant. The AR is considered the primary person responsible for the participant enrolled in the Program. Adult participants are usually their own AR, but for infants and children the AR can be one of the following: • Parent • Caretaker • Legal guardian • Relative with whom the participant lives • Spouse or significant other • Individual who has significant knowledge of family history of the participant

The primary AR has the right to identify an Alternative Authorized Representative (AAR) during any point while in a valid certification but is not required to designate one. Both the AR and AAR shall have access to the family’s WIC records. In order to have rights and access to the family’s WIC records, an individual shall be recorded as an AAR in participant’s HANDS record.

ARs and AARs shall be instructed on the Rules and Regulations of the WIC Program, including how to use WIC Food Benefits. Refer to Policy Section IX – Food Benefits, for additional details.

The designated AR, and AAR if applicable, is required to sign the “WIC Rights and Obligations” signature type in HANDS. II. Procedures for Naming Authorized Representatives

A. If two ARs are present at certification: • Request identification from both Representatives and enter their names into HANDS on the Family screen, including what proof of ID was seen • “Rights & Obligations” signature type in HANDS shall be signed by one or both Authorized Representatives • Explain the WIC Rules and Regulations to the Authorized Representatives, including WIC-eligible foods and how to use the eWIC card to redeem Food Benefits. Staff shall ask questions to verify the AR’s understanding of how to use the eWIC card.

B. If the AR names an AAR who is not present: • Staff will add the first and last names of the AAR in the appropriate fields on the Family screen, and will select the “Other” from the Proof of Identity drop-down list • Staff will enter a Staff Alert stating AAR needs to show ID and sign R&O. However, no names shall be entered into the note, in order to ensure confidentiality.

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.012 - 2

C. If one AR is present and the AAR is not present at a subsequent certification: • Request identification (ID) from the present AR and update in HANDS what proof of ID was seen • For the AR who is not present, select “OTHER” from the Proof of Identity drop-down list • “Rights & Obligations” signature type in HANDS shall be signed by the present AR • When the AR who was not present at Certification returns to the clinic at a subsequent visit, ID will be verified and staff shall update the ID provided in the appropriate field on the Family screen in HANDS, and have the AR sign the R&O signature type in HANDS

Note: If the AAR is present and the primary AR is not present, the AAR can continue to sign the “Second AR Rights & Obligations” signature type in HANDS.

D. If the AR is contacting WIC remotely for non-certification appointments and names an AAR: • For non-certification appointments, staff shall verify identity by either reviewing the AR’s ID or using identifiers such as having the AR verify their date of birth, address, and/or phone number • Staff will add the first and last name of an AAR in the appropriate fields on the Family screen and will select “OTHER” from the Proof of Identity drop-down list • Staff will enter a Staff Alert stating that the AAR needs to show ID and sign the R&O; no names shall be entered into the note in order to ensure confidentiality

III. Change of AR during a Certification period (i.e., Change of Guardianship and/or Custody)

When an AR changes during a certification period (i.e., change in guardianship and/or custody) stating that the infant/child is currently under their care, the clinic may issue up to three (3) months of food benefits to the infant/child if ALL five (5) of the following conditions are met:

1. The new AR shall bring the infant/child participant to the WIC appointment. If they do not bring the infant/child to the clinic, they are to be rescheduled. 2. The new AR shall show proof of the infant/child’s ID. If ID is not available, staff can issue one (1) month Food Benefits and have the AR return the following month with the appropriate documents. 3. The new AR shall sign the “Change of Authorized Representative” Form declaring that they are caring for the infant/child and an explanation of the circumstances that led them to becoming the caretaker (visit “Policies & Forms page under Local Agencies on www.dcwic.org for the Change of Authorized Representative Form). 4. LA staff will assist the new AR with the written statement if they are unable to write, and he or she shall sign the statement or make their identifying mark (see Appendix 8.001a). 5. The income of the new AR shall be verified by WIC staff to ensure it meets the WIC eligibility criteria.

Procedure: A new Family ID number will be created in HANDS to accommodate the new AR’s demographic information. This procedure needs to occur even when the former and new AR(s) are from the same household. The infant/child will be transferred into this new family. The procedure is as follows:

1. In HANDS, identify the correct participant to be moved into the new family. Go to the Client screen.

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.012 - 3

2. If the new AR already has a HANDS record, select “transfer client” from the Client screen of the person to be transferred and select “existing family.” Search for the family you wish to transfer them into. Click the correct family and select “transfer client.” The participant is now in the new family. 3. If the new AR does not have an existing record in HANDS, select “transfer client” from the Client screen of the person to be transferred, and select “new family.” You will then be taken to a blank Family screen. Enter all information for the new AR. Click Save. The participant is now in the new family. 4. Proceed with the transaction. NOTE: Verify and document the new AR’s income. 5. The new AR shall sign the “WIC Rights and Obligations” signature type in HANDS. 6. If the new AR does not currently have an eWIC Card, an eWIC card will be issued to the family. The new AR shall sign the “eWIC Card Received” signature type in HANDS, if applicable. 7. The WIC staff member shall scan the completed Change of Authorized Representative form into the participant’s HANDS file.

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.013 - 1 Policy 8.013 Transfers and VOCs CFR § 246.7(k) Transfer of Certification I. Policy Statement

Transfers that are currently in a valid certification period shall be placed on the program when present at the receiving clinic.

II. Out of State Transfers

For our-of-state transfers within a valid certification period, the LA to which the participant is transferring shall:

• Confirm that at least one AR is present in the clinic at the time of transfer. Agencies utilizing a secured online platform such as Zoom, the transfer shall be completed when the staff and at least one AR begin the appointment. • Ensure that the participant was never participating in DC WIC by using HANDS to do a statewide search. o If the participant was once a DC WIC participant, staff shall transfer the participant(s) into their clinic first. o If the participant was certified in DC, transferred out of state, and then returned to DC WIC within the timeframe in which the certification is still current, the previous certification shall be reinstated. • Verify approved forms of ID and proof of residency for all transferring WIC participants. o If neither proof of ID nor residency are brought in at time of transfer, staff shall input “Forgot Documentation” and issue one month of Food Benefits. o Additional benefits shall NOT be issued until proof of ID and/or residency have been received. • Complete the Out-of-State Transfer screen in HANDS. o For participants transferring from another state WIC Program, clinic staff will select priority 0. • For the unique VOC number in the Transfer screen, use the 2-letter state abbreviation followed by the unique identifier on the actual VOC. If there is no unique identifier on the VOC, use the state abbreviation followed by the Participant or Family ID that is provided on the VOC. • Have AR(s) sign the “Rights and Obligations” signature type in HANDS and scan the VOC into the participant’s file in HANDS. • LA staff shall obtain the food instruments or eWIC card issued by the sending agency if still in the participant’s possession, if applicable. The receiving LA shall destroy the unused food benefits or eWIC card from the transferring participant.

III. Verification of Certification

LAs receiving transfers shall accept Verification of Certification (VOC) documents from other states.

A document containing the following information is to be considered a valid VOC:

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.013 - 2 • Name of participant • Beginning date of Certification • Ending date of Certification • Date of income determination • Participant’s nutrition risk • Normal signature and full printed/typed name of the certifying Local Agency official • Name and address of the certifying Local Agency • An identification number or other means of accountability • Identification of migrant status

IV. Partially Complete Verification of Certification (VOC)

A partially complete VOC will be considered proof of WIC eligibility if it contains the following information:

• Name of participant • Beginning date of Certification • Ending date of Certification period • Name and address of the certifying Local Agency

NOTE: Participants who arrive in a new service delivery area showing a partially complete VOC will be treated as if the VOC contained all the information.

V. Retention of VOC/Rights and Obligation

LAs will retain the VOC from the transferring agency by scanning it into the participant’s file in HANDS and having the AR sign the “Rights and Obligations” signature type in HANDS.

VI. Transfer When a Waiting List Exists

An individual transferring from out-of-state into a DC WIC Local Agency will be allowed to participate (unless there is a waiting list for all priorities) until the designated end of their current certification period.

VII. Special Conditions

Participants that transfer to DC WIC and present a VOC which indicates they are transferring from a State Agency with a shorter certification period than DC, but they are still in a current Certification, shall have their Certification period extended.

• Infants who have a Certification start date on the VOC that was prior to the infant turning six months old shall have their Certification extended to their first birthday.

• Children with six-month Certification periods on the VOC will have their Certification extended to one year from the Certification start date that appears on the VOC.

• Breastfeeding women with six-month Certification periods on the VOC will have their Certification extended to the infant’s first birthday.

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.013 - 3 VIII. In-State Transfers

For transfers within the DC WIC Program, the LA to which the participant is transferring shall do the following:

• Confirm that at least one AR is present in the clinic at the time of transfer. In agencies utilizing a secure online platform such as Zoom, the transfer shall be completed when the staff and at least one AR begin the appointment. • Verify the identity by either reviewing the AR’s ID or using identifiers such as having the AR verify their date of birth, address, and/or phone number. • Perform a statewide search using HANDS to locate the participant/family. • Assess the type of service(s) the participant/family needs by asking questions of the AR and evaluating the Certification information on the search screen in HANDS. If additional information is needed, contact the clinic in which the participant is transferring from for more details. • Inform the participant that transferring will automatically cancel any appointments they may have at the other clinic and request permission to transfer the participant/family. • Complete the In-State Transfer process in HANDS.

NOTE: Transfers over the phone are NOT permitted for the sole purpose of making an appointment in HANDS.

Once the transfer in HANDS is completed:

• If the participant/family is not in a current Certification, a Certification shall be completed. • If the participant/family is in a current Certification, the following will be completed in addition to providing the rest of the required services for that appointment: o Update Address and Voter Registration status on the Family screen in HANDS o Provide an updated Local Agency referral list

NOTE: A transfer from Navajo Nation WIC or Inter Tribal Council of Arizona, Inc. (ITCA) WIC programs is considered an out-of-state transfer.

IX. Transferring out of DC WIC

If a participant is transferring to a WIC Program in another state, staff shall provide the participant/AR with the VOC. If the participant/AR does not obtain a VOC ahead of time, the other state may request information about the incoming participant. The requested information will be faxed to the requesting program upon receipt of the request from the other state’s WIC Program.

NOTE: If the participant is in a “Conditional Certification” status and has pending eligibility documentation, staff shall write “30 Day Conditional Certification-Missing Eligibility Documentation” on the VOC before providing it to the participant or agency to which the participant is transferring. Staff shall specify which eligibility documentation was missing by writing it on the VOC.

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.013 - 4 X. WIC Overseas

When participants are transferring from WIC Overseas, DC WIC will utilize their signed VOC (also called a Participant Profile Report), and transfer them into DC WIC. The Out-of-State Transfer screen in HANDS shall be completed, the Rights and Obligation Form signed, and the Local Agency will scan the VOC Form into the participant’s HANDS record.

If the participant does not have a VOC, contact WIC Overseas at 1 (877) 267-3728. If the applicant is not in a valid Certification period, they will begin a new Certification period if still eligible.

When participants are transferring to WIC Overseas, participants will use their DC WIC Program VOC printed from HANDS.

body:
VIII. Certification December 2021 8.014 - 1 8.014 Ineligibility CFR § 246.7(j) Notification of participant rights and responsibilities I. Policy Statement Persons found ineligible for the Program during a certification visit must be advised in writing of the ineligibility, of the reasons for the ineligibility, and of the right to a fair hearing. The reasons for ineligibility must be properly documented and must be retained on file at the local agency.

II. Notification of Ineligibility The Notification of Ineligibility form notifies applicants and participants of their right to a fair hearing, of the reason they were determined ineligible for the program and/or the reason for a program disqualification. This form is available in HANDS or under “Policies and Forms” page under Local Agencies at www.dcwic.org. A signature is not required.

Persons found ineligible at the time of certification shall be issued the DC WIC “Notification of Ineligibility” form. Staff shall ensure the name of the participant is on the form. It is not necessary or required to issue this form when category changes are made, as category changes do not lead to appeal rights. Those who change categories after a certification shall be notified verbally of their new certification dates.

A person who will be disqualified from the program by the State Agency shall be issued the Notification of Ineligibility form no less than 15 days before the disqualification.

NOTE: Staff shall not make photocopies of applicants’ proof of income. LA Staff shall use the termination codes listed in Appendix 8.001c when terminating certifications. III. Information About Reapplication

Applicants will be informed on how to reapply if conditions change or if they obtain the necessary documentation.

IV. Referrals

Applicants will be given written information regarding other food assistance programs for which they may be eligible.

body:
VIII. Certification 8.015 - 1 December 2021 Policy 8.015 Violations and Sanctions CFR §246.12 (u) Participant violations and sanctions

I. Policy Statement

DC WIC will implement policies and procedures for the detection of fraud and abuse within the Program, and may disqualify, terminate, and/or assess fines as outlined in this policy.

II. Definitions:

a. Abuse - An intentional infliction of physical harm and/or to attack with verbal words. This can include, but is not limited to, ridiculing or being demeaning, making derogatory remarks toward or verbally harassing another.

Abuse is also defined as misuse: to use something in an improper, illegal, or harmful way.

b. Fraud - An intentional misrepresentation of the truth to deceive others for the purpose of acquiring something of value, such as a financial gain or WIC benefits. Anything calculated to deceive, whether it be by a single act or combination, by the suppression of truth, or by a suggestion of what is false, whether it is by a direct lie (deception), silence, omission, a look, or a gesture. An example of fraud could be the selling of an issued food instrument (i.e. eWIC card or Farmers’ Market Nutrition Program check) and/or state issued equipped (i.e. breast pump, accessories) for personal gain; an act which intentionally deceives the WIC program and abuses one’s benefits.

c. Intent to Violate - Any intentional action of a participant, parent or caretaker of an infant or child participant that violates Federal or State statutes, regulations, policies, or procedures governing the Program.

• For the purposes of DC WIC, an intentional violation is defined as a participant making a verbal offer to sell to another individual or providing the posting of WIC foods, WIC items or any other issued WIC benefits for sale, given away or traded online, in any type of printed manner (newspapers, etc.), or allowing someone else to conduct this act for them (knowingly or unknowingly), would be evidence that the participant has intentional, whether direct or indirect, committed a participant violation.

d. Participant Violation - Intentional activities or actions of DC WIC participants or their ARs taken to obtain benefits to which they are not entitled and/or to misuse benefits they receive. Activities and actions include, but are not limited to:

• Misrepresenting facts used to determine eligibility (e.g. total household income, age of children, existence of children, custody of children, address, etc.) • Exchanging/substituting food benefits for non-approved items (e.g., cash, alcohol, or tobacco products, sundries, etc.) • Selling or giving away foods obtained with WIC issued food benefits

VIII. Certification 8.015 - 2 December 2021 • Selling or attempting to sell (either in person, online, or through any other means available), WIC foods or WIC items (i.e. Breast pump, breast milk storage bags, and/or other accessories) received through the WIC Program. • Participating at more than one WIC agency simultaneously (dual participation) • Verbally/physically abusing WIC vendors and/or WIC staff

III. Participant Disqualification for Program Fraud

DC WIC participants shall receive written warning or be disqualified when an investigation and supporting evidence/documentation verifies that participant fraud has occurred.

The State Agency reserves the right to disqualify participants for other actions not listed herein if the participant violates any program policies and/or regulations.

Disqualification Without Warning Serious substantiated violations of program integrity, such as the sale of WIC food benefits or breast pumps will result in disqualification without any prior warning. Warnings before sanctions are at the sole discretion of the State Agency and are conducted on a case by case basis.

Participants Rights and Responsibilities When Disqualified Participants have the right to appeal any denial, claim or disqualification at a fair hearing or an informal dispute resolution conference. Participants shall be provided, within a minimum of 15 calendar days, written notice prior to a disqualification. For more information on hearing and informal dispute resolution procedures, see Local Agency Policy and Procedure Manual section 12.

Exception for Disqualification The State Agency may decide not to impose a mandatory disqualification if, within thirty (30) days of receipt of the notice of repayment, full restitution is made or a repayment schedule is agreed upon. A participant will have the opportunity to provide a personal statement explaining the circumstances surrounding the loss of the pump. All decisions are at the discretion of the State Agency.

Reapplication A participant may be permitted to reapply for the program before the end of a disqualification period if full repayment is made or a repayment schedule is agreed upon.

IV. Dual Participation within DC WIC

When Local Agencies are faced with factors/situations that include participants traveling routinely between local services located across the State Agency Borders, dual participation must be evaluated and consequences discussed when a participant received benefits from more than one (1) State WIC Agency. Examples of these factors/situations may include the following: lack of geographic barriers and common vendors. If Dual Participation is determined, the sanctions in Section VII, #14 and #15, are to be followed. The State Agency will produce Dual Participation Reports. The purpose of Dual Participation Reports is to detect potential dual participation within DC WIC.

VIII. Certification 8.015 - 3 December 2021 A. State Agency Responsibilities The State Agency will:

• Coordinate efforts with LAs when potential dual participation has occurred • Request supporting documentation from LAs to include, but not limited to, signature receipts and signed Rights and Obligations forms • Conduct an exhaustive investigation to determine if dual participation occurred and will inform LAs of the necessary course of action and/or sanction

B. Local Agency Responsibility Local Agencies will:

• Request information from applicants about previous participation in other WIC programs • Appropriately handle potential dual participants when prompted by HANDS • Notify the State Agency, in writing, of any identified possible dual participation within 15 business days of discovery • Provide information as requested by the State Agency • Coordinate with the State Agency to impose appropriate sanction when dual participation has been determined

V. Responsibilities

State Agency Local Agency Consult with the Attorney General’s Office in cases of alleged fraud and abuse, and if appropriate, the USDA Office of the Inspector General and/or Local Law Enforcement. Document all allegations of Program abuse or fraud. Responsible for incoming reports of Program abuse or fraud to the State Agency by email, phone, or www.dcwic.org, and any/all information obtained. In all cases where Program abuse or fraud is alleged against a participant, the Local Agency shall immediately contact the Nutrition Services team and provide supporting documentation to the State Agency. Verify information regarding alleged participant abuse and/or fraud, and will retain documentation. Consult with the State Agency prior to taking any action regarding participant abuse and fraud. Following a thorough investigation, the State Agency will determine the appropriate participant sanction (if applicable). If there is a sanction, the Local Agency will advise the participant of the Program requirements they violated (i.e. what they did wrong, and the correct procedure). Determine the amount of funds improperly received by the participant. Assist the participant in preparation and submission of their written request for an appeal of a claim and/or a Program disqualification. (See Appendices B and C for appeal procedure forms). Assist the participant with completing a repayment schedule for claims.

VIII. Certification 8.015 - 4 December 2021 When an investigation has verified fraud or abuse, the State Agency will send a certified letter to the participant regarding the sanction and, if appropriate, the amount of repayment requested. A copy of the certified letter will be sent to the Local Agency. Provide the participant with Program benefits (i.e. food package) as stated below. Inform the participant of their right to appeal a claim or a Program disqualification. Provide program benefits to participants who appeal disqualification within fifteen (15) calendar days of the written notification of disqualification until the appeal is decided, the participant becomes categorically ineligible, or the certification periods expires, whichever occurs first. Provide an informal dispute resolution meeting and/or a fair hearing.

VI. Claims If the State Agency determines that Program benefits have been obtained or disposed of improperly as the result of a participant violation, the State Agency will establish a claim against the participant for the full value of the improperly received benefits, in addition to applying any appropriate sanctions per the sanction schedule. Following an investigation that has confirmed there was a participant violation, the State Agency will: • Determine the amount of any improperly received benefits. • Establish a claim against the participant for the full value of the improperly received benefits. • Send the claim by certified mail to the participant and an electronic copy to the Local Agency If the participant chooses to appeal the claim, the Local Agency may assist in completing the appeal request. If the participant chooses a repayment plan for claims, the Local Agency will assist in developing a payment schedule.

If the participant has not paid the State Agency directly within 15 days of the notice, the participant’s account will be flagged internally and benefits will be restricted until the claim is paid. If full payment or a payment schedule has not been established after two (2) letters demanding repayment, the State Agency will not pursue further collection sanctions under $500.00. If the sanction exceeds $500, the Office of Inspector and Compliance (OIC) will assist the State Agency in recovering the claim.

VIII. Certification 8.015 - 5 December 2021 VII. Types of Violations and Sanctions

ABUSE SANTION 1. Using Food Benefits to buy unauthorized food equaling $99 or less 1st – 90 day disqualification and repayment 2nd – Disqualification of 1-year and repayment 2. Using Food Benefits to buy unauthorized food equaling $100 or more 1-year disqualification and repayment 3. Exchanging food benefits for credit or non- food items 1st – 90 day disqualification and repayment 2nd – Disqualification of 1-year and repayment 4. Direct or indirect theft of food benefits 1-year disqualification, repayment, referral to the appropriate Law Enforcement Authorities, and possible referral to SNAP authorities 5. Deliberate misrepresentation of any intake criteria to obtain WIC benefits, including: • Income • Residency • Family size • Health status

Immediate termination, 1-year disqualification, and repayment 6. Attempting to sell WIC foods, WIC items or any other WIC-issued benefits either verbally, online, in any type of printed manner (newspapers, etc.), or knowingly allowing someone else to conduct this act for them, with or without that person’s knowledge of WIC participant fraud, abuse and misuse

1st – 90-day disqualification and possible referral to SNAP authorities 2nd – 1-year disqualification and possible referral to SNAP authorities 7. Selling supplemental food that was purchased with WIC food benefit(s) (to include infant formula) and/or WIC-issued items (i.e., personal or hospital-grade breast pumps). 1-year disqualification, repayment, and possible referral to the appropriate Local Enforcement Authorities, and possible referral to SNAP authorities 8. Attempting to give away or trade WIC foods, WIC items or any other WIC-issued benefits either verbally, online, in any type of printed manner (newspapers, etc.), or knowingly allowing someone else to conduct this act for them, with or without that person’s knowledge of WIC participant fraud, abuse and misuse 1st - Written Warning 2nd - 30-day disqualification 3rd - 90-day disqualification 9. Giving away or trading supplemental food that was purchased with WIC food benefit(s) (to include infant formula) and/or WIC- issued items (i.e., personal or hospital-grade breast pumps). 1st - 30-day disqualification 2nd - 90-day disqualification

VIII. Certification 8.015 - 6 December 2021 10. Using food benefit(s) at unauthorized stores and/or through any other unauthorized channels. 1st - 90-day disqualification and repayment and possible referral to SNAP authorities 2nd - 1-year disqualification and repayment and possible referral to SNAP authorities 11. Creating a public nuisance, or disrupting normal activities through verbal misconduct at the Local Agency or at any DC WIC- authorized vendor. 1st - Warning letter 2nd - 30-day disqualification 3rd - 1-year disqualification 12. Threatening harm to Local Agency or Vendor staff. 1-year disqualification and possible referral to the appropriate Law Enforcement Authorities 13. Physically abusing Local Agency or Vendor staff or property 1-year disqualification and reported to Law Enforcement 14. Dual participation: using food benefits(s) from two programs/agencies in the same month, includes WIC programs from surrounding states (VA, MD, PA, WV, etc). Immediate termination from all but one (1) program/agency received, full repayment of the dual benefits to other Programs, and possible referral to SNAP authorities 15. Dual Participation resulting from intentional misrepresentation. 1-year disqualification from all Programs, repayment of all benefits, and possible referral to SNAP authorities 16. Assessed a claim for $100 or more. 1-year disqualification and repayment. 17. Assessed a 2nd claim or subsequent claim, for any amount 1-year disqualification and repayment. 18. Trafficking WIC food benefits, WIC benefits, or other WIC-issued items and/or collusion with an authorized vendor. 1-year disqualification and repayment referral to the appropriate Law Enforcement Authorities and possible referral to SNAP authorities

Note: Combined sanctions may be applied when more than one kind of violation, actual or attempted, is involved in an instance of abuse.

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.016 - 1 8.016 Rights & Obligations 7 CFR 246.7(j) Notification of Participant Rights & Obligations I. Policy Statement

Participants and ARs shall be informed of their WIC Rights and Obligations (R&O) at every Certification and out-of-state transfer(s), in their preferred language. WIC staff shall read out loud, at minimum, the highlighted sections of the R&O to the applicant/AR (in a language they understand). The highlighted sections include:

• Health Information • Fair Treatment • Honesty • Accurate information • Good Use of the Program • Protect your Benefits

WIC staff shall inform the participant or AR that the complete R&O can be found online at dcwic.org and offer a copy (paper or electronic) each time the R&O are signed.

II. Documentation

Documentation of WIC R&O shall be completed at every certification and out-of-state transfer by having the participant/AR sign the signature type “Rights and Obligations” on the signature pad in HANDS.

III. Paper Rights and Obligations Form

If, for some reason, HANDS is not available to capture signatures on the “Rights and Obligations” signature type and/or the “Consent” signature type, a paper copy of the R&O Form shall be used. This form can be found on dcwic.org under Local Agencies > Policies & Forms. The form can be used for all members of the WIC family if desired.

1. The form shall be signed and dated at each certification by the AR and the certifier or income verifier. LAs are required to have systems in place to obtain a signature if an AR forgets to sign. 2. The AR’s initials are necessary and serve as permission that staff can weigh/measure and check hemoglobin status for each participant listed on the form. Additionally, the AR can agree to receive assistance with breastfeeding, if applicable. 3. Fill in the Family ID # in the table. 4. Fill in only the names of participants being certified on that particular day. 5. The height/weight/hemoglobin fields are not mandatory; however, LAs may choose to create a LA policy to make those fields mandatory. 6. The vertical bubbles for Family ID # and Authorized Representative Name are not mandatory; however; LAs may choose to create a LA policy to make those fields mandatory. The fields will prefill if the form is printed from HANDS. 7. Signed R&O forms must be scanned into the participant’s HANDS record.

body:
VIII. Certification September 2021 8.017 - 1 8.017 - Voter Registration National Voter Registration Act (NVRA) (1973), Pub L, 103 931 §7(a)(5); DC Official Code § 1-1001.07; 11 CFR 8.2; 11CFR 8.3(c), and 7 CFR 246. I. Policy Statement LA staff shall provide each applicant, participant, or - in the case of infants and children – authorized representatives (ARs) the opportunity to register to vote:

• With each application for Certification or Recertification • With each transfer, including a change of address • When the participant or AR reports a change of address

LA staff providing voter registration assistance shall not:

• Seek to influence an applicant’s or participant’s or AR’s political preference or party registration • Wear or display any material that o Identifies past, present, or future seekers of partisan elective office o Contains logos or other graphics that may be identified with a political party or preference o Would reasonably be associated with a political party or preference o Identifies a political issue or ballot measure • Make any statement to an applicant, participant, or AR or take any action, the purpose or effect of which is to discourage the applicant from registering to vote

LA Staff shall advise applicants, participants, or ARs that: • The voter registration process is separate from the WIC Program eligibility process • An interview is not necessary to register to vote

LA Staff shall ensure the confidentiality of the Voter Registration process

LA Staff shall complete training developed by the State Agency upon hire and annually thereafter.

II. Voter Registration Procedures

LA Staff will follow use the following procedure when offering an applicant, participant, or AR the opportunity to register to vote:

1. Ask the applicant, participant, or AR if they are registered to vote at their current address a. If they say “yes” – document in HANDS b. If they say “no” – go to step 2

2. Ask the applicant, participant, or AR if they are interested in registering to vote today. Inform them that they can complete the voter registration form at the clinic or they may take it with them and mail it in later (postage is paid). Also inform them that applying/denying to register to vote will not affect their application or enrollment in DC WIC.

VIII. Certification September 2021 8.017 - 2 a. If they say “no” – document in HANDS record. If the applicant does not provide a reason for saying no, staff may use their best judgment in whether or not to probe for why the applicant is not interested in registering to vote. Staff may select “not interested”, or “not yet 18” in the HANDS record. b. If they say “yes” and want to complete the form later – provide a physical copy of the form and/or show the applicant a link or QR code to where they can find the voter registration form online. Document using “refused, gave form” in HANDS record. Using this code will help DC WIC identify between participants who were not interested in registering to vote and those who were interested but did not do so on site. c. If they say “yes” and want to complete the form onsite – see step 3

3. Provide the applicant with a DC Voter Registration Form to complete. Staff shall also inform the applicant, participant, or AR of the availability of the Federal Voter Registration Form. a. Staff will assist the applicant, participant, or AR when requested. Assistance provided shall be to the degree that assistance is provided for completing a WIC form. b. When the client has completed the voter registration form, review it completely to ensure that it contains all of the information required for voter registration, including the applicant’s signature. c. Inform the client that you will send the voter registration form to the DC Board of Elections (DCBOE) and that they should receive their voter registration card within three weeks if the form was accepted. If they do not receive their voter registration card within three weeks, they should contact DCBOE. d. Mail the voter registration form to DCBOE within five (5) calendar days i. LA Best Practice: Mail voter registration forms the day they are completed, or store them in a secure location and mail any collected forms on Friday morning each week.

III. HANDS Documentation

LA staff shall indicate in the Voter Registration field in HANDS the response given by the applicant, participant, or AR either. HANDS will not allow a certification appointment to be completed until Voter Registration status has been documented. The following table lists HANDS documentation codes for Voter Registration, and when to use them:

Code Explanation When to Use CR Currently Registered If client states they are registered already at their current address NO Not Interested If client is not currently registered and does not want to register NA Not yet 18 years of age If client is under 18 years old and is not eligible to register RG Refused, gave form If client took a form home with them or said they would register online YG Yes, Gave Form If client completed form onsite and LA staff mailed it to DCBOE

VIII. Certification September 2021 8.017 - 3 IV. State Agency Responsibilities

The DC WIC State Agency will assume the responsibilities of both the “Voter Registration Site Coordinator” and the “Voter Registration Agency Coordinator”. The HANDS MIS allows the State Agency to pull reports for each LA, by clinic site, on certification appointments and voter registration indication. The State Agency will use such reports to chart the following information on a monthly basis for reporting to DCBOE:

LA 1 LA 2 LA 3 LA 4 Total # Certification appointments

# Clients currently registered (CR)

# Clients not interested (NO)

# Clients not yet 18 (NA)

# Clients took form offsite (RG)

# Clients completed form onsite (YG)

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.018 1 | P a g e Title: Referrals Overview Category: Certification CFR Reference 7 CFR 246.7 7 CFR 246.11 Policy Number: 8.018 Effective Date: December 1st, 2021 Revised Date: April 30th, 2024

POLICY STATEMENT: In accordance with 7 CFR 246.7(b) the Local Agency must provide program applicants and participants with information on other health-related and public assistance programs and when appropriate, shall refer applicants and participants to such programs. Each referral provided to the participant must be documented in the participant’s record in the MIS. The Local Agency must also ensure that: 1. Each participant is made known of adjunct eligibility programs and provided appropriate referrals as applicable to the Supplemental Assistance Nutrition Program (SNAP), Medicaid, the National School Lunch Program (NSLP), and Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF). 2. Each participant under the age of two is provided screening for immunization status and appropriate referrals for immunization (FNS WIC Policy Memorandum #2001-7). 3. All participants are screened for blood lead testing (FNS Policy Memorandum 93-3A – WIC’s Role in Screening for Childhood Lead Poisoning) in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.010 Anthropometric and Biochemical Data Collection and refer all child participants to their healthcare provider if testing has not been performed or if the Authorized Representative (AR) is unsure of the child participant’s blood lead value. 4. A listing of community resources for substance abuse is maintained and available for distribution in accordance with 7 CFR 246.7(a) and DC WIC policy 8.020 Substance Use Screening and Referral. 5. Referral procedures are established for high-risk participants in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.008 Serving High Risk Participants and participants needing breastfeeding support in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.009 Breastfeeding Education and Support Overview. PROCEDURE 1. Each referral provided to the participant must consider their individual needs based on the nutrition assessment, environmental concerns, and/or living conditions. Referrals to other health-related and public assistance programs can include: • Local food banks, pantries, or other food assistance programs • Housing assistance • Early childhood services • Childcare • Dental care • Prenatal care • Shelters and other services for domestic violence • Infant care supplies • Mental health services

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.018 2 | P a g e Local agency staff are encouraged to use approved online referral resources such as https://linkudmv.org/. 2. Any referral that is made to directly assist the participant in achieving their health outcome- based goal must be documented in the “I” portion of the TGIF note in accordance with DC WIC 2.005 Nutrition Education Overview. • For example, a referral to the Produce Plus Program is made to the participant to assist in achieving their goal of consuming a fresh fruit and vegetable at least once per day. 3. See additional DC WIC policies for more information on referral procedures for: • Immunization Screening and Referral – 8.019 • Substance Use Screening and Referral – 8.020 • Domestic Violence and Neglect – 8.021 REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.7(b) FNS WIC Policy Memorandum #2001-7 DC WIC policies 2.005 Nutrition Education Overview, 2.008 Serving High Risk Participants, 2.009 Breastfeeding Education and Support Overview, 8.020 Substance Use Screening and Referral ATTACHMENTS & FORMS
