DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.019 1 | P a g e Title: Immunization Screening and Referral Category: Certification CFR Reference Policy Number: 8.019 Effective Date December 1st, 2021 Revised Date: April 30th, 2024

POLICY STATEMENT: The Local Agency must screen all infants and children under age two for DTaP immunization status, document according to the procedures below in the participant’s record in the MIS, and provide appropriate referrals, as needed. PROCEDURE Immunization Screening At each initial certification and subsequent certification appointments, the Local Agency staff member will verify with the Authorized Representative (AR) if the infant or child is up to date on DTaP vaccinations based on the schedule below (also available in HANDS): Age Recommended number of DTaP doses 2-3 months 1 dose 4-5 months 2 doses 6-17 months 3 doses 18-24 months 4 doses

Immunization Documentation Acceptable forms of immunization status verification include a documented record that lists both the vaccination type administered and date received. This can include: • An immunization record from a medical provider • An immunization registry • An electronic medical record Missing Immunization Documentation If the immunization record is missing at the time of certification: 1. Encourage the caretaker to provide the immunization record at their next WIC appointment. 2. Provide the recommended immunization schedule for the infant or child. 3. Refer the participant to their healthcare provider or local immunization program and document this referral in the participant’s record in the MIS. Immunization Referral A referral should be provided if the AR is unsure of their infant or child’s immunization status or if the child is under-immunized (i.e. not up to date on the recommended number of DTaP doses). A referral is not needed if the AR states the family does not vaccinate. This reason must be documented both on the “Immunization” screen (under “No Assess Code”) and in the “I’ portion of the TGIF note in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.005 Nutrition Education Overview. It is additionally recommended to place a Staff Alert for the family that does not vaccinate.

body:
DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.020 1 | P a g e Title: Substance Use Screening and Referral Category: Certification CFR Reference: 7 CFR 246.7(a) 7 CFR 246.7(n)(2) Policy Number: 8.020 Effective Date: September 1st 2021 Revised Date: April 30th, 2024

POLICY STATEMENT: In accordance with 7 CFR 246.7(a), 7 CFR 246.7(n)(2), and 7 CFR 246.11(a)(3) the Local Agency must ensure: 1. Local Agency Resource List - A listing of local resources for drug and other harmful substance abuse counseling and treatment is maintained and made available for distribution to all pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding women and to parents or caretakers of infants and children in the DC WIC program, as required by Public Health Law 101-147. 2. Screening - Drug and other harmful substance abuse screening is performed at certification as part of the nutritional assessment for all pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding women and to parents or caretakers of infants and children. 3. Brief Intervention (Education) and Referral - Education on the harmful effects of drug and other harmful substances is provided at certification, and if needed, a referral is made to the participant or to the parent or caregiver of an infant or child. Education needs to be provided once per certification. 4. Documentation - The CPA/CPPA documents the education and referral (if provided) in the participant’s record in the MIS (see DC WIC policy 2.006 Nutrition Education Documentation). PROCEDURE Substance Abuse Screening Substance abuse screening must be performed at certification for all pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding participants and to parents or caretakers to infant and child participants as part of the nutrition assessment. The CPA/CPPA should ensure privacy and conduct the screening process in a nonjudgemental manner. Screening questions can include: 1. Have you ever had difficulties in your life because of alcohol, smoking, or other drug use, including unprescribed medications? 2. Do you have any concerns about the use of drug, alcohol, or other harmful substances for yourself or someone who spends a significant amount of time with you and/or your child? If the participant or parent or caretaker of an infant or child participant responds “no” to either screening question above, then general substance use education must be provided (see below). If the participant or parent or caretaker of an infant or child participant responds “yes” to either screening question above, then the CPA/CPPA must further evaluate if any nutritional risk codes should be applied to the participant (see DC WIC Nutrition Risk Manual) and provide tailored substance use education (see below).

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.020 2 | P a g e Substance Use Brief Intervention (Education) and Referral All participants and caretakers must receive brief intervention education on the harmful effects of substance use at the time of certification. Depending on the response provided by the participant or caretaker above, the CPA/CPPA must provide one of the following forms of education: 1. General education – if the participant or caretaker responds “no” to the substance use screening questions and/or if the participant does not appear to need tailored substance use education. The CPA/CPPA may perform the following: a. Provide brief education related to the dangers of substance use. Staff may reference the “Give Your Baby a Healthy Start” handout or the “Substance Use: Risk to You and Your Family” handout created by DC WIC (handouts are available on www.dcwic.org). b. Provide the local agency listing of substance use resources. Staff may describe how to access resources online. 2. Tailored Education – if the participant or caretaker responds “yes” to the substance use screening questions and/or if a substance use related nutrition risk code has been identified for the participant. The CPA/CPPA should discuss the answers provided to the substance use screening questions and the potential substance abuse problem. The CPA/CPPA should provide the brief intervention in a positive framing, such as below:

Accentuate the Positive and Avoid the Negative (Source – FNS Substance Use Prevention Guide) Positive Negative If you stop drinking now, you have a better chance of having a healthy baby. Your drinking has already damaged your baby. Your concern for your baby will help you be a good mother. If you really loved your baby, you would not drink so much. You will feel better when you are sober and so will your child. Continued drinking will ruin your health and prevent your child from developing normally.

Substance Use Referral The information collected from the substance use screening and nutrition assessment must be used as the basis of providing a general or tailored substance use referral to the participant: • Informal (general) – the referral can be considered general if the participant receives general education related to substance use and its harmful effects. • Semi-formal (tailored) – the referral can be considered semi-formal if the participant responds “yes” to the substance use screening questions and the CPA/CPPA works with the participant to identify specific resources that may best address the substance use concern. A tailored referral must be documented in the “I” portion of the TGIF note. • Formal (tailored and action-based) – the referral can be considered formal if the participant responds “yes” to the substance use screening questions and the CPA/CPPA initiates contact

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 8.020 3 | P a g e with an assessment, counseling, treatment, legal, or any substance use-related agency on behalf of the participant. This type of referral is generally considered outside the normal practice for WIC staff and requires a Release of Information form to be signed by the participant or Authorized Representative in accordance with DC WIC policy 12.019 Confidentiality. • No referral – there may be cases where no referral is made for the participant at the time of certification such as if the participant or caretaker denies the request for a referral to substance use services. A referral denial must be documented in the “I” portion of the TGIF note for the participant in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.005 Nutrition Education Overview. Documentation The CPA/CPPA must ensure that the brief intervention (education) and referral (if applicable) are documented in the participant’s record at the time of certification as follows: • The education provided (either general or tailored) must be documented in the “I” portion of the TGIF note for the participant at the time of certification. • If a referral is provided, it must be documented under the “Referrals” tab of participant’s record in the MIS. o If the referral is a tailored (i.e. formal) referral, this information must be documented in the “I” portion of the TGIF note. o If the participant or caretaker refuses a referral for substance use, this must be documented in the “I” portion of the TGIF note. REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.7(a) 7 CFR 246.7(n)(2) 7 CFR 246.11(a)(3) DC WIC policy 2.005 Nutrition Education Overview, 2.006 Nutrition Education Documentation, 12.019 Confidentiality ATTACHMENTS & FORMS Substance Use Prevention Guide (USDA – WIC) Substance Use Screen / Educate / Refer Cheat Sheet DC WIC Nutrition Risk Manual

body:
VIII. Certification December 2021 8.021 - 1 8.021 - Domestic Violence And Neglect District of Columbia law (see D.C. Code §22-3020.52[a]); D.C. Code §4-1321.02)

I. Policy Statement

Abuse is most often perpetrated by one person to another with whom they have an intimate or family relationship. While domestic violence of an adult is not considered a reportable offence, state law requires reporting suspected child sex abuse. Reporting suspected physical abuse or negligence of children is also encouraged.

II. Abuse of adult participants

In the HANDS participant Assessment screen under letter E (Environmental/Other Factors) probing questions, there is a question on abuse that must be asked at every certification, unless the safety of the participant would be at risk with a potential abuser present. If the participant or authorized representative answers “yes,” Local Agency Policy and Procedures must be followed.

The safety of the client must be the first priority. Some questions that can be asked include: • “Do you have a safe place to go?” • If client is residing in a safe place, ask, “Do you want to talk to someone about your abusive situation?” • “Do you want a referral to a safe house, program, or hotline for abuse?” • “Is it safe to give you information on abuse to read?” o In many cases, if the abuser sees materials on the subject, the safety of the client could be jeopardized. o If the client does not want the referral materials, WIC staff can offer to write down telephone numbers or addresses for the clients.

Staff must have information available on domestic violence service providers in their area. Domestic Violence resources for DC residents can be found on the Metropolitan Police Department’s web page at https://mpdc.dc.gov/page/domestic-violence-resources

III. Child Abuse Everyone Has an Obligation to Report Child Sex Abuse Under District of Columbia law (see D.C. Code §22-3020.52[a]), any person 18 or older who knows, or has reasonable cause to believe, that a child under the age of 16 is a victim of sexual abuse must immediately report such knowledge or belief to the police (911) or the DC Child and Family Services Agency (202-671-7233). Reporting Child Abuse or Neglect DC requires “mandated reporters” who interact with children up to age 16 on a regular basis to complete training on the signs of child abuse and neglect, and to make reports to the Child and Family Services Administration. See be below for more information on mandated reporters.

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.021 - 2 How Can WIC Help?

Sometimes, people fear that reporting child abuse or neglect will destroy a family. The truth is that getting help can protect children from further harm and assist the family in overcoming problems.

Staff should be familiar with the following signs of child abuse and neglect: • Infants excessive crying or with developmental delay • Unexplained bruising, burns, or welts in different stages of healing • Red flags with injuries: o Explanation of injury doesn’t fit as to pattern, timing, or developmental ability of child o Explanation keeps changing o Delay in seeking medical care o Repeated injuries of any kind • Malnutrition • Poor hygiene, matted hair, dirty skin, or body odor

If staff have reason to suspect child abuse or neglect, they are encouraged to make a confidential phone call to the District hotline at (202)-671-7233.

A trained hotline worker will ask for: • The name, address, age, and gender of the child. • Who is caring for the child and whether other children live in the home. • The nature and extent of the abuse or neglect, as you know it—and any previous abuse or neglect you know about. • Any additional information that may be helpful.

Staff should not document making this phone call in the participant’s HANDS record.

Resources to Learn More About Child Abuse and Reporting

DC’s Child and Family Services Agency: https://cfsa.dc.gov/service/report-child-abuse-and-neglect

Office of the Attorney General for the District of Columbia: https://oag.dc.gov/public-safety/reporting-child-abuse-what-know

Stanford Medicine https://childabuse.stanford.edu/screening/signs.html

VIII. Certification December 2021 8.021 - 3 Helpful information about mandated reporting in the District

Mandated Reporters Must Report All Child Abuse or Neglect Mandatory reporting requirements help protect children from harmful situations and ensure that law enforcement officials and social workers can immediately begin investigating. In addition to the general obligation to report suspected sexual abuse, DC law also requires certain people who regularly work with children to be “mandated reporters” for suspected child abuse or neglect of any kind and for certain other injuries to children under the age of 18 (see below). This means they have a legal obligation to report any kind of suspected mistreatment of children to law enforcement and social services immediately and without delay.

Who Is a Mandated Reporter? Mandated reporters are defined by law (see D.C. Code §4-1321.02) as people who must report suspicions of child physical or sexual abuse or neglect. These are people who work in certain professions where they come into regular close contact with children, such as: • School officials, teachers, and athletic coaches; • Department of Parks and Recreation employees; • Public housing resident managers; • Social service workers; • Daycare workers; • Persons involved in the care and treatment of patients, including: physicians, psychologists, medical examiners, dentists, chiropractors, registered nurses, and licensed practical nurses; • Law-enforcement officers; • Humane officer of any agency charged with the enforcement of animal cruelty laws; • Child and Family Services Agency employees, agents and contractors; • Human trafficking counselors as defined in D.C. Code §14-311(2); • Domestic violence counselors as defined in D.C. Code §14-310(a)(2); and • Mental health professionals as defined in D.C. Code §7-1201.01(11). When and What Kind of Information Must Mandated Reports Provide to Authorities? Mandated reporters must report when they know or suspect that a child whom they have encountered through their professional work: • Is being neglected (his or her parent or guardian is not providing adequate housing, food, clothing, hygiene) • Is being abused (physically or mentally) • Is being exposed to domestic violence • Is in imminent danger of being abused due to the abuse of a sibling or other child living in the same household • Has a parent who is intoxicated, incarcerated, or suffering from a fault in their mental or physical capacity (i.e. drug use or mental illness) and is unable or unwilling to provide care • Is being regularly exposed to illegal drug activity • Has been or is in immediate danger of being the victim of sexual abuse or attempted sexual abuse; is a victim of human trafficking; or has been injured by a bullet, a knife or other sharp object by non-accidental means – regardless of whether the perpetrator was a family member, acquaintance, or stranger

body:
DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.001 1 | P a g e Title: Food Benefit Overview Category: Food Delivery CFR Reference 7 CFR § 246.12 Policy Number: 9.001 Effective Date: 04/2022 Revised Date: 8/15/2023

POLICY STATEMENT The State Agency is responsible for the financial management of, and accountability for, the food delivery system utilized in the DC WIC program.

The Local Agency is responsible for the issuance, inventory, and security of the food delivery instruments (i.e. eWIC cards) in accordance with DC WIC policy 9.003 Food Benefit Security and for educating DC WIC participants on food benefit use and security.

PROCEDURE The Local Agency will utilize the MIS to issue food delivery instruments and food benefits for DC WIC participants.

eWIC Card Issuance Once a participant is deemed eligible for WIC, the Local Agency must issue an initial eWIC card to the Authorized Representative (AR). The AR must sign indicating that they received their initial eWIC card. Only one eWIC card is issued per Family ID (FID).

The Local Agency staff must instruct the AR on: • eWIC card PIN security, including to not write the PIN on the eWIC card • How an eWIC card account can become locked • How to reset the PIN • How and where to shop for WIC approved foods using the eWIC card • How to determine family benefits balance • How to report the eWIC card as lost or stolen and how to request a new eWIC card (see below)

Lost/Stolen eWIC Cards A lost or stolen eWIC card may be replaced via three methods: the Interactive Voice Response (IVR), visiting their WIC clinic, or visiting www.ebtedge.com.

IVR The IVR can be used by calling the number on the back of the eWIC card (877-559-0912). The AR can • report the eWIC card as lost or stolen • change their PIN • lock their eWIC card • deactivate their eWIC card • request a replacement eWIC card. Once requested, the previous eWIC card will be inactivated. A replacement eWIC card is delivered to participants via USPS and can take up to 7 days to be delivered.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.001 2 | P a g e

Visiting the WIC clinic The AR may visit their WIC clinic to request a new eWIC card. When the AR arrives, the Local Agency staff must: • Verify the identity of the AR in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.003 Physical Presence and Identification. • Verify the current eWIC card associated with the FID (i.e. check if the eWIC card has already been deactivated or if the eWIC card is locked). o eWIC cards that have been deactivated require the AR to select a new PIN. • Issue a replacement eWIC card; informing the AR that any prior eWIC cards are no longer active and cannot be reactivated. • Review with the AR the PIN: o If the previous eWIC card was not deactivated (i.e. only replaced) – the previous PIN is still associated with the new card. o If the previous eWIC card was deactivated – the AR will need to select a new PIN.

*A note on deactivated eWIC cards – the option to deactivate an eWIC card may be appropriate if the AR knows the eWIC card is with an unauthorized user and does not want benefits to be used until a new eWIC card can be obtained by the AR, or if the AR is transferring their WIC participation to another State.

EbtEdge The AR may visit www.ebtedge.com to: • report the eWIC card as lost or stolen • change their PIN • lock their eWIC card • deactivate their eWIC card • request a replacement eWIC card. Once requested, the previous eWIC card will be deactivated. A replacement eWIC card is delivered to participants via USPS and can take up to 7 days to be delivered.

Mailing of eWIC Cards The Local Agency may replace an eWIC card by mail if the AR is unable to come to the WIC clinic. The Local Agency must verify the identity of the AR in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.003 Physical Presence / Identification before the replacement card can be mailed.

The Local Agency will cover the cost of mailing replacement cards. When replacing an eWIC card by mail, the Local Agency must: • Inform the AR that they may continue to use their PIN only if the card was replaced and not deactivated (see above – Visiting the WIC clinic). o If deactivated, inform the AR that they can set a new PIN by calling IVR, visiting www.ebtedge.com or coming to the WIC clinic. • Verify the AR’s mailing address. • Place in an envelope that prevents the identification of the eWIC card • Stamp/write clearly “DO NOT FORWARD – RETURN TO SENDER” on the front of the envelope.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.001 3 | P a g e

Food Benefit Issuance The CPA/CPPA must tailor and issue food benefits to the participant based on nutritional risk and dietary assessment in accordance with DC WIC policies 2.003 Nutrition and Breastfeeding Assessment and 2.004 Determining Nutritional Risk. Food benefits may be issued on a monthly, bimonthly, or trimonthly basis. Food benefits may be issued remotely in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.003A Hybrid Services.

The Local Agency must provide food benefit education to the AR/AAR on: • DC WIC authorized foods list and DC WIC authorized vendors and how to identify authorized vendors (this information can be found at www.dcwic.org/wic-families ). • The Family Balance Summary; the quantity of foods issued to the participant(s); aggregated benefits if more than one participant in the FID; first date to use (FDTU) and the last date to use (LDTU) of benefits. • How to check their current food benefit balance via: o the EzWIC app o www.ebtedge.com o IVR o Calling the WIC clinic o Requesting the cashier to print off a receipt of their food benefit balance at an authorized vendor (the AR will need to swipe the card for this to print). • eWIC card security – anyone with the eWIC card and PIN can use it as ID is not checked at the POS at authorized DC WIC stores. • Food benefits cannot be exchanged for cash, non-authorized food items, or credit in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.015 Violations and Sanctions. • The PIN must be entered prior to completing the eWIC transaction. • Prior to completing the transaction, the cashier will hand the eWIC card user a mid-transaction receipt that lists the food items to be deducted from the food benefit balance on their eWIC card. • The receipt received after the completed transaction will list the remaining food benefit balance for that month’s benefit cycle. Frequency of Food Benefit Issuance The Local Agency may only issue eWIC cards and food benefits during established clinic hours. The Local Agency must issue food benefits in accordance with DC WIC policy 9.002 Accountability of Food Benefits.

Early Issuance The Local Agency may issue benefits prior to the FDTU to accommodate participant availability but must educate the AR that food benefits cannot be redeemed prior to the FDTU.

Mid-Benefit Cycle Issuance The Local Agency may adjust food benefits for a participant mid-cycle (i.e. a date in between the FDTU And LDTU) and in accordance with DC WIC policy 9.005 Food Package Responsibilities:

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.001 4 | P a g e • Voiding/reissuing food benefits - The Local Agency staff can void the food benefits, tailor the food package, and reissue food benefits only if none of the food benefits have been redeemed for the current month. • Adding formula to food benefits – If partial food benefits have been redeemed for the current month, depending on the type of food adjustment needed, the Local Agency may add a special formula or WIC-eligible nutritional by utilizing the “Add Formula” button on the Family Balance Screen in this MIS. • Contacting WIC Service Desk – in special cases, the WIC Service Desk can adjust food benefits for a participant mid-cycle. Examples include when new food benefits are medically warranted or in cases of a change in custody. See DC WIC policy 3.002 Help Desk Procedures for contacting the WIC Service Desk.

Missed Appointments and Food Package Proration (Late Pickup) The Local Agency must make reasonable efforts to ensure a participant attends their scheduled appointment. Food benefits cannot be withheld for a participant who attended their initial certification appointment but did not attend a subsequent nutrition education appointment in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.007 Nutrition Education Choice.

A “late pickup” or issuance of food benefits after the FDTU for a participant will not result in a prorated food package.

Food Benefits Expungement Any food benefits remaining on the eWIC card on the LDTU can be redeemed up until 11:59:59 PM (local time). Any remaining food benefits will be expunged by the EBT processor after this time.

Changes in Custody WIC food benefits are aggregated when more than one participant is issued benefits within the same FID. If a participant is transferred to a new FID, benefits are de-aggregated and transferred with the participant to the new FID. If the participant is transferring to a FID that has not previously been issued an eWIC card, the Local Agency staff must follow procedures for issuing an eWIC card as outlined previously (se above – eWIC Card Issuance). See examples for guidance:

Issue a new eWIC card: If the participant has food benefits remaining for the month, they will receive a prorated package automatically calculated by HANDS to sync with the new family’s benefit dates (FDTU and LDTU).

Multiple cards for an Authorized Representative: An AR with multiple foster children enrolled in WIC has the option to request that each child have their own eWIC card assigned to them. In this case, benefits are not aggregated for the family. To do this, the Local Agency staff will need to create a unique FID for each child. The AR may use the same PIN for each card.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.001 5 | P a g e

Example of the eWIC Card The State Agency reserves the right to change the design of the food instrument based on Program needs.

Front of Card • eWIC card number assigned to family

Back of Card • Signature panel (no signature required) • Participant portal web address • Interactive Voice Response (IVR) toll-free number: 1-877-559-0912

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.001 6 | P a g e REFERENCES 7 CFR § 246.12 DC WIC policies 2.003 Nutrition and Breastfeeding Assessment, 2.004 Determining Nutritional Risk, 2.007 Nutrition Education Choice, 3.002 Help Desk Procedures, 8.003 Physical Presence / Identification, 8.015 Violations and Sanctions, 9.002 Accountability of Food Benefits, 9.003 Food Benefit Security, 9.005 Food Package Responsibilities DC WIC attachment 8.003A Hybrid Services

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.002 1 | P a g e Title: Replacement of Food Benefits Category: Food Delivery CFR Reference 7 CFR 246.12(bb)(2) Policy Number 9.002 Effective Date 6/15/2026 Revised Date

POLICY STATEMENT: WIC participants needing a replacement of full or partial food benefits prior to their current Last-Date- To-Use (LDTU) must meet one of the following criteria to have food benefits reissued to their eWIC account: • Impacted by a disaster event or a declared emergency event • Change in custody for a WIC participant • Medically warranted (and documented) change of food benefits • Lost, stolen, or damaged WIC foods documented with appropriate documentation (see below for additional guidance) Any request to replace purchased WIC food benefits after the LDTU will not be authorized. All requests for food benefit replacements must be approved by the State Agency. In accordance with 7 CFR 246.12(bb)(2), all approved requests for the replacement of EBT cards and the transfer of participant benefit balances must be completed within no more than seven business days following notice by the participant or Authorized Representative to the State Agency. PROCEDURE Local Agency staff will ensure that one of the following scenarios applies to request a replacement for current WIC food benefits: Disaster or Declared Emergency Event The need for a replacement of purchased WIC food benefits during a disaster or declared emergency event will be considered on a case-by-case basis. The WIC participant or Authorized Representative (AR) must submit a written request to info.wic@dc.gov and the State Agency will coordinate efforts to reissue WIC food benefits lost due to a disaster event or declared emergency event if determined appropriate. See DC WIC Emergency Plan for more details. Change in Custody Documentation of the change of custody for the WIC participant must be provided in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.008 Eligibility Special Cases. Once documentation is provided, Local Agency staff may complete the participant transfer to the new Family ID (FID) and, if needed, issue an eWIC card to the new AR (see DC WIC policy 8.012 Authorized Representatives). Food benefits may be prorated for the current month if the participant is transferring to an existing FID in the MIS (based on the existing family’s LDTU). See DC WIC policy 9.001 Food Benefit Issuance Overview for more details. Medically Warranted Change of Food Benefits If a WIC participant has a completed DC WIC Medical Prescription Form and/or other acceptable documentation provided by a healthcare provider in accordance with 9.008 Qualifying Medical Conditions, then Local Agency staff may contact the State Agency to request a reissuance of food benefits to the participant’s account. If the request is related to a change in formula, the AR must return

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.002 2 | P a g e the purchased formula to their WIC clinic and staff are to follow the procedures under “Exchange of Purchased Formula” below. Lost, Stolen, or Damaged WIC foods An AR or participant reporting lost, stolen, or damaged purchased WIC foods must provide documentation of the event or circumstances leading to the loss of WIC foods for a reissuance of benefits to be considered. Examples of acceptable documentation include a police report or statement, insurance claim, or other documentation that may be considered on a case-by-case basis. These items must be sent to the State Agency at info.wic@dc.gov. Miscellaneous Scenarios Additional scenarios may exist that prompt a request to replace or adjust food benefits during the current benefit cycle, including the following: Breastfeeding status change Mother-infant food packages typically cannot be adjusted during the current month’s benefit cycle if partial food benefits have been redeemed, unless medically warranted. A request to add additional amounts of formula to the infant’s food package will not be approved unless the infant has a qualifying medical condition (see DC WIC policy 9.008 Qualifying Medical Conditions). Food package tailoring error If a CPA/CPPA mistakenly tailor a participant’s food package and partial food benefits have been redeemed, the State Agency may approve requests to adjust the participant’s food package. Please note that this can only be accommodated for partial food benefit redemption. If the food item from which the tailoring mistake was made has been redeemed for the month (e.g. a request to add yogurt if all the participant’s milk benefit has been redeemed) then the request cannot be approved. EXCHANGE OF PURCHASED FORMULA For a participant that has purchased their formula food benefit in the current month’s benefit cycle and needs an exchange to a different formula due to medical, dietary, and/or environmental concern (i.e. product safety or recall, contaminated water supply, etc), staff should ensure the following: 1. The staff member speaks with the AR to validate the need for formula exchange and then refers the participant to the appropriate WIC staff member as needed (i.e. CPA for medical or dietary concerns, DBE for breastfeeding concerns, etc). 2. The staff member informs the AR that an exchange for the purchased formula can be completed only if the AR returns all unopened cans/containers to their WIC clinic prior to the LDTU. The staff member and AR must sign attachment 9.002B Returned Formula Form that details the type and amount of formula returned. This form must be scanned into the participant’s record. 3. Once the AR has returned all unopened cans/containers of formula, the staff member may send a request to the State Agency to request a reissuance of the formula amount returned to the clinic onto the participant’s account. 4. The Local Agency ensures the returned formula is discarded per attachment 9.002A Processing Returned Formula. REFERENCES WIC Policy Memorandum #2020-1

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.003 1 | P a g e Title: Food Benefit Security Category: Food Delivery CFR Reference: CFR 246.12 Policy Number: 9.003 Effective Date: 1/2022 Revised Date: 1/31/2026

POLICY STATEMENT: The State Agency is responsible for the ordering and distribution of food instruments, i.e. eWIC cards, to the Local Agency and will maintain a backstock supply for emergency distribution and/or other program operations (e.g. vendor monitoring/compliance buys). The Local Agency must maintain an inventory of eWIC cards and ensure these items are kept secure from theft and loss. The Local Agency must report its eWIC card inventory to the State Agency on a quarterly basis. PROCEDURE State Agency Ordering of eWIC Cards DC WIC’s eWIC card supplier and distributor are Custom Data Processing (CDP) and Fidelity National Information Services, Inc (FIS), respectfully. Orders are processed through CDP and fulfilled through FIS. Purchasing eWIC cards from CDP entails the following: Quantities for Ordering • eWIC cards are packaged in quantities of 250 per sleeve and are purchased in increments of 250, with a minimum purchase order of 500 cards (i.e. two sleeves). • Orders for less than 5,000 cards are processed and shipped within 5 to 10 business days. • Orders for more than 5,000 cards are considered Large Order Files (LOF) and require advanced notice. o For LOFs, the State Agency must coordinate with CDP to contact FIS State Support o FIS State Support will coordinate with CardPro to identify a date when CDP can send the card file ▪ CardPro requires 30-day notice for LOFs ▪ CardPro typically processes and ships purchase orders within 5 to 10 business days Requesting eWIC cards The Local Agency must communicate in advance to the State Agency its need for additional eWIC cards to ensure that ordering and shipping of supplies can be accommodated within the established timeframes listed above. The Local Agency must request additional eWIC cards when the designated WIC clinic site has a minimum of three unissued card sleeves. The State Agency will review eWIC card issuance and replacement data in HANDS to verify that the request is justified. CDP Shipping Notes • CDP uses the United Postal Service (UPS) for shipping requests • Packages do not require a signature upon delivery

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.003 2 | P a g e Local Agency Responsibilities The Local Agency must ensure the following for inventorying its eWIC cards: Security of eWIC cards The Local Agency must designate one of its WIC clinic sites as its main location for storing and distributing unopened eWIC card sleeves to its remaining WIC clinic locations as a measure to prevent the loss and theft of these items. The designated WIC clinic must have a locked safe where the cards are stored and kept secured from the public and unauthorized staff. This location should be specified on the eWIC card inventory log. The State Agency recommends that the remaining WIC clinic sites maintain only two sleeves of eWIC cards at a time – one to be used for distribution within the clinic and the other to remain unopened as an inventory backup. These sleeves must also be protected from loss and theft by securing them in a locked safe at the WIC clinic site. Daily eWIC card inventorying at each WIC clinic site Daily inventory of eWIC cards must be performed at each of the Local Agency’s WIC clinic sites to include the number of: • opened sleeves with the number of individual eWIC cards remaining within that sleeve, and • unopened sleeves This data will be used to assist in tracking and accounting for the fiscal year eWIC card inventory log that must be submitted to the State Agency on a quarterly basis. The Daily eWIC Card Inventory Log (see attachment 9.003A) requires daily documentation of all cards removed and returned and includes an end-of-month audit conducted by someone other than the card remover or returner. The auditor must complete the review and sign off within three (3) business days following the close of the month. The Local Agency Director must review the completed audit and sign off within five (5) business days. The Local Agency is required to maintain all daily eWIC card inventory logs for a minimum of three years for auditing purposes. Fiscal Year eWIC card inventorying at each WIC clinic site The Local Agency Director must use the Fiscal Year eWIC Card Inventory Log (see attachment 9.003B) to maintain monthly counts of unissued, unopened, open and finished sleeves at each of its WIC clinic sites and submit this log to the State Agency each quarter. The end-of-month auditor (attachment 9.003B) must be a different individual than the daily card remover or returner (attachment 9.003A). If staffing constraints require the auditor to also serve as the card remover or returner at a site, a replacement auditor must be assigned if that individual performed daily inventory coverage for more than 15% of the site’s monthly operating hours. REFERENCES

ATTACHMENTS & FORMS 9.003A Daily eWIC Card Inventory Log 9.003B Fiscal Year eWIC Card Inventory Log

Policy 9.004 1 | P a g e Title: Federal Food Packages Category: Food Delivery CFR Reference: 246.10 Policy Number 9.004 Effective Date 4/2022 Revised Date: 03/01/2026

POLICY STATEMENT The State Agency is responsible for ensuring that all federally authorized WIC supplemental foods are available in quantities that meet and do not exceed the Maximum Monthly Allowances (MMAs) to DC WIC participants established by the seven federal WIC food packages in accordance with 7 CFR 246.10(e). A Food Package Committee at the State Agency determines which foods shall be authorized for inclusion in the DC WIC Approved Food List. Each authorized supplemental food must align with the federal minimum requirements and nutrition specifications in accordance with 7 CFR 246.10(e)(12). The Local Agency is responsible for ensuring each WIC participant receives the appropriate federal food package based on category and nutritional risk as part of performing a comprehensive nutrition and breastfeeding assessment in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.003 Nutrition and Breastfeeding Assessment. DEFINITIONS Maximum Monthly Allowance – MMA; the maximum quantity of any WIC supplemental food that can be assigned to a participant each month based on the seven federal food packages. Supplemental foods- each federally authorized food item available in DC WIC for issuance to participants. Examples include whole grains, yogurt, infant cereal, and cow’s milk. PROCEDURE The seven federal food packages are described below and may only be assigned to WIC participants by a CPA or CPPA that meets the categorical and/or nutritional risk requirements in accordance with DC WIC policies 8.001 Certification Overview and 9.008 Qualifying Medical Conditions.

Though only a CPA or CPPA may tailor a food package for a participant, additional staff roles (i.e. Nutrition Education Technicians or Administrative Clerks) may be allowed at the Local Agency’s discretion to issue food benefits onto a participant’s account.

Each authorized DC WIC participant category and their allowable supplemental food substitution options can be found in DC WIC policies 9.005 Infant Food Packages, 9.006 Children Food Packages, 9.007 Women Food Packages, and 9.008 Qualifying Medical Conditions.

ADDITIONAL FOOD PACKAGE CONSIDERATIONS Food package tailoring in the MIS defaults to issuing the MMA for each supplemental food category. The CPA or CPPA may tailor and issue amounts less than the MMA if: - It is medically or nutritionally appropriate (e.g. removing a food item due to an allergy) - A participant requests to receive less than the MMA for a food item - The quantities necessary to supplement another program’s contribution to fill a medical prescription would be less than the MMA (e.g. a participant is receiving assistance on infant formula from another food program).

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.005 1 | P a g e Title: Infant Food Packages Category: Food Delivery CFR Reference: 7 CFR 246.10 Policy Number: 9.005 Effective Date: 04/2022 Revised Date: 11/17/2025

POLICY STATEMENT: The State Agency will make available in the MIS infant food packages based on infant age and categories (see DC WIC policy 8.004 Categorical Eligibility) that allow up to the Monthly Maximum Allowance (MMA)* of authorized infant foods in accordance with 7 CFR 246.10(b)(2)(ii). Each infant will receive a tailored food package based on a breastfeeding and nutrition assessment conducted in accordance with DC WIC policy 2.003 Nutrition and Breastfeeding Assessment. Mother- infant dyads must have corresponding categories that best characterize the infant’s feeding status. *See DC WIC policy 9.004 Federal Food Packages for definition of MMA. DEFINITIONS Mother Infant Dyad – refers to the WIC participant category assignment of a mother to her infant based on infant feeding status. A mother infant dyad must have corresponding participant categories for a singleton birth (e.g. a PN category for a woman must have an infant assigned IPN). Standard Contract Infant Formula – refers to the milk-based and soy-based infant formulas offered in DC WIC as part of the program’s foods cost containment contracts in accordance with 7 CFR 246.16a. Noncontract Infant Formulas – refers to all other infant formula offerings in DC WIC intended to meet the nutritional and medical needs of WIC participants that are not included in the program’s food cost containment contracts in accordance with 7 CFR 246.16a. PROCEDURE The CPA or CPPA must provide each infant with a tailored food package based on the MMAs established for each infant age range and category: Infant Exclusively Nursing (IEN) (Fully Breastfeeding) For infants fully breastfeeding, the following food packages, including food items and amounts, are available based on the infant’s age at the time of issuance:

Federal Food Package I (0-5 Months) Federal Food Package II (6-11 Months) Infant Cereal N/A – infants fully breastfeeding do not receive any WIC foods 16 oz Infant Fruits and Vegetables* 128 oz Infant Meats 40 oz *CVB may be substituted in place of jarred infant fruits and vegetables at either 64 oz for $11 or 128 oz for $22. Monthly CVB amounts may be adjusted annually.

Infant Partially Nursing (IPN) (Mostly Breastfeeding) For infants partially nursing (mostly), the following food packages, including food items and amounts, are available based on the infant’s age at the time of issuance:

Federal Food Package I (0-3 Months) Federal Food Package I (4-5 Months) Federal Food Package II (6-11 Months) Infant Formula May receive up to: • 388 fl oz reconstituted liquid concentrate, or • 384 fl oz RTF, or • 435 fl oz reconstituted powder May receive up to: • 460 fl oz reconstituted liquid concentrate, or • 474 fl oz RTF, or • 522 fl oz reconstituted powder May receive up to: • 315 fl oz reconstituted liquid concentrate, or • 474 fl oz RTF, or 522 fl oz reconstituted powder Infant Cereal N/A N/A 8 oz Infant Fruits and Vegetables* N/A N/A 128 oz *CVB may be substituted in place of jarred infant fruits and vegetables at either 64 oz for $11 or 128 oz for $22. Monthly CVB amounts may be adjusted annually.

Infant Partially Nursing (IPN+) (Some Breastfeeding) For infants partially nursing (some), the following food packages, including food items and amounts, are available based on the infant’s age at the time of issuance:

Federal Food Package I (0-3 Months) Federal Food Package I (4-5 Months) Federal Food Package II (6-11 Months) Infant Formula May receive up to: • 823 fl oz reconstituted liquid concentrate, or • 832 fl oz RTF, or • 870 fl oz reconstituted powder May receive up to: • 884 fl oz reconstituted liquid concentrate, or • 913 fl oz RTF, or • 960 fl oz reconstituted powder May receive up to: • 630 fl oz reconstituted liquid concentrate, or • 643 fl oz RTF, or • 696 fl oz reconstituted powder Infant Cereal N/A N/A 8 oz Infant Fruits and Vegetables* N/A N/A 128 oz *CVB may be substituted in place of jarred infant fruits and vegetables at either 64 oz for $11 or 128 oz for $22. Monthly CVB amounts may be adjusted annually.

Infant Formula Fed (IFF) For infants’ formula-fed, the following food packages, including food items and amounts, are available based on the infant’s age at the time of issuance:

Federal Food Package I (0-3 Months) Federal Food Package I (4-5 Months) Federal Food Package II (6-11 Months) Infant Formula May receive up to: • 823 fl oz reconstituted liquid concentrate, or • 832 fl oz RTF, or • 870 fl oz reconstituted powder May receive up to: • 884 fl oz reconstituted liquid concentrate, or • 913 fl oz RTF, or • 960 fl oz reconstituted powder May receive up to: • 630 fl oz reconstituted liquid concentrate, or • 643 fl oz RTF, or • 696 fl oz reconstituted powder Infant Cereal N/A N/A 8 oz

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.005 3 | P a g e Infant Fruits and Vegetables* N/A N/A 128 oz *CVB may be substituted in place of jarred infant fruits and vegetables at either 64 oz for $11 or 128 oz for $22. Monthly CVB amounts may be adjusted annually.

INFANT FORMULA ISSUANCE DC WIC authorizes several types of infant formulas in powdered, liquid concentrate, and/or ready-to- feed (RTU/RTF) forms that support the nutritional and medical needs of DC WIC participants. Authorized infant formulas are classified as one of the following: • Standard contract infant formulas • Non-contract infant formulas: o Includes DC WIC-authorized exempt infant formulas (see DC WIC policy 9.008 Qualifying Medical Conditions), and o Competitive infant formulas that may be available on a limited and temporary basis A listing of all currently authorized DC WIC formulas and their classifications can be found in the DC WIC Formula Guide. Standard Contract Infant Formulas Standard contract infant formulas authorized in DC WIC may be issued without a DC Medical Prescription Form to any infant with an assigned category of IFF, IPN+, or IPN in powdered or liquid concentrate form by a CPA or CPPA. Ready-to-feed (RTF) Formulas RTU/RTF formulas may only be authorized by a CPA and must meet one of the following conditions in accordance with 7 CFR 246.10(e)(1)(iv): • The participant’s household has an unsanitary or restricted water supply or poor refrigeration; • The person caring for the participant may have difficulty in correctly diluting concentrated or powdered forms; or • The WIC infant formula is only available in RTU/RTF. The CPA must document the justification for issuing a RTU/RTF formula in the participant’s record. Non-Contract Infant Formulas Non-contract infant formulas available in DC WIC may be assigned by a CPA when one of the following conditions applies: a. Religious Beliefs – a participant who cannot use a standard contract infant formula due to religious reasons or other circumstances may be issued a non-contract comparable infant formula. The CPA must contact the State Agency for approval and document the exception in the participant’s TGIF note.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.005 4 | P a g e b. Qualifying Medical Condition – a participant with a qualifying medical condition (see DC WIC policy 9.008 Qualifying Medical Conditions) may receive an exempt infant formula with the completion of a DC WIC Medical Prescription Form and approval by a CPA. Tailoring Infant Formula for Partially Nursing Infants Partially nursing infants (IPN or IPN+ categories) must have food packages tailored and issued that meet but do not exceed the infant’s daily formula needs. CPA/CPPAs must conduct a comprehensive nutrition and breastfeeding assessment that ensures the following: 1. The CPA/CPPA identifies the frequency of infant formula and breastfeeding intake in a 24-hour period and probes the infant’s caretaker on formula preparation methods (e.g. formula type and mixing ratios, bottle heating, bottle cleaning, formula storage, etc). 2. The CPA/CPPA identifies the mother’s breastfeeding goals and provides appropriate education, anticipatory guidance, and/or breastfeeding support to help her achieve these goals. Staff may reference the WIC Breastfeeding Check-In Tool to provide breastfeeding education and support information. 3. The CPA/CPPA calculates the total amount of formula the infant receives in a 24-hour period and determines the amount of formula to issue based on the DC WIC Formula Tailoring Guide (see below). 4. The CPA/CPPA tailors the infant’s food package to reflect the above formula calculation and provides food benefit education to the Authorized Representative (AR) in accordance with 9.001 Food Benefit Issuance Overview. MOTHER-INFANT DYAD CATEGORY CHANGES For a mother-infant dyad with a change in breastfeeding status, staff must ensure the following to complete the category change: 1. The CPA/CPPA probe to determine the change in breastfeeding and/or categorical status* and document this information accordingly on the infant’s Breastfeeding Surveillance Tab in HANDS. 2. The CPA/CPPA identify the new corresponding infant/mother categories that best characterize the infant’s feeding status and update the category on the Cert Tab in HANDS for the infant and mother**. 3. The CPA/CPPA reviews the category changes with the participants including updates to the certification period(s), appropriate risk codes, and food packages. Please note that food packages typically cannot be adjusted for mother-infant dyads during the current month’s benefit cycle if partial benefits have been redeemed. See DC WIC policies 9.001 Food Benefit Issuance Overview and 9.002 Replacement of Food Benefits for more details. *For a postpartum woman with an active certification that is now pregnant, staff must complete a new certification reflecting her pregnancy status in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.001 Certification Overview. ** For an infant 6 months or older who is no longer breastfed, staff only need to update the infant’s category, risk codes, and food package. The infant’s mother will no longer be considered categorically

Policy 9.005 5 | P a g e eligible and will be terminated from the program. Additionally, PN+ (Some Breastfeeding) participants are no longer eligible to receive a food package at 6 months postpartum but continue to receive breastfeeding support and participant-centered nutrition education, up to one year postpartum.

Policy 9.006 1 | P a g e Title: Children Food Packages Category: Food Delivery CFR Reference: 246.10 Policy Number 9.006 Effective Date: 3/2022 Revised Date: 03/01/2026

POLICY STATEMENT: The State Agency will make available in the MIS children food packages based on the child’s age that allow up to the Maximum Monthly Allowance (MMA)* of authorized supplemental foods in accordance with 7 CFR 246.10(e)(4). PROCEDURE The CPA or CPPA must provide each child with a tailored food package based on the MMAs established and allowable substitutions for each age and category below: Child 1-year-old (C1) Authorized Supplemental Food Food Package IV, Part A Juice 64 fl oz full substitution: - $3 CVB Whole milk 4 gallons (i.e. 16 quarts) partial substitutions: - 1 lb of cheese (in place of 3 quarts of milk) - Up to 64 oz of yogurt* (32 oz per 1 quart of milk) - Up to 4 quarts of kefir (1 quart of kefir per 1 quart of milk) full substitutions: - 1 lb of tofu for each quart of milk - Any additional authorized milk (e.g. dry powdered milk, lactose-free, soy, goat’s milk, UHT milk, etc) for each quart of milk** Breakfast cereal 36 oz Eggs 1 dozen full substitution: - 1 lb of tofu or - 1 CTR of dry or canned beans, peas, lentils, or 16 to 18 of peanut butter or nut or seed butter Fruits and vegetables $26*** CVB Whole wheat bread or other whole grain option 24 oz Canned fish 6 oz Mature legumes 1 lb dry beans or 64 oz canned beans or 1 CTR of 16 to 18 oz peanut butter or nut and seed butters

Policy 9.006 2 | P a g e WIC formula (see DC WIC policy 9.008) Up to 455 fl oz of liquid concentrate (powdered and RTF may be substituted at equivalent rates). *Yogurt – whole fat or low-fat yogurts are standard issuance when substituting yogurt. Nonfat yogurt may be issued to 1-year-old children for whom overweight or obesity is a concern as determined by a CPA **Authorized milk – see a full listing of authorized milks in the DC WIC Authorized Foods List *** CVB amounts may be adjusted annually.

Reduced-fat milk issuance to 1-year-olds Reduced fat (2%) milks can be issued to 1-year old children only when determined appropriate by a CPA. The need for reduced fat milk must be based on an individual nutritional assessment and if issued, must be documented in the participant’s TGIF note. A DC WIC Medical Prescription form is not required to issue reduced-fat milk to 1-year-olds as part of Food Package IV, Part A. Nonfat yogurt issuance to 1-year-olds Nonfat yogurt may be issued to 1-year-old children only when determined appropriate by a CPA. The need for nonfat yogurt must be based on an individual nutritional assessment and if issued, must be documented in the participant’s TGIF. A DC WIC Medical Prescription form is not required to issue nonfat yogurt to 1-year-olds as part of Food Package IV, Part A. Additional food package tailoring options for 1-year-olds Additional food item tailoring options may be considered as part of Food Package III issuance including infant fruits and vegetables, infant cereal, and special formula as determined appropriate by a healthcare provider per medical documentation. Whole fat yogurt may be authorized per medical documentation by a healthcare provider. **Authorized milk – see a full listing of authorized milks in the DC WIC Authorized Foods List *** CVB amounts may be adjusted annually.

Whole milk issuance to 2 to 4-year-olds Whole milk may be issued to 2 to 4-year-olds in place of low-fat and nonfat milk only when determined appropriate by a healthcare provider per medical documentation and must be assigned as part of Food Package III (see DC WIC policy 9.008 Qualifying Medical Conditions). Reduced-fat milk (2%) issuance to 2 to 4-year-olds Reduced-fat milk (2%) may be issued to 2 to 4-year-olds in place of low-fat and nonfat milk only as determined, at minimum, by a CPA based on an individual nutritional assessment and its justification documented in the participant’s record. A DC WIC Medical Prescription form is not needed to issue reduced-fat milk as part of Food Package IV, Part B. Additional food package tailoring options for 2 to 4-year olds Additional food tailoring options may be considered as part of Food Package III issuance including infant fruits and vegetables, infant cereal, whole milk yogurt, and special formula as determined appropriate by a healthcare provider per medical documentation. DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.008 1 | P a g e Title: Qualifying Medical Conditions Category: Food Delivery CFR Reference 7 CFR 246.10(e)(3) Policy Number 9.008 Effective Date 3/2022 Revised Date: 11/17/2025

POLICY STATEMENT: The State Agency will make available in the MIS specialized food packages designed to meet the cultural, medical, and dietary needs of participants with qualifying medical conditions that allow up to the Monthly Maximum Allowance (MMA)* of authorized supplemental foods* as part of Food Package III in accordance with 7 CFR 246.10(b)(2)(ii). Food package III may not be issued solely for the purpose of enhancing nutrient intake or managing body weight or for infants whose only condition is a diagnosed formula intolerance or food allergy to lactose, sucrose, milk protein, or soy protein that does not require the use of an exempt infant formula or a non-specific formula or food intolerance (7 CFR 246.10(e)(3)(ii)). *See DC WIC policy 9.004 Federal Food Packages for definition of MMA and supplemental foods. DEFINITIONS Qualifying medical condition – any diagnosed medical condition which requires the issuance of a WIC formula, exempt infant formula, or WIC-eligible nutritional as deemed appropriate by a healthcare provider per medical documentation. Examples include preterm birth, low birth weight, failure to thrive, inborn errors of metabolism and metabolic disorders, gastrointestinal disorders, and severe food allergies. Reconstituted Fluid Ounces (RFO) – the amount of formula prepared from one can or container of formula product when prepared with water according to standard mixing instructions. PROCEDURE Only a CPA may issue a WIC infant formula, noncontract infant formula*, or WIC-eligible nutritional as part of Food Package III with appropriate medical documentation in accordance with 7 CFR 246.10(d) as described below. Required Medical Documentation Any issuance of a WIC infant formula, noncontract infant formula, or WIC-eligible nutritional as part of Food Package III requires a completed DC WIC Medical Prescription Form or other medical documentation form from a licensed healthcare provider with prescriptive authority in the District of Columbia. The following information is required and may be obtained in writing or received verbally (see further guidance on this below): A. The name of the formula or WIC-eligible nutritional being requested, including the amount needed per day (this can be determined by the CPA if indicated as so). B. The authorized supplemental food(s)* appropriate for the qualifying condition(s) and their prescribed amounts. C. Length of time the prescribed WIC formula and/or supplemental food is required by the participant. D. The qualifying condition(s) for issuance of the authorized supplemental food(s).

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.008 2 | P a g e E. Signature, date, and contact information (or name, date, and contact information) if the initial medical documentation was received verbally and the signed document is forthcoming. All medical documentation requesting a formula or WIC-eligible nutritional must be uploaded into the participant’s record. All requests are subject to approval by a CPA. If a medical provider has prescribed a formula or feeding plan that, based upon the nutritional assessment of the CPA is not appropriate or indicated, the CPA should contact the medical provider to discuss alternative options. *See DC WIC policy 9.005 Infant Food Packages for definitions of noncontract infant formula. In accordance with 7 CFR 246.10(d)(4)(iii)(B), medical documentation may be provided by telephone to a CPA who must promptly document the information. The collection of the required information by telephone for medical documentation purposes may only be used until written confirmation is received from a licensed healthcare provider with prescriptive authority and used only when absolutely necessary on an individual participant basis. Written medical documentation must be received no later than 2 weeks after accepting the initial medical documentation by phone. Licensed healthcare providers with prescriptive authority In accordance with District of Columbia Code § 3–1201.02 the following healthcare providers are authorized to complete a DC WIC Medical Prescription Form or other written medical documentation to prescribe WIC authorized foods: • Doctor of Medicine (MD) • Doctor of Osteopathy (DO) • Physician Assistant (PA) • Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist (CRNA) • Certified Nurse-Midwife (CNM) • Certified Nurse-Practitioner (CNP, CRNP, NP, DNP) • Clinical Nurse Specialist (CNS) Hospital discharge forms Hospital discharge forms may be used to prescribe and issue a special formula or WIC-eligible nutritional for up to two months of food benefits. The DC WIC Medical Prescription Form or other completed written medical documentation must then be obtained and uploaded into the participant’s record. Recommended prescription duration length DC WIC recommends that all approved requests for special formula for infants be reassessed at a duration of no greater than three months from issuance. The recommended maximum duration of a prescription for women and children is six months. CPAs may approve special formula and WIC-eligible nutritional requests beyond these ranges as they deem appropriate. Food Package III issuance in HANDS The following food packages descriptions are used to indicate Food Package III issuance in HANDS (i.e. contain special formula or WIC-eligible nutritionals to tailor and issue): Infants (IFF, IPN+, IPN) • Special Formula

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.008 3 | P a g e • No Solid Foods Children and Women (C1, C2, C3, C4, PG1, PG2, P, PN+, PN) • Special with Formula • Formula Only No Solid Foods Packages In lieu of infant foods (cereal, fruit, and vegetables), infants older than 6 months of age in Food Package III may receive WIC formula (infant formula, exempt infant formula, or WIC-eligible nutritionals) at the same MMA as infants ages 4 through 5 months of age of the same feeding option (i.e. fully formula feeding or partially (some) breastfeeding, and partially (mostly) breastfeeding). Children and Women Special with Formula – Additional Tailoring Options For a participant receiving Food Package III, the healthcare provider must indicate which WIC-authorized supplemental foods and their forms (e.g. pureed fruits and vegetables or whole fruits and vegetables) to issue to the participant or indicate that the WIC CPA may determine the supplemental foods, forms, and amounts to issue to the participant on the written medical prescription form. Standard tailoring options for each participant category and accompanying food package can be found in DC WIC policies 9.005 Infant Food Packages, 9.006 Children Food Packages, and 9.007 Women Food Packages. In addition to the standard tailoring options available to each participant category, the following additional tailoring options are available in the “Special with Formula” food packages: Category(s) Additional Food Item Substitution Food Category to Substitute From Children 1-year-old Nonfat yogurt Whole milk Infant cereal Breakfast cereal Infant fruit and vegetable CVB for fruits and vegetable Juice Children 2 to-4-years Pregnant women Postpartum women (all feeding statuses) Whole milk Low-fat or nonfat milk Whole milk yogurt Infant cereal Breakfast cereal Infant fruit and vegetable CVB for fruits and vegetable Juice

DC WIC NONCONTRACT FORMULA TAILORING GUIDE The following tables can assist the CPA in tailoring the amount of powdered formula for participants issued food package III. Ready-to-feed (RTF) formulas should be issued in quantities that match the total amount needed for one month up to the MMA. Exempt Formula and WIC-Eligible Nutritionals - Liquid concentrate and RTF amounts See DC WIC policy 9.005 Infant Food Packages for tailoring guidance on liquid concentrate and RTF formula. Customized Food Package Creation and Issuance Additional formulas and WIC-eligible nutritionals may be available for issuance in DC WIC beyond those listed in this policy and the DC WIC Formula Guide. The CPA should contact the State Agency to assist with food package issuance for any of the following:

Policy 9.008 5 | P a g e 1. A request for a formula or product not currently available as a tailoring option for the participant’s age and category. 2. DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.009 1 | P a g e Title: Food Packages for Homeless Participants Category: Food Delivery CFR Reference 7 CFR 246.10(b)(1)(ii) Policy Number 9.009 Effective Date: 1/2022 Revised Date: 11/17/2025

POLICY STATEMENT: The State Agency will ensure that authorized supplemental foods* and food tailoring options are available to address any food storage and preparation constraints of homeless participants in DC WIC. The Local Agency will ensure that a CPA/CPPA performs a comprehensive nutrition assessment in accordance with 2.003 Nutrition and Breastfeeding Assessment that identifies the cultural, medical, and dietary needs of the participant. For a participant identified as homeless and residing in a homeless facility, the CPA/CPPA must provide food benefit education that supplemental foods issued are for their personal use only and not to be used in a communal setting or belonging to the homeless facility or institution, in accordance with 7 CFR 246.10(b)(2)(ii)(D). *See DC WIC policy 9.004 Federal Food Packages for definition of supplemental foods. PROCEDURE The following food tailoring options can be used to assist the CPA/CPPA in providing food benefit education to homeless participants: Food Item Food tailoring considerations Infant formula - Powdered formulas are shelf-stable and can be prepared as needed. - Powdered formula is preferred for mothers that are partially nursing. - The CPA can determine the need for RTU/RTF formulas if a lack of access to clean water and/or refrigeration is a concern (see DC WIC policy 9.005 for more information). Milk - For storage concerns, the CPA/CPPA can issue milk in smaller package sizes like quarts and half gallons. - If there is a lack of access to refrigeration, DC WIC authorizes UHT milk, powdered milk, and evaporated milk as shelf-stable options. Cheese and yogurt - DC WIC has expanded its allowable package sizes to allow for purchasing of smaller quantities at once. Cheese can be purchased in 8 oz packaging, yogurt can be purchased in 16 oz packaging. Juice - 64 ounce juices authorized in DC WIC are shelf-stable. Eggs - Eggs can be substituted for canned beans or peanut butter or nut or seed butters. Breakfast cereals - DC WIC has expanded its allowable package sizes to allow for purchasing of smaller quantities at once. Breakfast cereals can be purchased in minimum package sizes of 9 ounces up to 36 ounces. Fruits and Vegetables - DC WIC authorizes several forms of fruits and vegetables that allow for flexibility in purchasing including fresh, frozen, canned, and dried.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.009 2 | P a g e Whole wheat bread and whole grains - DC WIC has expanded its allowable whole wheat bread options to include English muffins, bagels, and naan, and has additionally authorized more whole grain options that are shelf-stable (e.g. quinoa, oats, brown rice, etc) Fish - Allowable package sizes range from 2 ounces to 15 ounces, allowing for flexibility in purchasing. Dry beans, canned beans, peanut butter or nut or seed butters - The participant may choose from any of the three options. Each form is shelf stable. Infant foods (cereal, fruit and vegetable, meats) - All approved infant foods are in shelf-stable forms (e.g. jars, pouches, containers, etc).

REFERENCES DC WIC policies 2.003 Nutrition and Breastfeeding Assessment, 9.004 Federal Food Packages, 9.005 Infant Food Packages ATTACHMENTS & FORMS

Policy 9.010 1 | P a g e Title: Authorized Foods List Category: Supplemental Foods CFR Reference: 246.10 Policy Number: 9.010 Effective Date: 01/2021 Revised Date: 6/15/2026

POLICY STATEMENT: The State Agency will develop and maintain a list of authorized foods – the DC WIC Food List – which specifies the types, sizes, and nutrient standards of authorized foods in the DC WIC program. The Food List will be revised and reissued when there is: a. A change in federal program regulations b. Information on new products developed since the issuance of the last Food List c. A product recall, discontinuation, or reformulation resulting in a change of eligibility status The DC WIC Food List can be found online at www.dcwic.org/foods-formulas.

DC WIC FOOD ITEM SPECIFICATIONS The following chart provides food item selection criteria for inclusion on the DC WIC Food List. Food Item Allowed on the DC WIC Food List Cow’s Milk USDA requirements: ▪ Must be pasteurized ▪ Must contain at least: - 400 IU vitamin D per quart (100 IU per cup) - 2000 IU vitamin A per quart (500 IU per cup)

Not Allowed: o Flavored milk o Added protein (ultra skim)

o Any brand o Organic store brands Regular Milk Nonfat, low-fat, reduced-fat, whole o Quarts, half gallons, gallons Lactose-reduced Milk Nonfat, low-fat, reduced-fat, whole o Quarts, half gallons Buttermilk Low-fat or reduced-fat o Quarts, half gallons Evaporated or Powdered Nonfat, low-fat, reduced-fat, whole o 5 oz to 64 oz packages UHT Milk Nonfat, low-fat, reduced-fat, whole o Quarts Kefir milk o Quarts Goat’s Milk

USDA Requirements: ▪ Must be pasteurized ▪ Must contain at least: - 400 IU vitamin D per quart o Fluid goat’s milk, pasteurized, unflavored o Quarts, half gallons o Approved brands only

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.010 2 | P a g e (100 IU per cup) - 2000 IU vitamin A per quart (500 IU per cup) Cheese

USDA requirements: Made from 100% pasteurized milk Not Allowed: o Cheese from in-store deli o Imported cheese (made outside USA)

o Any brand o Organic store brands o 8 oz, 16 oz, 24 oz, 32 oz packages o Monterey Jack, Colby, Cheddar, Swiss, Muenster, Provolone, part-skim or whole Mozzarella, pasteurized processed American, or blends of these o Block, sliced, cubed, shredded, individually wrapped slices, or string cheese

Soy Milk

USDA requirements (per cup): ▪ Must contain ≤10g added sugar ▪ 276 mg calcium ▪ 8 g protein ▪ 500 IU vitamin A ▪ 100 IU vitamin D ▪ 24 mg magnesium ▪ 222 mg phosphorus ▪ 349 mg potassium ▪ 0.44 mg riboflavin ▪ 1.1 mcg vitamin B12

o Approved brands and flavors o Quarts, half gallons

Tofu

USDA requirements: o 100 mg of calcium per 100 g of tofu o No added fats, sugars, oils, or sodium o Any texture (soft or silken, regular, firm, medium firm, extra firm, super firm) o 8 oz, 14 to 16 oz packages Yogurt

Eggs

Not allowed: o Brown or white fresh chicken eggs o Organic store brands only o Cage-free or free-range

USDA Requirements o Must contain at least: - 28mg iron per 100g dry cereal - < 21.2g added sugar per 100g dry cereal

o Hot cereals - ready-to-eat, instant, and regular o Cold cereals - bagged or boxed o 9 oz to 36 oz

Dried or Canned Beans, Peas, Lentils

Not allowed: o Added sugar, fat, oil, meat, fruit or vegetable o Baked beans or bean soups o Green beans or peas – these can be purchased with the Fruit and Vegetable CVB o Any brand o Organics allowed o Regular, low-, or no-sodium allowed o Refried beans allowed with no added fat o Spices or seasonings are allowed o Dried beans, peas, and lentils – 16 oz, 32 oz, 48 oz packages o Canned beans, peas, and lentils – 15 oz to 16 oz packages Peanut Butter

Not allowed: o Add-ins such as jam, jelly, marshmallow, chocolate, honey or other similar ingredients are not allowed

o Any brand o Organic store brands o Creamy, crunchy, chunky, plain or reduced fat/sodium, unsalted forms allowed o 16 oz to 18 oz packages o Low-fat, reduced-fat, or reduced sodium o “Natural” Nut and Seed Butters

Not allowed: o Add-ins such as jam, jelly, marshmallow, chocolate, honey or o Approved brands only – almond butter o Creamy or chunky, regular, or reduced-fat, salted or unsalted forms allowed o Limited brand options for tahini, sunflower seed butter o 16 oz packages

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.010 4 | P a g e other similar ingredients are not allowed

Canned Fish

“Canned’ refers to processed food items in cans or other shelf-stable containers – cans, jars, or pouches are allowed o Any brand o Packed in water or oil o With bones or skin o Added spices, sauces, and flavorings o Regular or low sodium o 2.5 oz to 40 oz packages

Bread and Bread Products

USDA requirements: o Whole wheat must be the primary ingredient by weight o No added sugars, fats, or oils o 100% whole wheat bread, buns, and rolls o Whole grain breads – whole grain must be the primary ingredient by weight o Whole grain bread products – naan, English muffins, pita, bagels o 12 oz to 48 oz packages Whole Grains – Oats

Not allowed: o Added sugars, fats, or oils o Dry, plain whole oats o May be old-fashioned, quick, or instant o 12 oz to 48 oz packages Whole Wheat Pasta

USDA requirement o Whole wheat must be the primary ingredient by weight o No added sugars, fats, or oils o 100% Whole wheat pasta o Dry, plain, any shape o Organic allowed o 12 oz to 48 oz packages Whole Grains - Rice, Barley and Quinoa

Not allowed: Added sugars, fats, oils, or salts

o Any brand o 100% whole grain brown rice or barley o Organics allowed o 12 oz to 48 oz packages Whole Grains – Tortillas

Not allowed: o Added sugars, fats, or oils

o 100% whole wheat tortillas or corn tortillas o Soft tortillas only o 12 oz to 48 oz packages Infant Cereal

USDA requirement: o Must contain at least: - 45 mg iron per 100g dry cereal Not allowed: o Any brand o Organics allowed o Rice, Oatmeal, or Multigrain cereal o 8 oz or 16 oz packages

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.010 5 | P a g e o Added DHA o Added sugar, milk, fruit, or other non-cereal ingredients Infant Food Fruits and Vegetables

Not allowed: o Added sugars, starches, fats, oils, or sodium o Added DHA

o Any brand o Organics and Naturals allowed o Single fruits, single vegetables, or fruit + vegetable combinations o Texture may range from pureed through diced o Single serving- 2 oz to 4 oz packages o Multipacks- up to 128 oz packages

Infant Meats

Not allowed: o Added sugars, starches, fats, oils, or sodium o Added DHA

o Any brand o Organics and Naturals allowed o Any variety of infant food with a single major ingredient of chicken, turkey, beef, veal, lamb, or ham o May contain broth or gravy o Texture may range from pureed through diced o Single serving - 2.5 oz packages o Multipacks up to 77.5 oz packages

Fresh Fruits and Vegetables

Not Allowed: o Added sugars, fats, or oils o Artificial sugars o Frozen fruit cannot have added salt o Edible blossoms and flowers o Ketchup or other condiments o Vegetable-grain mixtures, fruit-nut mixtures, breaded vegetables, salad bar items, peanuts o Ornamental and decorative fruits and vegetables o Fruit baskets and party trays o Fruit muffins or other baked goods o Mature legumes (beans, lentils, etc.) o Plain fruits and vegetables o Organics allowed o Whole, cut, loose, bagged or plastic o Any immature beans (i.e. green beans, lima beans, succotash) o Fresh herbs

Canned Fruits and Vegetables

Not allowed: o Pickled vegetables, olives, soups o Creamed or sauced vegetables o Fruits packed in syrups or with artificial sugars o Organics allowed o Canned or jarred o May be seasoned with herbs and spices o Fruit or vegetable must be listed as the first ingredient o Canned fruits packed in 100% juice allowed o Canned immature beans, peas, or lentils (e.g. edamame, green beans, yellow wax beans)

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 9.010 6 | P a g e

Frozen Fruits and Vegetables

Not allowed: o Added sugars or oils o Frozen fruits cannot have added salt

o Organics allowed o May be seasoned with herbs and spices o Frozen vegetables may have added salt o Frozen beans (immature or mature) are allowed. Beans purchased with CVV may contain added vegetables and fruits, but may not contain added sugars, fats, oils, or meat as purchased. Canned beans, peas, or lentils may be regular or lower in sodium content. Dried Fruits and Vegetables

Not allowed: o No added sugars, oils, or salt

o Organics allowed

AUTHORIZED PRODUCT LIST The State Agency will additionally maintain an Approved Products List (APL), which lists the Universal Product Codes (UPCs) for each unique food item that meets the above specifications and is authorized in DC WIC. The APL file is disseminated daily to DC WIC authorized vendors to ensure their Point of Sales (POS) systems stay current on allowable food item redemption and ensure eWIC purchase of eligible WIC food items. Participants can check whether a specific food item is authorized and eligible for their purchase by scanning the UPC via the EzWIC mobile app prior to scanning the item at the POS system.

SUBMISSION OF NEW ELIGIBLE FOOD PRODUCTS New food items found to meet the above food item specifications may be considered for inclusion on the DC WIC Authorized Foods list if all required components below are submitted to info.vendor@dc.gov :

• Full UPC or PLU Code • Brand name and full name of product • Full product description, including container size • Picture: Front label • Picture: UPC barcode • Picture: Nutrition information • Picture: Ingredients

The State Agency will review each submission. If approved, the item will be added to the APL within three (3) business days.

REFERENCES 7 CFR 246.10

10.002 - 1 Monitoring and Audits

Revised August 2019 X. Monitoring and Audits - Audits

PROCEDURE 10.002 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 08/11/2015

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.20 Audits (b)(3) III. Applicability DC WIC Local Agency

IV. Policy Statement 1. Local agency sponsored audit reports of Program operations shall be made available for State Agency and the U.S. Department of Agricultural (USDA) review upon requests.

2. The local agency shall submit the current A-133 audit to the State Agency along with the Local Agency Annual Plan of Operations. The A-133 audit must provide a line item audit review of the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC) with the CFDA No. 10.557. The A-133 audit must cover at least the second year prior to the current fiscal year (for example in Fiscal Year 2010—October 1, 2009– September 30, 2010, the A-133 Audit that is submitted will cover FY 2009, not FY 2010).

3. The State Agency will monitor submission of the most current A-133 Audit during site visits (10.003) and the management evaluation process (10.004).

V. Procedures The following concerns auditing procedures: 1. Submit current A-133 Audit to the State Agency along with the Local Agency Workplan and Quarterly Narrative Report (see appendix 10.001B). 2. Provide other audits reports upon request from State Agency or USDA.

VI. Appendix

N/A VII. Reference 10.001B Local Agency Workplan and Quarterly Narrative Report 10.003 State Monitoring, Technical Assistance, and Site Visits 10.004 State Management Evaluations
