10.003 - 1 Monitoring and Evaluation

Revised January 2020 X. Monitoring and Audits - State Monitoring of Local Agencies

PROCEDURE 10.003 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised 01/2020 Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective 10/1/2019

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy The State Agency may visit Local Agencies on a rolling basis to monitor the delivery of Program Services, competency of staff, and to provide technical assistance.

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement State Agency visits to WIC Local Agency sites may be announced for the purpose of technical assistance or corrective action plan reviews, or unannounced for candid Program monitoring.

V. Procedures 1. The State Agency shall monitor 20% of all Local Agencies on an annual basis to ensure adequate delivery of Program services by competent staff. 2. When monitoring the process of Certifications, State Agency staff shall refer to 10.003A (or 10.003B) to record observations of Local Agency staff performing the certification and the environment of the clinic. 3. When monitoring general Program procedures and customer service, the State Agency staff shall refer to appendix 10.003B to record observations and recommendations for corrective action. 4. When monitoring Local Agency sites for compliance with participant’s files, the staff performing the monitoring visit shall use a participant’s Household ID number to assess the presence of the Voter Registration Agency Certification form, as this form is meant to be stored in the youngest participant’s file (see policy 12.007 Voter Registration) and for that reason may not be found in a woman participant’s file. 5. The Local Agency staff shall return reports in conjunction with State Agency monitoring visits according to policy 10.001 - Reporting Procedures. VI. Appendix

10.003A Certification Monitoring Workbook 10.003B Certification Monitoring PDF 10.003C Local Agency Program Monitoring Form VII. Reference 10.001 Reporting Procedures 12.007 Voter Registration

10.004 - 1 Monitoring and Audits Revised September 2019 X. Monitoring and Audits – State Management Evaluations PROCEDURE 10.004 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised September 2019 Approved by: _______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel: ____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: September 2019 I. Authority USDA II. Reason for the Policy FED § 246.19 State Agency Responsibilities b (2), (3), (4) and (6). III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff IV. Policy Statement 1. Management Evaluations of Local Agencies shall encompass, but not be limited to, certification, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, civil rights compliance, accountability, financial management systems, and food delivery systems. 2. The State Agency shall conduct management evaluations of each Local Agency at least once every two years, but reserves the right to conduct the management evaluation every year. Such reviews shall include on-site reviews of a minimum of 20 percent of the clinics in each Local Agency or one clinic, whichever is greater. 3. The State Agency shall develop a corrective action process which includes: prompt notification of deficiencies to the Local Agency, timely development of corrective action plans, and monitoring of Local Agency implementation of such plans. 4. The State Agency shall require Local Agencies to establish management evaluation systems to review their operations and those of associated clinics or contractors. 5. The Local Agency must submit a corrective action plan, including implementation time-frames, within 30 days of receipt of a Management Evaluation report. V. Procedures 1. Sixty days before a management evaluation, the Local Agency shall receive written notification from the State Agency that a management evaluation will be conducted. See appendix 10.003A for an example of the pre-management evaluation questionnaire. 2. The Local Agency shall provide documentation and/or access to files as indicated in the written notification.

10.004 - 2 Monitoring and Audits

Revised September 2019 3. The Local Agency shall set aside an appropriate workspace for State Agency staff. 4. The Local Agency Director, or a designated representative, shall participate in an entrance interview with State Agency staff. 5. The Local Agency shall ensure availability of staff for observation of actual service delivery, gathering data, and interviews. 6. The Local Agency Director, or a designated representative, shall participate in the exit interview with WIC State Agency staff. 7. The Local Agency shall receive the management evaluation report from State Agency within 30 days of exit interview. 8. The Local Agency shall submit a corrective action plan within 60 days of receipt of the management evaluation report. 9. Once the Local Agency has submitted their Corrective Action Plan, the State Agency shall review within 30 days.

VI. Appendix

10.004A Pre-Management Evaluation Questionnaire 10.004B Management Evaluation Workbook 10.004C Management Evaluation Report Template with Corrective Action Plan

VII. Reference N/A

Policy Statement Local Agency Directors, or appropriate designated staff, are expected to monitor staff performance, delivery of Program services, and clinic environments on a rolling basis to ensure competency of staff, satisfaction of Program participants, and compliance to State and Federal Regulations.

The Local Agency staff shall submit monitoring reports as outlined in policy 10.001 - Reporting Procedures, or as requested by the State Agency.

10.006 - 1 Monitoring and Audits

Revised September 2019 X. Monitoring and Audits – Internal Evaluation

PROCEDURE 10.006 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised September 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: September 30, 2019

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy 7 CFR 246.19 (b)(6)

III. Applicability DC WIC Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement The Local Agency shall conduct a thorough evaluation of its operations at least once, every other year and at any time as deemed appropriate. The management evaluation tool entails chart reviews, staff’s competency observations, and Management Information System (MIS) documentation review.

V. Purpose The purpose of Local Agency internal-evaluation is to identify strengths and areas for improvement. This also allows the Local Agency to realize its achievements, identify competent staff and those who need coaching or re-training. The following staff shall be evaluated during internal evaluations:

1. Competent Professional Authorities (CPAs). The Local Agency Director or designate staff shall monitor CPAs for competency in the following areas:

a. Nutritional risk screening using ABCDE guidance b. Care plan (TGIF) notes and SMART goal setting c. Special formula prescriptions and approvals d. Group or class nutrition education e. High nutritional risk management and follow ups f. Design of lesson plans

2. Competent Para-Professional Authorities (CPPAs) and Clerks. Depending on their job description, the Local Agency Director or CPA shall evaluate their competency as it relates to:

a. Participants’ intake (proof of address, income, adjunctive eligibility, pregnancy, etc.)

10.006 - 2 Monitoring and Audits

Revised September 2019 b. Laboratory works (anthropometric measurement and hematological assessment) c. Rights and responsibilities (R&R) d. Voter registration and immunization record e. Participant’s appointment scheduling f. Food package tailoring g. Check issuance and registers h. TGIF note and SMART goal setting i. Missed appointment contact and rescheduling j. Referrals

3. Breastfeeding Peer Counselors (BPCs). The Local Agency Director, Local Agency Breastfeeding Coordinator, designated CPA, or IBCLC shall assess peer counselors regarding:

a. Breastfeeding promotion and support b. Pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers’ follow-up contact (text messaging, phone calls, emails, etc.) c. Effective counseling and understanding of participant’s needs d. Breast pump issuance and log keeping e. Processing and management of breastfeeding referrals

4. New WIC Employees. The Local Agency Director, CPA or designated staff shall evaluate the competency of all new staff members during the first six (6) months of employment or until they are deemed competent to operate independently. This entails consistently monitoring their work, including direct observation and files reviews.

V. Procedures 1. Local Agencies shall perform internal evaluations every other year, as directed by the State Agency.

2. Local agencies shall use the following tools to prepare for and document staff and program evaluations:

a. 10.004A – Pre-Management Evaluation Questionnaire i. LAs shall use this document as a guide to prepare them for performing the ME, allowing appropriate staff members at the given site/s being evaluated to answer relevant questions, while the LAD will answer other questions (such as those pertaining to Local Agency policies, and financial management).

b. 10.004B – Management Evaluation Workbook This excel workbook has tabs for the following: i. Certification Observations ii. File Reviews

10.006 - 3 Monitoring and Audits

Revised September 2019 iii. Clinic Environment Reviews iv. Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Reviews v. Secondary Nutrition Education Reviews 3. Local agencies shall submit pre-Management Evaluation questionnaires, Management Evaluation workbooks, and internal evaluation reports with corrective action plans (see 10.004C) by April 15 of the years when no State agency Management Evaluation is occurring or as directed by the State agency. body:
DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 11.001 1 | P a g e Title: Civil Rights Overview Category: Civil Rights CFR Reference: 7 CFR 246.8

Policy Number: 11.001 Effective Date: 01/01/2019 Revised Date: 01/31/2024

POLICY STATEMENT: The DC WIC program is a federally assisted program and therefore must comply with • Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (42 U.S.C. 2000d et seq.) • Title IX of the Education Amendment of 1972 • Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 • The Age Discrimination Act of 1975 • Department of Agriculture regulations on nondiscrimination • FNS instructions and the requirements of 7 CFR 246.8 to ensure that no person shall on the grounds of race, color, national origin, age, sex (including gender identity and sexual orientation), or handicap, be excluded from participation in, be denied benefits of, or be otherwise subjected to discrimination under the Program. The State and Local Agency are responsible for the following: 1. Informing DC WIC program applicants and participants on how to file a civil rights complaint with the USDA. Civil rights complaints must be referred to FNS within 5 calendar days. 2. Maintaining a record of civil rights complaints. 3. Make WIC program information available to the public upon request. 4. Providing service assistance for persons with disabilities and language services for applicants and participants with Limited English Proficiency (LEP). 5. Including the most current FNS non-discrimination statement (available at https://www.fns.usda.gov/cr/fns-nondiscrimination-statement) on all essential Program materials and prominently displaying the “And Justice for All” poster in all offices where there is a USDA presence and where it may be read by customers. All “And Justice for All” posters must be displayed in a specific size” 11” width x 17” height. The Local Agency must contact the State Agency to order posters. 6. Collecting and reporting racial and ethnic participation data as required by title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. 7. Provide ongoing civil rights training to staff on an annual basis, at minimum. 8. Regularly review and monitor activity to ensure Program compliance with the nondiscrimination laws and regulations. DEFINTIONS 1. Limited English Proficiency – individuals who do not speak English as their primary language and who have a limited ability to read, speak, write, or understand English because of their national origin.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 11.001 2 | P a g e 2. Disability – a person who has a physical or mental impairment which substantially limits one or more major life activity, has a record of such an impairment, or is regarded as having such an impairment. PROCEDURE The State and Local Agency must perform at minimum the following actions related to their civil rights responsibilities: Inform DC WIC program applicants and participants on ways to file a civil rights complaint with the USDA Applicants or participants may file a civil rights complaint via the following methods: 1. Any of the contact methods listed on the most recent nondiscrimination statement. The most recent nondiscrimination statement can be found at https://www.fns.usda.gov/cr/fns- nondiscrimination-statement .

2. The State or Local Agency staff may use attachment 11.001B WIC Complaint Form to collect the complaint information and refer this information to program.intake@usda.gov within 5 calendar days. The Local Agency must notify the State Agency when referring a complaint. The State or Local Agency staff must inform the applicant or participant that complaints may be written, verbal, or anonymous. All complaints must be filed within 180 days of the alleged act of discrimination. Maintain a record of civil rights complaints If a civil rights complaint is completed by the State or Local Agency using the 11.001B WIC Complaint Form, the complaint must be logged using attachment 11.001C Civil Rights Complaint Log Sheet. This log sheet, along with any correspondence regarding the complaint, must be kept on file for three years from the date the State Agency is notified that the complaint is closed. Make WIC program information available to the public upon request The State and Local Agency must ensure DC WIC program applicants and participants are made aware of Program availability in accordance with DC WIC policy 7.007 Wait List Overview, program rights and obligations in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.016 Rights and Obligations, and procedures for filing a civil rights complaint (see above). Program assistance for persons with disabilities The State and Local Agency must make reasonable accommodations to provide Program services in a manner appropriate to persons with disabilities. Examples of reasonable accommodations include architectural accommodations (e.g., wheelchair accessible entrances, elevator access, etc.), remote WIC services in accordance with 8.003 Physical Presence and Identification, and access to communication aids to persons that have hearing, vision, or speech disabilities. Serving persons with LEP State and Local Agency staff must notify LEP persons of their right to free language assistance services. This can include a bilingual staff member or interpretation services through the Language Line.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 11.001 3 | P a g e The LEP person may opt to provide their own interpreter. The State Agency highly discourages reliance on children as interpreters. Likewise, the LEP person should be permitted to use family and friends as interpreters only after the State or Local Agency has offered free language assistance. If the LEP person opts to use their own interpreter or chooses to decline interpretation services, they must sign the Language Service Waiver in the participant’s record in the MIS. If requested, a physical form of the Language Service Waiver may be used (see attachment 11.00D Language Service Waiver). The physical form must be signed and scanned into the participant’s record in the MIS. The Language Service Waiver must be completed each time an LEP person declines the use of free language assistance services. The Local Agency must ensure that all rights and responsibilities are read to the AR/AAR or participant in the appropriate language and in accordance with DC WIC policy 8.016 Rights and Obligations. In accordance with DC code § 2–1933 (a)The State and Local Agency must ensure that all vital Program documents are available in each language spoken by a limited or no-English proficient population that constitutes 3% or 500 individuals, whichever is less, of the population served. Vital documents include at minimum: • Rights and Obligations form • Ineligibility Notice • Waiver forms (i.e. Language Service Waiver, Zero Income, Breast Pump Release of Liability, etc) • Notice of Program Violations Nondiscrimination Statement and “And Justice for All” poster At minimum, the State Agency must ensure that the nondiscrimination statement must be included on: • Rights and Obligations form • Ineligibility Notice • Notice of Program Violations • Public information promoting the DC WIC program (e.g., program brochures, marketing materials, webpages, etc). The Local Agency must display the “And Justice for All” poster in a prominent location for all to view. The State and Local Agency must convey the message of equal opportunity in all photos and other graphics that are used to provide program or program-related information, including the use of the nondiscrimination statement when and where applicable. Regular review/monitoring of Program activities The State and Local Agency must annually review their activities for civil rights requirements compliance. The Local Agency may use 11.001A Monitoring Civil Rights Compliance as a checklist for monitoring civil rights compliance. The State Agency will monitor the Local Agency civil rights activities and compliance in accordance with 10.004 State Agency Management Evaluations. Collection/reporting of racial and ethnic participation data In accordance with 7 CFR 246.8(a)(3), the State Agency must collect and report racial and ethnic participation data. This data is collected in the MIS and must be maintained for three years.

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 11.001 4 | P a g e The Local Agency must: 1. Ask for race and ethnicity data of each applicant to the DC WIC program. 2. Inform the applicant (or AR/AAR for children and infants) that reporting this data is voluntary and is requested solely for the purpose of determining the State’s compliance with Civil Rights laws and has no effect on their eligibility. 3. Inform the applicant (or AR/AAR for children and infants) that another data collection method will be used if they decline to self-identify (i.e. the Local Agency staff will observe and report based on their judgement). 4. Collect ethnicity before race. 5. Provide an option to select one or more races. Civil rights training requirements The State Agency will provide civil rights training to the Local Agency on an annual basis. The Local Agency must provide civil rights training: • On an annual basis to all staff who interact with DC WIC program applicants or participants • To all new employees prior to participating in the delivery of DC WIC program services The State and Local Agency civil rights training must cover: • the collection and use of Program data • effective public notification system (i.e. program information available to the public upon request and notice of nondiscrimination) • complaint procedures • compliance review techniques • resolution of noncompliance • requirements for reasonable modifications and auxiliary aids and services for persons with disabilities, requirements for LEP persons • confliction resolution and customer service REFERENCES DC WIC policies 7.007 Wait List Overview, 8.016 Rights and Obligations, 10.004 State Agency Management Evaluations Code of the District of Columbia; Subchapter II. Language Access; DC code § 2–1933 (a) Americans with Disabilities Act - www.ada.gov/resources/disability-rights-guide/ ATTACHMENTS & FORMS 11.001A Monitoring Civil Rights Compliance 11.001B WIC Complaint Form 11.001C Civil Rights Complaint Log 11.001D Language Service Waiver

body:
DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy # 11.002 1 | P a g e Title: Mandatory Non-Smoking in WIC Clinics Category: Civil Rights CFR Reference: CFR § 246.6 Policy Number 11.002 Effective Date: 01/01/2016 Revised Date: 01/31/2024

POLICY STATEMENT: In accordance with CFR 246.6(b)(4), smoking is prohibited in the space used to carry out the WIC Program during the time any aspect of WIC services are performed. In accordance with DC code § 7-1704, the Local Agency must display a “no smoking” sign, using the internationally recognized symbol, in all WIC clinics where WIC services are provided. The State Agency must issue a written citation to the Local Agency and withhold administration funds if found out of compliance with this policy. This penalty will be lifted once the Local Agency complies with the policy. PROCEDURE The State Agency will monitor the Local Agency’s compliance in displaying the “no smoking” signs in each WIC clinic in accordance with DC WIC policy 10.003 State Monitoring of Local Agencies. The Local Agency must ask persons entering the WIC clinic with a lit smoking device (e.g. cigarettes, e- cigarettes, pipes, e-pipes, vapes, vaporizers, vape pens, hookah pens, etc.,) to extinguish the device before entering the clinic. Failure of the person to extinguish the smoking device may result in a delay in receiving WIC services.

REFERENCES CFR 246.6(b)(4) DC code § 7-1704 DC WIC policy 10.003 State Monitoring of Local Agencies ATTACHMENTS & FORMS DC WIC Style Guide

12.002 - 1 Administrative Procedures

Revised September 2019 XII. Administrative Procedures – Ordering Supplies

PROCEDURE 12.002 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 01/01/2016

I. Authority DC WIC State Agency

II. Reason for the Policy To ensure an accurate process for maintenance of inventory and reordering of forms and materials.

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement To ensure an accurate process for maintenance of inventory and reordering of forms and materials, the WIC State Agency utilizes an ordering control system for use by Local Agencies. All Local Agency supplies are ordered on an as-needed basis using the WIC Program Ordering Control Form (see Appendix 12.002A), which can be downloaded from dcwic.org. The supply request should be e-mailed to the State Agency at info.wic@dc.gov. Supply requests are not accepted by phone or face-to- face. The State Agency asks that Local Agency inventories be monitored carefully in order to avoid last minute request.

The ordering of pre-printed checks is monitored and initiated by the WIC State Agency on a bi-monthly basis. The State Agency schedules the automatic delivery of all manual checks.

V. Procedures Local and State agency staff must follow the procedure below when ordering supplies from the State agency:

1. The Local Agency must complete the DC WIC Program Ordering Control Form (Appendix 12.002A) and email the form(s) to the State agency at info.wic@dc.gov. Each Local Agency is responsible for ordering and/or purchasing its own nutrition, breastfeeding, and outreach materials.

2. Should the Local Agency be ordering supplies from the State agency, the State agency will arrange the delivery of the supplies to the site(s).

3. The requested supplies will be sent by courier to the Local Agency’s address listed on the request form.

12.002 - 2 Administrative Procedures

Revised September 2019

4. The DC WIC Program Ordering Control Form can be used to order a variety of administrative forms, as well as education/outreach materials and other supplies that are available at the State Agency. A minimum of five (5) business days for processing is needed to fill orders generated by the Ordering Control Form.

a. WIC Clinic Forms (individual forms can be accessed online at www.dcwic.org) b. WIC ID Folder Bags c. WIC ID Folder Spanish d. WIC ID Folder English e. Nutrition Education Handouts (appendix 12.002B))

5. Outreach Supply Material

Local Agencies are responsible for ordering their own outreach materials,, paraphernalia and general education materials for outreach events for the WIC Program. Updated brochures, posters and flyers can be found at https://www.dcwic.org/wic-marketing- materials. Approved paraphernalia and general education materials can be found in the DC WIC Resource Guide (12.002B), which can also be found on dcwic.org.

Delivery for supplies ordered using the WIC Program Ordering Control may be provided by a courier or a messenger from the State Agency.

VI. Appendix

12.002A DC WIC Program Ordering Control Form 12.002B DC WIC Resource Guide

12.003 - 1 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019 XII. Administrative Procedures – Customer Service, Vision and Guidelines

PROCEDURE 12.003 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 01/01/2016

I. Authority DC WIC State Agency

II. Reason for the Policy Vision – We, the WIC Staff, are proud to consistently deliver world-class customer service in all aspects of our work. We readily provide supplemental foods, nutrition education, breastfeeding promotion and support, and referrals to health and social services to meet the diverse needs of all customers. Our customers are impressed with the efficiency and timeliness and professionalism of the services.

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement 1. Each local agency shall implement the gold standard of customer service delivery, exemplified by the following four key components:

a. Reliable points of entry b. Prompt response to customer calls, written correspondence, and requests for services c. Front-line customer contacts handled with the highest level of professionalism and customer service d. Service delivery within the established, easily understood, and widely known performance standards 2. Each local agency shall ensure that they meet the following objectives of high quality customer service:

12.003 - 2 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019 a. Treat all customers with enthusiasm, courtesy and respect b. Promptly answer all customers’ questions with accurate, objective information c. Resolve all customers' needs with the fewest number of calls possible d. Provide educational information to all customers e. Use language that all customers can easily understand f. Ask for and consider all customers' ideas about program services g. Promptly respond to all customers' suggestions, concerns, and complaints 3. Each local agency is directly responsible for delivery of all customer service commitments. To better support the WIC staff, local agency management shall: a. Give staff the decision-making parameters that will enable them to go "the extra mile" to satisfy customers b. Involve staff in customer service improvement initiatives c. Establish a customer-focused culture and infrastructure at all levels of management and internal support V. Procedures The following steps must be implemented by all staff to ensure exceptional customer service: 1. Incorporate vision and guidelines in the Local Agency Workplan (see appendix 10.001B) 2. Report progress quarterly via the Quarterly Narrative Report (see appendix 10.001B) VI. Appendix

N/A VII. Reference 10.001B Local Agency Workplan and Quarterly Narrative Report

Revised August 2019 XII. Administrative Procedures – Customer Service Master Competencies

PROCEDURE 12.004 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by: _____________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel: ____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date:01/01/2016

I. Authority DC WIC State Agency

II. Reason for the Policy WIC Local Agency staff are expected to show respect and courtesy towards Program participants when providing WIC services. III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff IV. Policy Statement 1. All WIC staff shall demonstrate master (core and contributory) competencies to provide the gold standard of customer service delivery; See Appendix 12.004A for a list of the master competencies, and their corresponding practices and behaviors/evidences 2. Master competencies are the areas of knowledge, skills and attitudes that characterize exemplary service employees. 3. The Local Agency WIC Director is responsible for ensuring development of master competencies for local agency staff

V. Procedures Local agency staff must follow the procedure below when completing competencies: 1. Provide and/or participate in training to develop competencies in customer service skills 2. Monitor employee customer service competency skills 3. Provide corrective actions to address deficiencies in customer service skills VI. Appendix 12.004A Master Competencies for Service Providers

body:
12.005 - 1 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019 XII. Administrative Procedures – Customer Service, Telephone Standards

PROCEDURE 12.005 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 01/01/2016

I. Authority DC WIC State Agency II. Reason for the Policy DC WIC Local Agency staff shall treat all persons with respect during customer service, including those calling WIC clinics via telephone. III. Applicability DC WIC Local Agency Staff IV. Policy Statement The following must be implemented concerning customer service: 1. Develop objectives to ensure compliance with telephone standards 2. Submit objectives with the Local Agency Work Plan 3. Provide training to develop competencies in customer service skills 4. Monitor employee customer service skills 5. Provide corrective actions to address deficiencies in customer service skills V. Definitions a. Main Service Number - are the entry points into the Local Agency’s WIC clinics. This service number shall be staffed at all times during business hours, or may provide an automated system whereby customers can receive information, leave a message, or speak with a person. b. Desk Numbers - are telephone numbers for local agency employees. All employees shall answer calls professionally and courteously. Desk voicemail shall

12.005 - 2 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019 also reflect the same professionalism that would be provided during a direct conversation with a customer. VI. Procedures 1. Customer Service Voicemail Standard (CSVS) All voice mailboxes shall be set-up with the customer service voicemail standard and ready to accept voice messages. Each voice mailbox shall never be full and unable to accept new messages. The automated greeting option available through the standard voice messaging system does not comply with the standard. a. Main Service Greetings - This greeting shall convey the following information: I. Name of WIC clinic II. Hours of operation III. What number to dial for immediate assistance IV. Options for caller (e.g., website address, fax number) V. When calls will be returned b. Desk Telephone Standard Greetings - Every telephone equipped with voice mail shall have a standard outgoing greeting that is professional, concise, and conveys relevant and useful information to the caller. Each desk phone shall have the following information included within the greeting: I. Name of employee II. Title of employee III. Clinic name IV. What number to dial for immediate assistance V. When calls will be returned c. Extended Absence Greeting - Every employee who will be out of the office for more than two business days (annual/sick leave, training, and jury duty) shall record an extended absence greeting. In addition to the standards, this greeting shall outline the expected date of return, or that all calls shall be forwarded to an employee in the office. d. Closed Greeting – When the WIC clinic is closed, a greeting must be recorded on the main service telephone. The greeting shall convey the following information: I. Name of WIC clinic II. Reason for closure III. Date(s) of closure IV. Date and time when clinic will be re-opened

12.005 - 3 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019 V. When calls will be returned 2. Receiving and Returning Telephone Calls a. Salutation - Staff name and agency, and solicit information (e.g., "Thank you for calling agency X. This is Mary Ann. How may I help you?"). At the end of the conversation, thank the person for calling. b. Receiving Telephone Calls – WIC staff shall receive all incoming calls during business hours. Each call shall be handled at the first point of contact or prioritized based on the greatest need during busy periods. c. Returning Telephone Calls - Calls made to all numbers at every level (main service or desk number) shall be returned within one (1) business day of receipt. 3. Receiving a Transferred or Three-Way Conference Calls a. All WIC local agency staff shall take transferred and three-way conference calls from the State Agency to resolve participant concerns or complaints. Local agencies shall also accept all transferred calls from other organizations. b. WIC staff shall minimize the number of times a caller is transferred to resolve an issue by taking the message and distributing it to the appropriate staff person for resolution. The goal is one transfer per customer and the transfer shall be to another person, not voicemail. 4. Basic Knowledge All WIC staff shall be knowledgeable of WIC benefits and services. 5. Telephone Etiquette In addition to the requirements for salutation, call transfer and basic knowledge, each telephone call shall be handled with the highest level of customer service by all WIC staff:

I. Answer calls within 3 rings II. Direct the conversation to obtain the essential information quickly III. Give customers options (i.e., hold, call back, leave a message, try another number) IV. Ask to put the caller on hold and wait for the response V. Check back with customer frequently when placed on hold VI. Use judgment by handling callers as you would want your call to be handled VII. Provide options for resolution VIII. Facilitate IX. Speak as you would like to be spoken to

12.005 - 4 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019 6. Courtesy Local Agency staff shall be treat all callers with the highest level of customer service:

I. No speakerphones unless the customer agrees II. No food or gum while talking with customer III. No secondary conversations while caller is on the phone IV. No loud music in the background V. Convey empathy, professional courtesy, and a pleasant attitude VI. Provide reference information when transferring calls VII. Treat callers as you would want to be treated VIII. No rudeness IX. Do not become confrontational

VII. Appendix N/A VIII. Reference N/A

12.006 - 1 Administrative Services

Revised August 2019 XII. Administrative Procedures – Customer Service: Comments, Complains and Compliments

PROCEDURE 12.006 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 02/01/2003

I. Authority DC WIC State Agency

II. Reason for the Policy Procedures must be set in place to ensure timely correspondence between WIC Local Agencies and current or potential Program participants, the State Agency, and the public.

III. Applicability DC WIC Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement 1. The local agency is responsible for receiving and responding to all customer comments, complaints and compliments within 48 hours (two days) of receipt. The WIC Local Agency Director shall determine whether an oral or written response is necessary based on the situation.

2. Each WIC clinic shall have customer feedback forms/surveys readily available (See Appendix 12.006A and 12.006B for examples) and in a conspicuous place for customers to provide anonymous comments.

3. The local agency is responsible for resolving customer complaints, except those relating to civil rights (discrimination). The State Agency will become involved only after the chain of command has been followed and there is no mutual resolution, or as referred to by the WIC Local Agency Director.

4. The Local Agency Director shall ensure that all clinic staff has the authority to resolve customer complaints at the initial point of contact.

V. Procedures Local agency staff must follow the procedure below concerning customer service:

1. The local agency staff person receiving the complaint shall facilitate resolution.

2. If at the initial point of contact, the staff person is unable to resolve the complaint, refer it to the clinic supervisor, then to the Local Agency Director,

12.006 - 2 Administrative Services

Revised August 2019 in that order.

3. The Local Agency Director shall refer the customer to the State Agency only if a mutual resolution cannot be achieved on the local agency level.

4. If referred to the State Agency, the State Agency staff will follow up with the Local Agency Director with the final resolution within 3 business days.

5. For civil rights (discrimination) complaints, refer to Policy 11.001.

VI. Appendix

12.006A WIC Client Survey (English) 12.006B WIC Client Survey (Spanish) VII. Reference 11.001 Civil Rights

12.009 - 1 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019 XII. Administrative Procedures – Facility Re-Organizing and Re-Location Planning

PROCEDURE 12.009 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 01/01/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.6 Agreements with Local Agencies

III. Applicability DC WIC Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement As a part of the State and Local Agency Agreement the Local Agency must notify the State Agency of any re-organization plans for the facility at least 3 months prior to relocating or reducing the designated space for these services.

V. Procedures The following process should be implemented pertaining to the opening, expansion, closing, or moving of a clinic:

1. The Local Agency must notify the State Agency in writing using their Local Agency letterhead of the relocation or reduction plans for the clinic with the signature of the administrator of the Local Agency- see template for example of letter- in appendix 12.009A.

2. Submit the Site Closing/Moving/Opening Information Sheet to the State Agency three (3) months prior to the closing and include:

(1) The reason for closing/moving/opening (2) Detailed plans for providing benefits to affected participants (3) A Civil Rights Impact Analysis (see appendix 12.009D)

3. Post announcements notices throughout the WIC clinic indicating the date for closing as well as the address of the new WIC site, or

4. Post announcements notices throughout the WIC clinic indicating the date for closing as well as alternative WIC sites to refer participants

5. Mail the announcement notices which indicate closing/new address of the new WIC sites

12.009 - 2 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019

6. Mail the announcement notices which indicate the closing and reference to alternative WIC sites where participants can voluntarily make a transfer

7. Arrange a visit with the State Agency liaison, IT Contractor, and the administrator’s building management of the new location

8. Provide the State agency with the actual moving date and notification of when the clinic will be operable to serve clients; this decision can be made in tangent with the State Agency liaison for the Local Agency

VI. Appendix

12.009A Template letter for clinic closing/moving/opening 12.009B Site closing/moving/opening information sheet/data equipment transfer request form 12.009C Completing the Site Closing/Moving/Opening Information Sheet/Data Equipment Transfer Request Form 12.009D Civil Rights Impact Analysis

VII. Reference N/A

12.010 - 1 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019 XII. Administrative Procedures – Termination and Installation of Network Connections at Closing and New Sites

PROCEDURE 12.010 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 01/01/2016

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.14(c) Program costs – Specified allowable nutrition services and administration costs III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement This policy outlines responsibilities and procedures for State Agency information technology (IT) support personnel when assisting in the termination of network connections at closing sites, and the installation of network connections at new WIC sites.

This policy also outlines the responsibilities of the network provider and WIC Local Agency staff in assisting State agency IT personnel in preparation for closing, opening, or relocation of a WIC site.

V. Procedure for Local Agency Staff The following steps must be completed by local agency staff in preparation for network installation/de-installation at WIC sites:

1. Notify the State agency 90 days in advance in writing of the opening, closing or relocation of a site. The written notification must be documented on the agency’s letter head (Appendix 12.009A), and emailed to info.wic@dc.gov.

2. A Civil Rights Impact Analysis (CRIA) Form (Appendix 12.016C) is required to be submitted to the State Agency 90 days prior to closing or relocating a local agency and must be submitted at info.wic@dc.gov.

3. Depending on the opening or closing of a site, the local agency must determine where WIC computer data outlets will need to be connected/disconnected.

4. Have the necessary network cabling (drops) in their newly designated spaces, including network panels in walls, going in ceilings and making appropriate connections to the existing patch panel.

12.010 - 2 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019

5. Distribute marketing materials to WIC enrollees including the specific move date as well as the new location at the local agency clinic site that is to be moved or closed. 6. Pack WIC equipment at the current WIC clinic site for transport to the new location.

VI. Procedure for DC WIC IT Support Staff The following steps must be completed by the Department of Health (DC Health) WIC IT support staff once notification of WIC new site opening or site closing:

1. Determine the number of network printers, PC (computers), network lines to be moved.

2. Unplug monitors, mice, keyboards, printers, switch and router.

3. Label all WIC equipment.

4. Plug monitors, mice keyboards, printers, switch and router at the new location.

5. Coordinate installation of new network with LA management, LA IT and contractors as well as the WIC State Agency LA liaison.

6. Coordinate installation/de-installation of circuit and router with network provider in time to ensure seamless continuation of WIC services.

7. Print labels of enrollees and send a letter of the clinic site that is be relocated / closed (See Policy 12.009).

8. Coordinate the addition of new service site number in CARES (through DC System Administration module) and set up the print queue for the new service site number.

VII. Procedure for State Agency Representative

The following step must be completed by the State agency representative:

1. Use the printing labels that DC Health IT provided to send notices or letters of clinic relocation / opening to WIC enrollees at affected clinic site

VIII. Procedure for Network Provider The following steps are performed by the network provider concerning installation of network connections at WIC clinics:

1. The order is placed by DC Health IT with OCTO/DCNet.

2. OCTO/DNCET acknowledges that the order was placed

12.010 - 3 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019 3. OCTO/DCNET performs their portion of the installation. (Note that the installation/de-installation process may take up to 30 days and must be factored into total relocation and/or closing of WIC sites).

4. OCTO/DCNET or DC Health IT, establishes the CARES connection in the cloud.

IX. Appendix N/A

X. Reference 12.009 Facility Re-organization/Relocation Planning 12.009A Site Closing/Moving Agency Announcement Letter 12.016C Civil Rights Impact Analysis

DC WIC POLICY & PROCEDURE MANUAL

Policy 12.011 1 | P a g e Title: State Plan Category: Nutrition Services Plan and Evaluation CFR Reference: 7 CFR § 246.4 7 CFR § 246.11 Policy Number: 12.011 Effective Date: 01/01/2016 Revised Date: 8/15/2023

POLICY STATEMENT By August 15 of each year, the State Agency must submit to FNS for approval a State Plan for the following fiscal year as a prerequisite to receiving funds under 7 CFR § 246.4. The State agency may submit the State Plan in the format provided by FNS guidance. Alternatively, the State agency may submit the Plan in combination with other federally required planning documents or develop its own format, provided that the information required below is included. The State Plan must be signed by the State designated official responsible for ensuring that the Program is operated in accordance with the State Plan. After receiving approval of the State Plan, the State Agency must only submit to FNS for approval substantive changes in the State Plan. The State agency must establish a procedure under which members of the general public are provided an opportunity to comment on the development of the State agency plan. PROCEDURE 1. A complete State Plan must include everything requested by FNS under Subpart B – State and Local Agency Eligibility, State Plan: 246.4(a), Requirements. 2. The State Agency must conduct an annual evaluation of its State Plan that includes participant feedback on nutrition education and breastfeeding promotion activities. (7 CFR § 246.11) The DC WIC State Plan will be open for public comment per DC Health standard procedures. REFERENCES 7 CFR § 246.4

12.012 - 1 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019 XII. Administrative Procedures – Program Integrity, WIC Services for Employees and Relatives

PROCEDURE 12.012 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 07/28/216

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.3(e) Administration – State staffing standards

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement The local agency employee is prohibited from participating in any component of the certification process and issuing checks to themselves, their relatives or close friends to ensure that no conflict of interest exists, and to prevent and detect staff fraud abuse.

V. Procedures The following procedure must be followed to ensure program integrity concerning WIC services for employees and relatives:

1. For any local agency employee, their relatives or close friends applying for or participating in WIC, only the local agency program manager, site supervisor or designee, appointed in the absence of the program manager and site supervisor, is authorized to:

a. Determine their eligibility to receive WIC benefits, and

b. Process the certification and provide appropriate nutrition education contacts including the prescribing of WIC checks.

2. The local agency program manager, site supervisor or designee must:

a. Restrict access to the participant’s information in CARES by rendering it “confidential”

b. Secure and file the applicant’s or participant’s paper records separately from the general paper files

12.012 - 2 Administrative Procedures

Revised August 2019 c. Maintain separation of duties between prescribing, printing and removing checks from the printer, and distributing Cash Value (CVC) and WIC checks

3. The local agency will develop and implement procedures to ensure WIC program integrity is maintained when services are provided by the designee. The written procedures will be made available to program reviewers upon request.

VI. Appendix

N/A VII. Reference N/A

12.013 - 1 Administrative Procedures

Revised February 2023 XII. Administrative Procedures – Fair Hearings

CFR Reference: 246.9 Policy Number: 12.013 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA)

Effective date: 04/11/2023 Revised Date: 09/15/2016 03/3/2023 Approved by:

_______________________ Dr Sharon Lewis DHA, RN-BC, CPM, Interim Director of DC Health Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel

I. Authority USDA

II. Reason for the Policy Program participants are entitled to a fair hearing if they are unsatisfied with an adverse action made by the State or Local Agency.

III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff

IV. Policy Statement This policy establishes the procedures under which an individual, parent, guardian or other representative may appeal an adverse action made by the State or a local WIC agency. V. Procedure for Availability of Hearings At the time of a claim against an individual for improperly issued benefits or at the time of participation denial or of disqualification from the WIC Program, the local agency shall inform each individual in writing of the right to a fair hearing, of the method by which a hearing may be requested, and that any positions or arguments on behalf of the individual may be presented personally or by a representative such as a relative, friend, legal counsel or other spokesperson.

1. The local agency shall provide written information on how to request a fair hearing to appeal an adverse action made by the local agency, (action which resulted in a claim against the individual at the time of the action. These actions may include request for repayment of the cash value of improperly issued benefits or denial of participation or disqualification from the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), DC WIC

12.013 - 2 Administrative Procedures

Revised February 2023 Policy 8.015 “Violations and Sanctions”). The participant may request notification form for Ineligibility and termination DC WIC Policy 8.006 Income Eligibility and 8.014 Ineligibility. The local agency shall appoint an impartial hearing official or panel to conduct the hearing, who does not have any personal stake or involvement in the decision and who was not directly involved in the initial determination of the action being contested. 2. A participant found ineligible for the Program at any time during the certification period shall be advised in writing of the reason(s) for ineligibility, the termination date, and of the right to a fair hearing. Reasons for ineligibility during a certification period and the termination notice timeframes are: 10 day Notification of Termination: a. No longer categorically eligible; b. Changes to income or family size making them income ineligible; c. No longer have a required nutritional need; or d. Sanctions for Program Abuse. All documentations are saved onto MIS system by the local agency. 3. The participant may request for a conference within 7 days of notification of the adverse action. The local agency shall set up a conference within 10 days of a written or verbal request by an individual. The participant may bring a relative, friend or lawyer to speak for them at the conference. 4. The individual may ask for a fair hearing with the Office of Administrative Hearings within 60 days of notification of an adverse action if no resolution is reached at a conference at the local agency. 5. The State Agency allows for an individual to request a fair hearing within 90 days after the date the agency mails or gives the applicant or participant the notice of adverse action.

Fair hearings are conducted at: WIC State Agency Office Headquarters (Administrative Office) 899 North Capitol Street NE | 3rd Floor | Washington, DC 20002 Telephone: 202-442-9397

Or Participant has an option of Fair Hearing at: District of Columbia – Office of Administrative Hearings 441 Fourth Street, NW Suite 450 North Washington, DC 20001 Telephone: 202-442-9094

In cases where the appointed hearing official is not available, a backup official must be appointed. A panel member could serve in this role. VI. Time Frame and Notification of Fair A written notification of the hearing shall be sent to the applicant/participant (and his/her representative) at least 10 days prior to the hearing date. The notification shall:

12.013 - 3 Administrative Procedures

Revised February 2023 Hearing Process 1. Specify the date, time and place of the hearing.

2. State briefly the issues, which are to be subject to the hearing.

3. Explain the manner in which the fair hearing will be conducted.

4. Inform participant of the right to be represented to verify and present documented evidence, produce witnesses, question adverse witnesses and to examine (prior to and during) the documents and records supporting the action under appeal.

VII. Denial of Fair Hearing Request

The Local Agency may deny or dismiss a request for a hearing due to the following reasons:

1. The request is not received within the time frame established by the State Agency 2. The request is withdrawn in writing by the applicant/participant or a representative of the applicant/participant; 3. The applicant/participant or representative fails, to appear at the hearing without good cause; 4. The applicant/participant has been denied participation by a previous hearing and cannot provide evidence that circumstances relevant to Program eligibility have changed in such a way as to justify a hearing; 5. Participants who request a fair hearing to appeal the termination of benefits before the date entered on the Ineligibility Notice shall continue to receive WIC benefits until the Hearing officer reaches a decision or the certification period expires, whichever occurs first. This does not apply to applicants denied benefits at initial certification, participants whose certification period has expired or participants who become categorically ineligible for benefits. VIII. Hearing Decision The applicant/participant shall receive, by mail, a written decision from the DC WIC State Agency or the Office of Administrative Hearings (depending on where the hearing was conducted) within 10 days following the date of determination, but no more than 45 days following the filing date.

When a fair hearing decision is unfavorable to the applicant/participant, OAH or the DC WIC State Agency shall explain the right to pursue judicial review.

If the decision is in favor of the applicant/participant and benefits were denied or discontinued, benefits shall begin immediately. IX. Appendix N/A

X. Reference CFR § 246.9 Fair Hearing Procedures for Participants

12.016 - 1 Administrative Procedures Revised August 2019 XII. Administrative Procedures – Application Process for New Local Agencies and/or New Site Locations PROCEDURE 12.016 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Revised August 2019 Approved by: _______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel: ____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 01/01/2017 I. Authority USDA II. Reason for the Policy CFR § 246.5 Application for New Local Agency III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff IV. Policy Statement When an organization expresses interest in becoming a WIC Local Agency (LA), the State Agency (SA) will send information regarding the DC WIC program and the responsibilities of being a WIC agency. The SA will instruct the potential new agency to complete the DC Health WIC Program Application for New Local Agencies (see appendix 12.016A), which should be completed and returned to the SA via email at info.wic@dc.gov. Current DC WIC Local Agencies may use the same application when seeking approval to open additional site(s). A copy of the DC Health WIC Program Application for Local Agencies can also be found on the DC WIC Website (dcwic.org). NOTE: Grant agreements start at the beginning of a FFY (October 1st). A new agency to WIC will not start their online training until October 1st and will not provide actual WIC services for clients until a later date to be determined. The SA will acknowledge receipt of an application within 20 days. If any additional information is needed or the application is completed incorrectly, the SA will inform the organization of the deficiencies within 20 days. After receipt of corrections or additional information, the SA will analyze the request and inform the organization of the approval or disapproval of the request within 90 days.

12.016 - 2 Administrative Procedures Revised August 2019 VI. Procedures An organization who would like to be a new WIC Local Agency (or – a current LA wishing to open a new site) must provide the following information to the State Agency: 1. Notify the SA of the desire to be a new WIC LA, or the desire to open new site(s) in conjunction with a currently contracted DC WIC LA 2. Provide a letter stating the reason why the organization would like to become a WIC Local Agency 3. Provide pictures of the exterior and interior of where WIC services would be performed 4. Complete the DC WIC Application for New Local Agency Form (Appendix 12.016A) 5. Review the Proposed WIC site Checklist (Appendix 12.016B) 6. Provide documents requested in bullets 2 thru 6 above via email to the State Agency at info.wic@dc.gov a. Subject Lines: i. New Local Agencies – “Application for new WIC Local Agency” ii. Current LA, new Site – “(LA Name) Application for new WIC Site” VII. Appendix 12.016A DC Health WIC Program Application for New Local Agencies 12.016B Proposed Site Checklist VIII. Reference N/A

12.017 - 1 Administrative Procedures Revised August 2019 XII. Administrative Procedures – Record Retention and Destruction PROCEDURE 12.017 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Created August 2019 Approved by: _______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel: ____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 01/01/2020 I. Authority USDA II. Reason for the Policy CFR 246.25 (a) III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff IV. Policy Statement This policy is meant to identify recordkeeping retention and destruction requirements for WIC records, which provide documentation of WIC program operations pertaining to fiscal operations, food delivery systems, food instrument issuance and redemption, equipment purchases and inventory, certification, nutrition education including breastfeeding promotion and support, civil rights and fair hearing procedures. Records must be destroyed in a manner that protects the confidentiality of WIC participants and vendors by the following methods: shredding, incineration. or landfill. WIC Local agencies must retain all WIC records for a minimum of three (3) years following the date of submission of the final expenditure report for the period to which the report pertains (usually covering an additional period of 150 days after the completed fiscal year) or until any litigation, claim, negotiation, audit or other action involving the records which was started before the end of the 3-year period has been resolved. V. Guidance Regarding Record Retention WIC RECORD RETENTION 1. Records, whether electronic or hard copy, that contain confidential client information must be stored in a secure manner. All records and reports that contain confidential client information shall be stored or kept in a locked area. Electronic records shall be kept under direct supervision at all times. See also Policy 3.001- DC CARES Management Information System, Appendix 3.001B - MIS CARES Confidentiality Agreement for New User ID Requests, and 12.019 - Confidentiality.

12.017 - 2 Administrative Procedures Revised August 2019 Note: There is no requirement for printing reports or records from the DC WIC data system except where necessary for documentation of compliance investigations. 2. The District of Columbia statutes require maintenance of medical records for a period longer than the WIC three-year guideline (see Record keeping requirements under the health regulations - D.C. MUN. REGS. tit. 22-B § 2030). Local Agencies that are affiliated with hospitals shall consult with the agency legal counsel and governing body for a decision regarding whether or not WIC participant charts are considered medical records. 3. The Local Agency must retain, as applicable, paper copies or electronic versions of the following records in accordance with this policy: a. Computer printouts or electronic reports for the District’s Management Information System (CARES) that serve as payment and/or source documents: • Check registers • Dual Issuance Report b. Other materials and information, which serves as source documents: • Audit documents • Civil rights complaints • Complaint information by and about the participant • Compliance investigation, sanction materials regarding client or employee compliance • Correspondence from State WIC office • Dual Participation materials such as paper reports or investigation materials • Equipment purchases and inventory • Fair hearing requests and documentation • Financial source documentation • Laboratory logs • Local Agency Plans Evaluations of Local Agency Plans • Local Agency Voter Registration Log Sheet • Monitoring reports, corrective action plan (CAP) and CAP approvals • News releases submitted to local media c. Program records: • Agency specific records, • Contracts, budgets and administrative records • Fair Hearing records d. Quality Assurance: • Records from quality assurance activities, • WIC State Agency Management Reviews • Local agency announced and unannounced Site visits e. Returned Formula Logs f. Staff credential verifications

12.017 - 3 Administrative Procedures Revised August 2019 4. During a federal or state management evaluation, participant records/files covering three (3) previous years plus 150 days for situations described above should be furnished upon request for inspection, auditing or copying purposes. If the items are not readily accessible due to being stored off-site based on space limitations, the Local Agency must present these records upon request within five (5) business days. 5. Complete participant files may require longer retention due to state statutes related to medical records. Refer to section 2, above. These include: • All materials used to assess, determine eligibility, or prove service offered, such as Physician documentation & referral, notarized documentation of income support, etc. • Certification Summary (if printed on a regular basis • Notification of Ineligibility and/or Termination • Rights and Responsibilities Participant Signature VI. Procedures for Record Destruction A. Prior to destruction of WIC records the local agency must determine that all agency audits and litigation pertaining to the information are completed for the period of these records. B. All records and printed reports containing client identifiers (e.g; names, addresses, phone numbers, and client IDs) must be destroyed in a manner that protects confidentiality. The approved methods to accomplish this are: a. Shredding (for records that are being recycled) b. Made Unreadable (for records that are being recycled) c. Incineration d. Landfill C. If instructed to do so by the State WIC office or FNS, the WIC Local Agency shall not destroy program records of historical interest, but shall forward such records to the State WIC office VI. Appendix N/A VII. Reference 3.001 – DC CARES Management Information System MIS 3.001B – MIS CARES Confidentiality Agreement for New User ID Requests 12.019 – Confidentiality

12.018 - 1 Organization and Management

Created August 2019 IV. Organization and Management – New Policies at the Local Agency Level

PROCEDURE 4.006 Implementing Office: Community Health Administration (CHA) Created August 2019

Approved by:

_______________________ LaQuandra S. Nesbitt MD, MPH; Agency Director Review by Legal Counsel:

____________________ Phillip Husband, Esq.; General Counsel Effective Date: 10/01/2019

I. Authority DC WIC State Agency II. Reason for the Policy The State Agency must be aware of and approve of Local Agency policies which affect the services provided at, or the WIC monies spent by, the Local Agency. III. Applicability DC WIC State Agency and Local Agency Staff.

IV. Policy Statement DC WIC Local Agencies may create policies and procedures specific to their organization. The State Agency must approve any new policies and procedures which the Local Agency may wish to implement, so long as it may impact the delivery of WIC services to Program participants. V. Procedures When creating new policies and procedures, the Local Agency must abide by the following process:

1. Create a draft of the policy/procedure including the following information: a. Functional area in which the policy resides b. Reason for the proposed policy c. Procedures which specify staff duties and processes to be followed, including any resources which should be attached as appendices d. List of appendices indicated in the procedures, if applicable 2. Submit the draft policy for review and approval by the State Agency: a. Save the proposed policy in draft format as a word document b. Email the proposed policy to the State Agency via info.wic@dc.gov c. Use the subject heading “New Policy_(Local Agency Name)” 3. The State Agency will have 30 days to review the policy, suggest amendments to the draft or approve as-is, and return correspondence to the Local Agency 4. The Local Agency will have 30 days to revise the draft if not approved, or to implement the approved policy within their organization 5. Final policies must be saved to the Local Agency’s Procedure Manual

VI. Appendix

N/A
